terms.name: Abbreviation
terms.definition: A shortened form of a word or phrase, from Dr. to NASA, with its own typographic conventions and an expansion assistive tech can speak.
terms.useWhen: shortened forms need setting, marking up, or expanding

terms.name: Accent color
terms.definition: The one saturated colour an interface spends sparingly on the things it wants clicked, so its rarity is what makes it read as important.
terms.useWhen: the one colour reserved for the primary action

terms.name: Access key
terms.definition: A single letter, usually shown underlined, that jumps straight to a menu or control once the access modifier is held.
terms.useWhen: the underlined letter that reaches a menu item

terms.name: Accessibility annotation
terms.definition: Notes attached to a design file that spell out the things a mockup cannot show: heading levels, focus order, names, roles, live regions, and alt text.
terms.useWhen: handing a design over without losing the semantics

terms.name: Accessibility grouping
terms.definition: Collapsing a cluster of elements, an icon plus a label plus a value, into one thing assistive technology stops at, instead of three stops that mean nothing apart.
terms.useWhen: a card reads as five fragments instead of one item

terms.name: Accessibility overlay
terms.definition: A third party script bolted onto a site with a promise of automatic compliance, usually a floating widget of font and contrast toggles that fixes nothing underneath.
terms.useWhen: someone proposes buying a widget instead of fixing

terms.name: Accessibility trait
terms.definition: The platform flag on a native view that says what it is and how it behaves, the mobile counterpart to a role plus a state, and the thing a custom control has to set by hand.

sources.title: Deque: What iOS accessibility traits actually do

terms.useWhen: a custom native control announces as plain text

terms.name: Accessibility tree
terms.definition: The parallel tree a browser derives from the DOM, holding the role, name, state, and value that assistive technology actually reads.
terms.useWhen: talking about what assistive technology sees, not what renders

terms.name: Accessible authentication
terms.definition: A sign-in route that never requires a cognitive function test such as recalling a password or solving a puzzle without offering an alternative.
terms.useWhen: a login demands memory or puzzle solving

terms.name: Accessible description
terms.definition: Supplementary text announced after a control's name, carrying hint or error detail without becoming part of the name itself.

sources.title: APG: Providing Accessible Names and Descriptions

terms.useWhen: extra detail that should follow the name, not replace it

terms.name: Accessible name
terms.definition: The string assistive technology announces for a control, computed from label, aria-labelledby, aria-label, or its own content in a fixed order of precedence.

sources.title: APG: Providing Accessible Names and Descriptions

terms.useWhen: asking what a control is actually called out loud

terms.name: Accordion
terms.definition: A stack of headers, each expanding to reveal its own section of content.
terms.useWhen: a stack of sections, each opening in place

terms.name: Achievement badge
terms.definition: A collectible marker awarded for a milestone and displayed on a profile, often shown greyed out before it is earned so the set is visible.
terms.useWhen: the collectible award shown on a profile

terms.name: Acid graphics
terms.definition: A 2020s rave revival style of chrome and liquid 3D objects, warped and stretched lettering, clashing saturated colour on near black, smileys, globes, and wireframe motifs.

sources.title: AIGA Eye on Design: Acid graphics are the new psychedelia

terms.useWhen: chrome, warped type, and rave motifs used ironically

terms.name: Action list
terms.definition: A vertical list of commands with icons, descriptions and dividers, the shared body used inside menus, panels and side sheets.
terms.useWhen: a list of commands reused inside several surfaces

terms.name: Action sheet
terms.definition: A modal list of choices that slides up from the bottom of a phone screen in response to something you just did, with cancel at the end.

sources.title: Apple Human Interface Guidelines: Action sheets

terms.useWhen: choices for an action you just started, on a phone

terms.name: Active descendant
terms.definition: A focus technique where DOM focus stays on a container or input and aria-activedescendant names which child is active, used when focus must not move.
terms.useWhen: the typing field must keep focus while a list moves

terms.name: Activity feed
terms.definition: A reverse chronological list of things that happened, each entry naming an actor, a verb, and an object, grouped when many are alike.
terms.useWhen: the running list of who did what, most recent first

terms.name: Adaptive layout
terms.definition: A layout that switches between a few discrete arrangements chosen per size class, rather than flowing continuously as the window changes.
terms.useWhen: distinguishing snapping between layouts from fluid reflow

terms.name: Additive animation
terms.definition: Composing an animation on top of whatever is already animating the same property instead of replacing it, so a second nudge adds to the first rather than restarting it.

sources.title: CSS-Tricks: additive animation with the Web Animations API

terms.useWhen: a repeated trigger should stack rather than snap back to the start

terms.name: Additive colour
terms.definition: Colour made by adding light, where red, green and blue at full strength give white, which is why a screen is at its brightest when it is showing all three.
terms.useWhen: colour mixed by adding light, as a screen does

terms.name: Address autocomplete
terms.definition: Replacing a set of address fields with one lookup that suggests full addresses after a few characters and fills the rest on selection.
terms.useWhen: typing a postcode fills in the whole address

terms.name: Affordance
terms.definition: What an element makes possible for the person using it, such as a surface that can be pushed, dragged, or scrolled.
terms.useWhen: naming what an element allows a person to do

terms.name: Afrofuturism
terms.definition: A style that pictures technology through the African diaspora, combining cosmic imagery, textile and mask pattern, gold and indigo, and geometric ornament used structurally.
terms.useWhen: a future told through African diaspora imagery

terms.name: Agenda view
terms.definition: The same events as a chronological list grouped by day, so the next thing is at the top instead of somewhere inside a grid.

sources.title: Google Calendar Help: view your day, week, or month

terms.useWhen: events as a list, with the next thing at the top

terms.name: Alert dialog
terms.definition: A dialog that interrupts the flow to demand acknowledgement or confirmation of a consequential action before anything else can continue.

sources.title: ARIA Authoring Practices Guide: Alert and Message Dialogs

terms.useWhen: a dialog that announces itself and blocks until answered

terms.name: All caps
terms.definition: Text set entirely in capitals, which reads slower than mixed case because the word's outline shape disappears.

sources.title: Title case vs sentence case in UI

terms.useWhen: short labels that must shout, never sentences

terms.name: Alpha channel
terms.definition: The transparency component carried inside a colour value itself, which lets a border or fill blend with whatever surface it lands on instead of assuming one.
terms.useWhen: a colour that must blend with an unknown background

terms.name: Alpha compositing
terms.definition: The arithmetic that combines a translucent layer with what is beneath it, and the reason two stacked 50 percent layers do not add up to fully opaque.
terms.useWhen: predicting the result of stacking translucent layers

terms.name: Alt text
terms.definition: The text alternative that stands in for an image, written to serve the same purpose in the same context rather than to describe every detail.
terms.useWhen: writing what an image says when it cannot be seen

terms.name: Analogous colors
terms.definition: A palette built from hues that neighbour each other on the wheel, giving a calm scheme with no colour fighting another for attention.
terms.useWhen: a quiet palette of neighbouring hues

terms.name: Anchor positioning
terms.definition: A CSS mechanism that tethers one element to another, sizing and placing it against its anchor and trying fallback positions when the default one would overflow.
terms.useWhen: pinning one element to another without JavaScript

terms.name: Anti-design
terms.definition: A deliberately awkward style that breaks layout, type, and color conventions so the interface reads as a statement rather than as a polished product.

sources.title: Envato: Minimalism vs. maximalism, battle of the divisive design styles

terms.useWhen: the rule breaking is the message

terms.name: Anti-pattern
terms.definition: A solution reached for again and again for a familiar problem, which fails at the thing it was reached for and often leaves the situation worse than doing nothing.
terms.useWhen: the fix everyone reaches for is the thing making the problem worse

terms.name: Anticipation
terms.definition: A small move in the opposite direction just before the main one, borrowed from character animation to telegraph what is about to happen.

sources.title: IxDF: UI Animation, applying Disney's 12 principles to UI

terms.useWhen: an action needs a wind-up so it does not start cold

terms.name: APCA
terms.definition: A perceptual contrast algorithm proposed for WCAG 3 that scores a text and background pair as an Lc value and takes font size and weight into account.
terms.useWhen: scoring contrast in a way that accounts for text size and weight

terms.name: Aperture
terms.definition: The partly enclosed opening in a letter, such as the gap where the two terminals of a c stop or the mouth at the bottom of an e.
terms.useWhen: why one sans feels clearer at small sizes

terms.name: App bar
terms.definition: The persistent bar across the top of an application carrying its title, navigation, and primary actions.
terms.useWhen: the app's own top bar, the same on every screen

terms.name: App shell
terms.definition: The persistent frame of an application, its header, navigation and footer, that stays put while only the content region swaps as you move around.

sources.title: Instant Loading Web Apps with an Application Shell Architecture

terms.useWhen: naming the part of the app that never reloads

terms.name: App shortcut
terms.definition: A short menu of app actions hung off the app icon itself, opened by a long press or a secondary click before the app is even running.

sources.title: Apple HIG: Home Screen quick actions

terms.useWhen: a frequent action should skip the app launch

terms.name: App silhouette
terms.definition: The recognisable outline of an app's chrome, which bars and panes it has and where they sit, used to classify one app's layout against another's.
terms.useWhen: classifying an app by the shape of its chrome

terms.name: Applied filters
terms.definition: A row of removable tokens above the results showing every filter currently in force, with a control to clear them all at once.
terms.useWhen: the removable tags showing which filters are on

terms.name: Aqua
terms.definition: Apple's early Mac OS X look of glossy blue gel buttons, pinstripes, gumdrop window controls, and a pulsing default button.
terms.useWhen: candy-gel Mac controls from the 2000s

terms.name: Arc motion
terms.definition: Moving an element along a curved path rather than a straight line, so a change of position reads as natural rather than mechanical.

sources.title: IxDF: UI Animation, applying Disney's 12 principles to UI

terms.useWhen: an element travels in two axes at once

terms.name: aria-hidden
terms.definition: An attribute that removes an element and its whole subtree from the accessibility tree while leaving it visible on screen.
terms.useWhen: hiding something from screen readers but not from eyes

terms.name: ARIA notify
terms.definition: A proposed API for speaking a message directly to assistive technology, without the live region trick of mutating hidden text and hoping the timing works out.
terms.useWhen: an announcement has no element it belongs to

terms.name: Art Deco
terms.definition: A 1920s luxury style of strict symmetry, stepped and fanned geometry, strong vertical emphasis, metallic gold on deep colour, and high contrast display capitals.

sources.title: Kittl: 60+ graphic design styles, names and descriptions
Big Human: 12 graphic design styles, a complete guide for 2026

terms.useWhen: symmetrical geometric luxury, gold on deep colour

terms.name: Art Nouveau
terms.definition: A turn of the century style of whiplash curves, botanical line ornament, muted jewel tones, and lettering drawn to fit the frame rather than set on a grid.

sources.title: Kittl: 60+ graphic design styles, names and descriptions

terms.useWhen: botanical line ornament and curved frames

terms.name: Ascender
terms.definition: The part of a lowercase letter such as b, d, or h that rises above the x-height.
terms.useWhen: naming the strokes that reach above lowercase height

terms.name: Aspect ratio box
terms.definition: A container that holds a fixed width to height proportion whatever its size, so media reserves its space before it loads.
terms.useWhen: reserving the right shaped hole before an image arrives

terms.name: Asymmetric easing
terms.definition: Giving a state change and its reverse different curves or durations, usually a quick confident exit and a slower entrance, so the two directions do not feel identical.
terms.useWhen: opening and closing should not be mirror images

terms.name: Atomic live region
terms.definition: A live region setting that makes assistive technology re-read the whole region when any part of it changes, instead of only the changed fragment.
terms.useWhen: a partial update would be read out of context

terms.name: Attract mode
terms.definition: A self-playing loop an idle screen falls into to demonstrate itself, inherited from arcade cabinets and reused by kiosks and product demos.

sources.title: School of Motion: motion design dictionary

terms.useWhen: an unattended screen should demonstrate itself

terms.name: Attribute editor
terms.definition: A repeating row of key and value fields with add and remove controls, used for tags, headers and other open ended pairs.
terms.useWhen: a form section that repeats a row of fields

terms.name: Audio control
terms.definition: A way to stop sound that started on its own, because autoplaying audio drowns out the screen reader voice a reader depends on to find the control that stops it.
terms.useWhen: anything makes noise before the reader asked

terms.name: Audio description
terms.definition: A narration track describing visual information the soundtrack leaves out, fitted into the gaps between dialogue.
terms.useWhen: the picture carries information the audio does not

terms.name: Auditory icon
terms.definition: A recorded everyday sound standing for an event, so a crumple means delete by resembling the act rather than by convention learned in the interface.

sources.title: Gaver: Auditory Icons, Using Sound in Computer Interfaces (Human-Computer Interaction, 1986, 167-177)

terms.useWhen: the sound that reports an event by resembling it

terms.name: Aurora UI
terms.definition: A style whose background is built from heavily blurred color blobs that glow and drift like the northern lights behind the content.

sources.title: Hype4 Academy: Aurora UI, new visual trend for 2021
Superdesign: Aurora UI, the CSS gradient recipe and when it breaks

terms.useWhen: the background is soft glowing bands of color

terms.name: Autofill
terms.definition: The browser filling a form from values it has already saved, on its own or from a dropdown of the reader's own profile, so a field arrives answered.
terms.useWhen: the browser answers the field before the reader does

terms.name: Autoplay
terms.definition: Playback that starts with no gesture from the reader, which browsers now allow only while the sound is off, so autoplay in practice means a silent moving picture.

sources.title: MDN: Autoplay guide for media and Web Audio APIs
Chrome for Developers: Autoplay policy in Chrome

terms.useWhen: media that starts playing before anyone asked

terms.name: Autosave
terms.definition: Persisting the reader's work continuously without a save action, usually with a quiet status line reporting when the last save happened.
terms.useWhen: work is kept without anyone pressing save

terms.name: Avatar
terms.definition: A small image standing in for a person or entity, falling back to initials or a generic glyph when there is no picture.

sources.title: Gravatar: one avatar, tied to an email address

terms.useWhen: a person represented by a small image

terms.name: Avatar group
terms.definition: Several avatars overlapped in a row to show a set of people compactly, with a plus n counter standing for the rest.
terms.useWhen: a row of overlapping faces with a plus n

terms.name: Axis
terms.definition: The ruled edge of a chart that maps position to value: scale, ticks, and labels that make the marks readable as numbers.

sources.title: Fundamentals of Data Visualization: Coordinate systems and axes

terms.useWhen: discussing tick density, label rotation, or what scale a chart hangs on

terms.name: Back to top
terms.definition: A control that appears after the reader has scrolled some distance and returns them to the top of the page in one action.
terms.useWhen: the button that appears partway down to send you back up

terms.name: Badge
terms.definition: A small marker attached to another element that carries a count or a status and is not interactive on its own.
terms.useWhen: a count or status stuck to something else

terms.name: Banner
terms.definition: A prominent message strip, usually spanning the top of a page or section, that stays visible until the user dismisses or resolves it.
terms.useWhen: a message strip that stays until it is dealt with

terms.name: Baseline
terms.definition: The invisible line that most letters sit on, and the line every other vertical type metric is measured from.
terms.useWhen: aligning text with an icon or another line of text

terms.name: Baseline grid
terms.definition: A set of evenly spaced horizontal lines that every line of text sits on, so type in adjacent columns lines up across the page.
terms.useWhen: text in neighbouring columns must line up

terms.name: Bauhaus style
terms.definition: A style reduced to primary red, yellow, and blue on off-white, elementary circles, triangles, and squares, and undecorated sans serif type.

sources.title: Digital Heroes: Bauhaus web design, form follows function revival
Inkbot Design: 20 iconic graphic design styles

terms.useWhen: primary colors and elementary shapes doing the work

terms.name: Bento grid
terms.definition: A grid whose cells are deliberately different sizes, tiled to fill a rectangle without gaps, like the compartments of a bento box.
terms.useWhen: cells at deliberately different sizes, tiled to fill a rectangle

terms.name: Bevel and emboss
terms.definition: Light and dark edges drawn along a shape's border so it reads as raised or carved, the depth trick behind classic desktop buttons.
terms.useWhen: a raised edge drawn from a light and a dark border

terms.name: Bidirectional text
terms.definition: Text mixing a right-to-left script with left-to-right runs such as numbers or Latin words, where each run keeps its own direction.
terms.useWhen: Arabic or Hebrew text containing Latin or digits

terms.name: Biophilic design
terms.definition: A style that borrows from the natural world on purpose, using earthy greens and clays, organic silhouettes, botanical imagery, and slow ambient motion to make a screen feel less mechanical.

sources.title: Silphium Design: Understanding biophilia in digital design

terms.useWhen: nature borrowed deliberately for calm, not decoration

terms.name: Blame view
terms.definition: Each line of a file labelled with the change that last touched it, so the file answers who and when rather than what it says.
terms.useWhen: every line labelled with its last change

terms.name: Blend mode
terms.definition: A formula for combining a layer's colour with the colour behind it, such as multiply or screen or overlay, instead of simply covering it.
terms.useWhen: combining layers by a formula rather than by covering

terms.name: Organic blob
terms.definition: A soft irregular shape with no straight edges, used as a background accent or image mask to soften a strictly rectangular layout.
terms.useWhen: an amoeba shape softening a rectangular grid

terms.name: Blockquote
terms.definition: A passage quoted from another source and set off from the running text as its own block, carrying the attribution with it.
terms.useWhen: quoting a source at paragraph length

terms.name: Bottom navigation
terms.definition: A bar of three to five top level destinations pinned to the bottom edge of a phone screen, with the current destination always marked.
terms.useWhen: top level destinations within thumb reach

terms.name: Bottom sheet
terms.definition: A surface anchored to the bottom edge that slides up over the content, often draggable between a peeked and an expanded height.
terms.useWhen: a panel that rises from the bottom edge

terms.name: Bounce
terms.definition: Motion that arrives, rebounds, and arrives again in decreasing amounts, reading as an object landing on a surface.
terms.useWhen: an arrival should read as landing, with weight

terms.name: Box
terms.definition: A bordered container, optionally titled, that groups logically related controls so the grouping is drawn rather than implied by spacing alone.
terms.useWhen: grouping controls with a visible boundary

terms.name: Braille display
terms.definition: A refreshable braille row that renders the same accessibility tree as speech, with abbreviated role names authors can override.

sources.title: Accessible Rich Internet Applications (WAI-ARIA), W3C editor's draft

terms.useWhen: output is a braille line, not synthesized speech

terms.name: Brand color
terms.definition: The colour an organisation owns in a customer's memory, carried into a product as the seed for its palette rather than used directly on every surface.
terms.useWhen: the colour the company owns, before it becomes UI tokens

terms.name: Breadcrumbs
terms.definition: A trail of links showing the path from the top of a hierarchy down to the current page, with every level above it clickable on the way back up.

sources.title: ARIA Authoring Practices Guide: Breadcrumb pattern

terms.useWhen: showing where a page sits in a hierarchy

terms.name: Breakout
terms.definition: A track wider than the reading column but narrower than the viewport, used for figures and code that need more room than prose.

sources.title: Layout Breakouts with CSS Grid, Ryan Mulligan

terms.useWhen: a figure that needs more width than the text

terms.name: Breakpoint
terms.definition: A viewport width at which a layout is allowed to change shape, defined once so every screen in a system reflows at the same places.
terms.useWhen: the widths where the layout is allowed to change

terms.name: Broken grid
terms.definition: A composition that sets up a grid and then deliberately violates it, overlapping and offsetting elements to create tension.
terms.useWhen: breaking the grid on purpose, not by accident

terms.name: Browse mode
terms.definition: The screen reader mode that intercepts keystrokes for reading and navigation, as opposed to focus or forms mode where keys reach the page.

sources.title: Accessibility Developer Guide: Browse and focus modes
Understanding screen reader interaction modes, Léonie Watson
Complete guide to Narrator, Microsoft Support

terms.useWhen: explaining why a key press never reached your widget

terms.name: Brushing
terms.definition: Dragging a selection across one chart to highlight the same records in every linked view.
terms.useWhen: coordinated views should answer a selection made in any one of them

terms.name: Brutalist web design
terms.definition: A raw style that leaves the document showing: system or monospace type, default link blue, hard borders, and no decoration beyond structure.

sources.title: Superdesign: Brutalist Web Design: CSS Recipe, Live Examples and Trend Data

terms.useWhen: the page looks like unstyled HTML on purpose

terms.name: Bubble toolbar
terms.definition: A small formatting bar that appears floating over a text selection and disappears when the selection is dropped.
terms.useWhen: the toolbar appears over the text you just selected

terms.name: Bulk actions
terms.definition: Selecting several rows and applying one command to all of them, usually through a bar that appears once a selection exists and reports its count.
terms.useWhen: picking many rows and acting on them at once

terms.name: Bulletproof button
terms.definition: A mail button built to survive a renderer that drops CSS: the fill carried by a cell or box behind the link rather than by a background the client can refuse.

sources.title: Litmus: your guide to bulletproof email buttons that work

terms.useWhen: a button that still reads as one when the CSS is dropped

terms.name: Busy state
terms.definition: Marking a region as still loading so assistive technology waits for the finished result instead of reading each row as it streams in.
terms.useWhen: a region updates in pieces and each piece speaks

terms.name: Button
terms.definition: A control that runs an action when activated, labelled with the thing it does rather than with where it goes.

sources.title: ARIA Authoring Practices Guide: Button pattern

terms.useWhen: the control does something instead of going somewhere

terms.name: Button group
terms.definition: Buttons set flush against each other so they read as one unit of related actions, usually with shared borders and rounded outer corners only.
terms.useWhen: several actions that belong together visually

terms.name: Button versus link
terms.definition: The rule that decides which element to use: a link goes somewhere, a button does something, and the choice sets the keyboard, the cursor, and the announced role.
terms.useWhen: a control looks like a button but navigates

terms.name: Bypassing pattern
terms.definition: A scanning shape where readers deliberately skip the opening words of each line because every line in a list starts the same way.

sources.title: F-Shaped Pattern of Reading on the Web, NN/g

terms.useWhen: arguing against repeated leading words in lists

terms.name: Calendar
terms.definition: A month grid of dates that can be read, navigated and selected from, whether standing alone or living inside a date field.
terms.useWhen: a month laid out as a grid of days

terms.name: Callout
terms.definition: A boxed note set into the flow of content to carry a warning, tip or aside, coloured by severity and staying put once shown.
terms.useWhen: a boxed note sitting inside the content

terms.name: Canonical layout
terms.definition: One of a small set of proven multi pane arrangements a platform recommends, such as list detail, supporting pane and feed, instead of a new layout per screen.
terms.useWhen: reaching for a proven arrangement, not a new one

terms.name: Cap height
terms.definition: The height of a capital letter measured from the baseline, and the edge designers usually mean when they say text should line up flush.
terms.useWhen: aligning a heading optically instead of by its box

terms.name: CAPTCHA
terms.definition: A challenge placed in a form to sort people from scripts, from distorted text to a single checkbox that watches how you got there.
terms.useWhen: the challenge that proves you are a person

terms.name: Captions
terms.definition: Synchronised text for a video's audio, including speaker changes and meaningful sound, distinct from subtitles which only translate dialogue.
terms.useWhen: text that carries the sound of a video, not a translation

terms.name: Card
terms.definition: A bounded surface holding a preview of one thing, usually an image, a title, some detail and one or two actions, that as a whole leads somewhere.
terms.useWhen: one thing previewed on its own surface

terms.name: Card flip
terms.definition: Rotating a card about its own axis to show a second face on the back, with the hidden face pre-rotated and its backface hidden so only one side is ever visible.

sources.title: David DeSandro: card flip, intro to CSS 3D transforms
Auroratide: a (more) realistic card flip animation

terms.useWhen: one surface carries two faces and both are the same object

terms.name: Card grid
terms.definition: Content laid out as equal width cards flowing across a responsive grid and wrapping to new rows as space allows.
terms.useWhen: many peers of the same kind, browsed by scanning

terms.name: Caret
terms.definition: The blinking marker showing where typed text will be inserted, moved by clicking, by arrow keys, or by dragging on touch.
terms.useWhen: the text insertion marker, not the mouse pointer

terms.name: Carousel
terms.definition: A row of items shown a few at a time that advances by arrows, swipe or a timer, with the rest waiting off screen.

sources.title: ARIA Authoring Practices Guide: Carousel pattern

terms.useWhen: a set of items shown a few at a time in a row

terms.name: Cascader
terms.definition: A select whose options open level by level, each choice narrowing the next, used for country then state then city style data.
terms.useWhen: choosing down a hierarchy one level at a time

terms.name: Cassette futurism
terms.definition: The analog future of late 1970s science fiction: beige and putty plastic, chunky toggles and rocker switches, amber or green CRT readouts, and monochrome bitmap type.
terms.useWhen: a future built from 1970s and 80s analog hardware

terms.name: Categorical palette
terms.definition: A data palette of distinct hues at roughly equal visual weight, used for groups that have no order so no colour reads as larger than another.
terms.useWhen: colouring unordered groups without implying rank

terms.name: Ch unit
terms.definition: A CSS length equal to the advance width of the digit zero in the current font, used to set column widths in characters rather than pixels.
terms.useWhen: setting a column width in characters, not pixels

terms.name: Chamfer
terms.definition: A corner cut flat at an angle instead of rounded, the sharp-edged sibling of border-radius that reads industrial, military, or sci-fi.
terms.useWhen: corners should read machined rather than soft

terms.name: Change of context
terms.definition: A shift big enough to disorient a reader, a new page, a new window, a moved focus, a rearranged form, and the rule that it should follow a request rather than a keystroke.
terms.useWhen: naming the surprise a select or focus event should not cause

terms.name: Character counter
terms.definition: The running count beside a text box showing how many characters are used, or how many remain, against a limit.
terms.useWhen: showing how much of a length limit is used

terms.name: Character key shortcuts
terms.definition: Single letter shortcuts that fire without a modifier, which must be switchable off or remappable because speech input and screen readers trigger them by accident.
terms.useWhen: a bare letter key does something on the page

terms.name: Chart
terms.definition: A drawing of data in which position, length, angle or colour carries the numbers, chosen so the comparison a reader needs is the easiest one to see.
terms.useWhen: numbers are easier compared by eye than by reading

terms.name: Chart annotation
terms.definition: A note pinned onto the data itself: a callout, arrow, or highlighted span that tells the reader what to see in the chart.
terms.useWhen: the takeaway should be written on the chart, not left to the caption

terms.name: Chart aspect ratio
terms.definition: How wide a chart is for its height, which sets the slopes of its lines; banking to 45 degrees keeps rates of change readable.
terms.useWhen: a line chart reads too steep or too flat for the story it tells

terms.name: Chart description
terms.definition: The text alternative for a chart: a summary of the takeaway plus access to the underlying values, not a recital of the pixels.
terms.useWhen: a chart needs to work for readers who cannot see it

terms.name: Chart legend
terms.definition: The key beside a chart that decodes series colours and symbols into names, and the first thing direct labeling tries to delete.
terms.useWhen: naming the colour key of a chart, not a fieldset caption

terms.name: Chartjunk
terms.definition: Tufte's word for ink that decorates a chart without carrying data: 3D bevels, gradient fills, mascots, gridline thickets.
terms.useWhen: a chart's decoration is fighting its data

terms.name: Chat bubble
terms.definition: A rounded container for one message in a conversation, aligned and coloured by who sent it, often with a tail toward the sender's side.
terms.useWhen: one message in a conversation view

terms.name: Check answers
terms.definition: A review screen listing everything the reader entered, with a change link beside each answer, shown before the submission is final.
terms.useWhen: a summary screen lets you review and edit before submitting

terms.name: Checkbox

sources.title: GoodUI: Try Direct Manipulation instead of contextless menus

terms.useWhen: you change the thing by grabbing the thing

terms.name: Directionality
terms.definition: The rule that every movement carries a direction, and that using it consistently tells the reader how the parts of an interface relate.
terms.useWhen: motion should say where a view sits relative to another

terms.name: Disclosure
terms.definition: A single button that shows and hides one region of content, reporting its state through aria-expanded.

sources.title: ARIA Authoring Practices Guide: Disclosure (Show/Hide) pattern

terms.useWhen: one control hiding one region

terms.name: Disclosure triangle
terms.definition: The small triangle beside a tree item that points right when collapsed and down when open, rotating as it toggles.
terms.useWhen: the little triangle that opens a branch

terms.name: Disguised ad
terms.definition: An advertisement styled to look like a control or an item of content, so the click it collects was aimed at something else entirely.
terms.useWhen: the download button that is actually an advert

terms.name: Display cutout
terms.definition: The camera housing that intrudes into the screen rectangle, which a layout has to route content around rather than under.

sources.title: Using safe-area-inset to build mobile-safe layouts, Polypane

terms.useWhen: naming the hole the layout must dodge

terms.name: Dissolve
terms.definition: A fade that carries the eye from one image or state to another without any movement, inherited from film editing vocabulary.

sources.title: School of Motion: motion design dictionary

terms.useWhen: the change should register without implying direction

terms.name: Dithering
terms.definition: Adding fine noise to a gradient or image so the eye averages neighbouring pixels into the missing intermediate colours, hiding the bands.
terms.useWhen: removing banding by adding fine noise

terms.name: Diverging palette
terms.definition: A data palette built from two sequential scales meeting at a neutral midpoint, used when values run above and below a meaningful zero.
terms.useWhen: values that run above and below a midpoint

terms.name: Divider
terms.definition: A thin line separating groups of content, decorative when the grouping is already clear and semantic when it is the only cue.
terms.useWhen: a line that groups content by separating it

terms.name: Dock
terms.definition: A persistent strip of application icons anchored to a screen edge, holding launchers, running apps and pinned items in one row.
terms.useWhen: the persistent row of app icons at a screen edge

terms.name: Dock magnification
terms.definition: Scaling each item in a row by how close the pointer is to it, so the item under the cursor swells, its neighbours ramp down, and the row reads as bulging.

sources.title: jQuery 1.4 Animation Techniques: resizing elements and the fisheye menu

terms.useWhen: a dense row of icons needs a hovered target enlarged in place

terms.name: Dolly and zoom
terms.definition: Borrowing the camera's vocabulary: dolly moves the viewer through the scene, zoom scales the scene itself, and the interface reads as travelling rather than rearranging.

sources.title: UX Magazine: creating usability with motion, the UX in Motion Manifesto
School of Motion: motion design dictionary

terms.useWhen: the reader should feel moved through the interface

terms.name: Dot grid background
terms.definition: A faint repeating field of dots or ruled squares behind content, borrowed from graph paper and canvas tools to suggest an editable surface rather than a page.
terms.useWhen: a faint grid or dot field behind the content

terms.name: Double click
terms.definition: Two clicks inside a short interval on the same spot, treated as one gesture that opens, edits, or selects a word rather than activating twice.
terms.useWhen: two clicks that mean something a single click does not

terms.name: Double opt-in
terms.definition: Asking a new subscriber to confirm from the address they typed, so a list holds only addresses whose owner agreed and a typo never becomes a stranger's mail.
terms.useWhen: a signup confirmed from the address itself

terms.name: Double tap
terms.definition: Two taps in quick succession on the same spot, conventionally used to zoom in on content or to zoom back out when already zoomed.
terms.useWhen: two quick taps that mean zoom, not activate

terms.name: Drag and drop
terms.definition: Picking up an object, moving it under continuous pointer or finger contact, and releasing it over a target that accepts it.

sources.title: MDN: HTML Drag and Drop API

terms.useWhen: moving an object onto a target by holding it the whole way

terms.name: Drag autoscroll
terms.definition: Scrolling a container automatically when a drag is held near its edge, so an item can be moved somewhere currently off screen.

sources.title: Cloudscape Design System: Drag and drop

terms.useWhen: a drag needs to reach past the visible area

terms.name: Drag handle
terms.definition: The small gripped area, often drawn as rows of dots or lines, that marks where an item may be picked up and dragged.
terms.useWhen: the part of an item that says grab me here

terms.name: Drag preview
terms.definition: The semi-transparent copy of the dragged item that follows the pointer, sometimes collapsed into a stack when several items move at once.
terms.useWhen: the ghost of the item that follows your cursor

terms.name: Drag threshold
terms.definition: The small distance a pointer must travel while pressed before the gesture counts as a drag, so a shaky click is not mistaken for one.
terms.useWhen: deciding when a press turns into a drag

terms.name: Drag to create
terms.definition: Making a new object by dragging out its extent rather than pressing Add: an event drawn across two hours, a frame drawn on a canvas, a range drawn on a chart.

sources.title: Google Calendar Help: create an event

terms.useWhen: drawing a new object out at the size you want

terms.name: Drag to reorder
terms.definition: Changing the order of a list by dragging an item to a new position, with the remaining items shifting to show where it will land.
terms.useWhen: you rearrange a list by dragging its rows

terms.name: Dragging alternative
terms.definition: A second, non-dragging route to anything a drag can do, such as arrow keys or a move-to menu on a sortable list.
terms.useWhen: a drag is the only way to perform an action

terms.name: Drawer
terms.definition: A panel docked to one edge of the screen that slides in over the content, holding navigation or the details of the thing you selected.
terms.useWhen: a panel that slides in from an edge and can stay open

terms.name: Drill-down navigation
terms.definition: Going deeper into a hierarchy one level at a time inside the same panel, each level replacing the last and offering a way back up.
terms.useWhen: a hierarchy is too deep to show all at once

terms.name: Drip pricing
terms.definition: Advertising a low headline price and adding mandatory fees one screen at a time, so the true total only appears once the buyer is committed.
terms.useWhen: fees keep appearing as you move through checkout

terms.name: Drop cap
terms.definition: An oversized opening letter set into the first lines of a paragraph, marking where the reading starts.

sources.title: How to use drop caps effectively in editorial design

terms.useWhen: marking where an article begins

terms.name: Drop indicator
terms.definition: The line or highlighted gap drawn during a drag to show exactly where the item will land if it is released now.
terms.useWhen: the line that shows where the dragged item will land

terms.name: Drop zone
terms.definition: The region that will accept a dragged item, usually highlighted while a compatible drag is in flight so the destination is unmistakable.

sources.title: MDN: HTML Drag and Drop API

terms.useWhen: the area that says a drag can land here

terms.name: Dropdown
terms.definition: The loose everyday word for any panel that opens downward from a trigger, whatever the panel holds and whatever the trigger does with it.
terms.useWhen: the loose word for anything that opens downward

terms.name: Dual axis
terms.definition: Two value axes sharing one plot so two series can be compared, and a free knob for manufacturing whatever correlation you like.

sources.title: Datawrapper: Why not to use two axes

terms.useWhen: someone proposes a second y-axis and the scales question needs asking

terms.name: Duotone
terms.definition: An image rendered in two colours instead of full colour, mapping its shadows to one hue and its highlights to another so photography joins the brand palette.
terms.useWhen: forcing photography into two brand colours

terms.name: Duration
terms.definition: How long a transition takes from start to finish, measured separately from the shape of its easing.

sources.title: Nielsen Norman Group: response times, the three important limits

terms.useWhen: how long a motion lasts, not its shape

terms.name: Dwell activation
terms.definition: Committing an action by keeping a pointer or gaze still on a target for a set time, for input methods that have no click of their own.

sources.title: NN/g: Timing guidelines for exposing hidden content

terms.useWhen: holding still is the only way to click

terms.name: Dynamic Type
terms.definition: A platform feature that scales interface text to a size the reader chose in system settings, with layouts expected to reflow around it.
terms.useWhen: the reader, not the designer, picks the text size

terms.name: E-ink aesthetic
terms.definition: A paper-like style built for or borrowed from electronic ink: near-white ground, pure black text, hairline rules, no shadows or gradients, and paged navigation.

sources.title: Intent: How to design for e-ink devices
CHI 2026: A Dedicated E-Paper Design System for Mobile Phones

terms.useWhen: an interface styled like reflective ink on paper

terms.name: Earcon
terms.definition: A brief synthesized sound standing for an event, abstract by design, so a rising figure means success only because the interface taught you it does.

sources.title: Blattner, Sumikawa and Greenberg: Earcons and Icons, Their Structure and Common Design Principles (Human-Computer Interaction, 1989)

terms.useWhen: the abstract tone that reports an event

terms.name: Easing
terms.definition: The rate of change across an animation, deciding how it accelerates and settles rather than how long it takes.
terms.useWhen: the shape of a motion over its duration, not its length

terms.name: Easter egg
terms.definition: A reward hidden behind an action nobody was told about, put there to be found rather than to be used.
terms.useWhen: a hidden extra whose whole value is the surprise of finding it

terms.name: Edge routing
terms.definition: How a connector gets from one node to another: a bezier sweep, a right-angled staircase, or a straight line, picked so the crossings stay readable.
terms.useWhen: the path a connector takes between two nodes

terms.name: Edge swipe
terms.definition: A swipe that begins off the screen edge and travels inward, reserved by the system for navigation such as going back or revealing a drawer.
terms.useWhen: a gesture that starts at the bezel, not on a control

terms.name: Edge to edge
terms.definition: Drawing an app behind the system bars so content reaches the physical screen edges, with insets applied only to what must stay tappable.
terms.useWhen: content under the bars, controls kept clear of them

terms.name: Editorial web design
terms.definition: A style that borrows print magazine craft for the screen: a visible column grid, display type at poster scale, pull quotes, rules, and captioned images set into the text.

sources.title: Wix: The biggest web design trends

terms.useWhen: a page styled like a magazine spread rather than a template

terms.name: 8 point grid
terms.definition: A spacing convention where every size and gap is a multiple of eight, so values stay whole numbers at every common screen density.
terms.useWhen: picking a base unit for a whole system

terms.name: Elevation
terms.definition: How high a surface sits above the one behind it, expressed as a shadow, a tint, or both, and held to a few named steps so that height means something.
terms.useWhen: how high a surface sits above the one behind

terms.name: Elevation overlay
terms.definition: The older dark theme technique of laying white over a surface at an opacity that rises with elevation, because shadows are nearly invisible on dark backgrounds.
terms.useWhen: raising a dark surface where a shadow would not show

terms.name: Em dash
terms.definition: The longest common dash, about the width of the letter m, used to set off an abrupt break or an aside inside a sentence.
terms.useWhen: naming the longest dash on the keyboard

terms.name: Em
terms.definition: A relative unit equal to the current font size, historically the width of the square the letter m was cast on.
terms.useWhen: sizing something relative to the text it sits in

terms.name: Emergency exit button
terms.definition: A control that leaves the current page immediately for an unrelated site and tries to clear it from history, for readers who may be watched.
terms.useWhen: leaving a page fast and without a trace

terms.name: Emoji picker
terms.definition: A searchable grid of emoji organised by category, with recent choices remembered and skin tone chosen once.
terms.useWhen: choosing an emoji from a searchable grid

terms.name: Emoji presentation
terms.definition: Whether a character that can be either a symbol or an emoji renders as flat text or as a colour emoji, selected by a variation selector or by CSS.
terms.useWhen: a symbol turns into an emoji you did not want

terms.name: Emphasis level
terms.definition: A three-rung text hierarchy, high, medium and disabled, ranked by stepping the opacity of one foreground colour instead of naming a separate colour for each rung.
terms.useWhen: ranking text by opacity instead of by separate colours

terms.name: Empty state
terms.definition: The screen a container shows when it holds nothing, naming the absence and offering the action that ends it.

sources.title: Nielsen Norman Group: Empty states in application design

terms.useWhen: the screen for a container with nothing in it yet

terms.name: En dash
terms.definition: A dash about the width of the letter n, used for ranges of numbers and for connections between two things.
terms.useWhen: writing a range of numbers or dates

terms.name: Endowed progress
terms.definition: Starting a progress meter part filled, so the reader feels they are continuing something already begun rather than starting from nothing.

sources.title: GoodUI: Try Upfront Progress instead of starting with a blank

terms.useWhen: the progress bar starts at 20 percent before you did anything

terms.name: Entrance animation
terms.definition: The motion an element plays as it arrives, running from a starting style that only exists before the element was ever rendered.
terms.useWhen: something new appears and should not just pop in

terms.name: Error bar
terms.definition: Whiskers on a mark showing the range a value could plausibly take, so a chart does not imply precision it does not have.

sources.title: Fundamentals of Data Visualization: Visualizing uncertainty

terms.useWhen: a chart states an estimate and honesty requires showing the spread

terms.name: Error identification
terms.definition: Naming the field that failed and saying what went wrong in text, rather than only outlining the input in red.
terms.useWhen: the failure has to be named in text, not carried by red alone

terms.name: Error message
terms.definition: The line attached to a field that says what went wrong and what to do about it, announced to assistive technology the moment it appears.
terms.useWhen: telling one field that its value failed

terms.name: Error page
terms.definition: The whole screen a site serves instead of the page that was asked for: what happened, in the reader's words, and the shortest way back to something that works.

sources.title: Nielsen Norman Group: Improving the dreaded 404 error message
GOV.UK Design System: Page not found pages
GOV.UK Design System: Problem with the service pages

terms.useWhen: the requested page cannot be served at all, not one field failing

terms.name: Error summary
terms.definition: A block at the top of a failed form listing every problem as links that move focus to the field that caused it.

sources.title: GOV.UK Design System: recover from validation errors

terms.useWhen: one list at the top links to each broken field

terms.name: Escape gesture
terms.definition: The screen reader equivalent of the Escape key, a two finger scrub that dismisses a sheet or steps back a level.

sources.title: Apple: Supporting Accessibility (View Controller Programming Guide)

terms.useWhen: a custom sheet ignores the platform dismiss gesture

terms.name: Exit animation
terms.definition: The motion an element plays on its way out, which requires deferring its removal from the layout until the animation has finished.
terms.useWhen: something is being removed and should not blink out

terms.name: Expandable row
terms.definition: A table row that opens to reveal a detail panel beneath it, keeping the row in place instead of navigating away.
terms.useWhen: row detail that opens in place under the row

terms.name: Expanded state
terms.definition: The open or closed state of a disclosure, exposed with aria-expanded on the control that owns it rather than on the panel it reveals.
terms.useWhen: the trigger must say whether its panel is open

terms.name: Explore by touch
terms.definition: The touch screen reader mode where dragging a finger reads whatever is under it and activation takes a second, deliberate tap, so nothing fires by accident.

sources.title: Android Accessibility Help: Navigate your device with TalkBack
Deque University: TalkBack keyboard shortcuts and gestures

terms.useWhen: designing touch targets a finger has to find blind

terms.name: Express checkout
terms.definition: A row of one-tap payment buttons placed above the normal form, which fetch address and payment details from a wallet the buyer already has.
terms.useWhen: the wallet buttons above the checkout form

terms.name: Eyebrow
terms.definition: A short line of text above a heading that says what category or series the content belongs to.
terms.useWhen: labelling what kind of thing a heading is

terms.name: Eyedropper
terms.definition: A tool that turns the cursor into a sampler so a colour can be picked from anywhere on screen, usually with a magnified preview of the pixel under it.
terms.useWhen: sampling a colour from pixels rather than typing a value

terms.name: F pattern
terms.definition: The scanning shape eye tracking finds on text heavy pages: two horizontal sweeps across the top, then a vertical run down the left edge.
terms.useWhen: predicting how a text heavy page gets skimmed

terms.name: Faceted filter
terms.definition: A panel of grouped checkboxes and ranges that narrows a result set, each option usually showing how many results it would leave.
terms.useWhen: narrowing results by category with counts

terms.name: Faceted search
terms.definition: Narrowing results by ticking values from several independent attribute groups, with counts showing how many results each value would leave.

sources.title: A List Apart: Design Patterns, Faceted Navigation

terms.useWhen: filters grouped by attribute, each showing result counts

terms.name: Fade
terms.definition: A change in opacity used to bring an element in or take it out, the cheapest transition and the one that implies no spatial relationship.
terms.useWhen: an element appears or leaves without moving

terms.name: Fade through
terms.definition: Material's transition for unrelated views: the outgoing view fades out completely before the incoming one fades in while scaling up slightly.
terms.useWhen: two views have no spatial or hierarchical relationship

terms.name: Fake door
terms.definition: A control that looks shipped and leads nowhere, put in the interface on purpose to count how many people want the feature behind it.

sources.title: Optimizely optimization glossary: Painted door test
Amplitude: What is fake door testing?

terms.useWhen: measuring demand for a feature by shipping only its entrance

terms.name: Fake scarcity
terms.definition: Claiming limited supply that is not real, with stock counts or demand messages generated to pressure a decision rather than report a fact.
terms.useWhen: only three left, and the number is invented

terms.name: Fake social proof
terms.definition: Manufacturing evidence that other people approve, through invented reviews, testimonials, or live activity messages nobody actually generated.
terms.useWhen: someone in Leeds just bought this, and nobody did

terms.name: Fake urgency
terms.definition: Presenting a deadline that does not exist, usually a timer that resets on reload, so the reader hurries a decision they had time to make.
terms.useWhen: the countdown resets when you refresh the page

terms.name: Fallback font
terms.definition: The typeface actually used when the preferred one is missing or has not loaded, either for the whole run of text or for characters it lacks.

sources.title: Framework tools for font fallbacks (Chrome for Developers)
Creating Perfect Font Fallbacks in CSS

terms.useWhen: naming what shows up when the real font does not

terms.name: False bottom
terms.definition: A page that looks finished at a point where content actually continues, so the reader stops scrolling and never sees the rest.

sources.title: GoodUI: Try Suggesting Continuity instead of false bottoms

terms.useWhen: the page looks like it ended but has not

terms.name: Faux bold
terms.definition: A bold or italic the browser fakes by smearing or shearing the regular weight, because the real style was never loaded.
terms.useWhen: your bold looks wrong and blurry

terms.name: Feature gate
terms.definition: Showing a locked feature in place, with its real position in the interface, so the reader sees what upgrading would unlock rather than a hidden absence.

sources.title: GoodUI: Try exposing options instead of hiding them

terms.useWhen: a locked feature stays visible with an upgrade badge

terms.name: Feature spotlight
terms.definition: A one-time announcement pointing at something newly added, shown in place next to the feature and dismissed for good once acknowledged.
terms.useWhen: the one-time New badge pointing at a change

terms.name: Feed layout
terms.definition: A scrolling column or adaptive grid of equivalent items built for browsing, where no item outranks another by position alone.
terms.useWhen: endless peers you skim rather than navigate

terms.name: Feedforward
terms.definition: What an interface says about the result of an act before it is taken, the half of the loop that sits ahead of the action rather than after it.

sources.title: Djajadiningrat, Overbeeke and Wensveen: But how, Donald, tell us how? (DIS 2002)
Vermeulen, Luyten, van den Hoven and Coninx: Crossing the bridge over Norman's gulf of execution (CHI 2013)

terms.useWhen: telling someone what will happen before they act

terms.name: Fictional user interface
terms.definition: The screen graphics style invented for film, television, and games: dense readouts, targeting reticles, and animated telemetry that look computational without computing anything.

sources.title: Reel Deal Film School: Creating Fantasy User Interfaces (FUIs)
Kit FUI: user interfaces from movies, TV and video games

terms.useWhen: interface art made to be watched rather than used

terms.name: Fieldset
terms.definition: A group of related form controls sharing one question, with a legend that acts as the label for the whole group.
terms.useWhen: several controls answering one question

terms.name: Figure
terms.definition: An image, table or code block bound to its caption so the two travel together and can be referred to from the running text.
terms.useWhen: a visual needs a caption that belongs to it

terms.name: File attachment
terms.definition: A row or card standing in for a file, showing its type, name and size, with the one action that file supports: download, open or remove.
terms.useWhen: a file has to be represented rather than uploaded

terms.name: File upload
terms.definition: A control that takes files, by opening the system picker from a button or by accepting a drop into a marked area.
terms.useWhen: the form takes files rather than text

terms.name: Fill mode
terms.definition: Whether an animation's first or last keyframe styles apply outside its running window, which decides if an element snaps back when it finishes or stays where it landed.
terms.useWhen: an animation ends and the element must not jump back

terms.name: Filmstrip
terms.definition: A scrollable row of thumbnails beside a larger view, where picking one changes what the large view shows.
terms.useWhen: a thumbnail rail that drives a big preview

terms.name: Fine print
terms.definition: Qualifying text set small and set last, carrying the conditions that the larger claim above it leaves out.

sources.title: FTC: .com Disclosures, How to Make Effective Disclosures in Digital Advertising (2013)

terms.useWhen: the terms that qualify a claim, set below the threshold of attention

terms.name: First-line indent
terms.definition: Indenting the opening line of a paragraph so the start of each paragraph is visible without a blank line between them.
terms.useWhen: marking new paragraphs without adding space

terms.name: First rule of ARIA
terms.definition: The maxim that no ARIA is better than bad ARIA: if a native element does the job, use it rather than pinning a role onto a div and reimplementing the behaviour.

aliases.name: no ARIA is better than bad ARIA

sources.title: W3C: Using ARIA, rules of ARIA use

terms.useWhen: someone proposes a role instead of an element

terms.name: First run experience
terms.definition: Everything shown only on the very first open, from a welcome sequence to seeded sample content, and never shown to that person again.
terms.useWhen: what happens only the very first time you open it

terms.name: Fisheye view
terms.definition: A focus plus context display that magnifies whatever has attention and progressively compresses everything further away, like a lens dragged along a list.

sources.title: A Review of Overview+Detail, Zooming, and Focus+Context Interfaces, Cockburn, Karlson and Bederson

terms.useWhen: magnifying one item without hiding the rest

terms.name: Fitts's law
terms.definition: The rule that the time to hit a target grows with its distance and shrinks with its size, which is why screen edges and corners are so easy to reach.

sources.title: Smashing Magazine: accessible tap target sizes

terms.useWhen: arguing about how big or how near a control should be

terms.name: Flame graph
terms.definition: Stacked bars where width is time spent and depth is call nesting, so the widest plateau rather than the tallest tower is the thing worth fixing.
terms.useWhen: nested call stacks with width as time spent

terms.name: Flash of inaccurate color theme
terms.definition: The moment a page paints in the wrong theme before the stored preference is applied, showing a light flash to a reader who chose dark.

sources.title: Avoiding Flash of Inaccurate Theme Color

terms.useWhen: the wrong theme showing for a frame on page load

terms.name: Flashing content
terms.definition: Content that flashes more than three times per second in a large enough area, restricted because it can trigger seizures.

aliases.name: general flash and red flash thresholds

sources.title: WCAG 2.2: Three Flashes or Below Threshold

terms.useWhen: judging whether a flash rate is dangerous

terms.name: Flat design
terms.definition: A style that strips away depth cues, using solid fills, sharp edges, and bold color instead of shadow, gradient, bevel, or texture.

sources.title: NN/g: Flat Design: Its Origins, Its Problems, and Why Flat 2.0 Is Better for Users
CareerFoundry: Flat Design: A Complete Beginner's Guide

terms.useWhen: no depth cues at all, only color and shape

terms.name: Flat 2.0
terms.definition: Flat design with the depth cues put back in small doses: soft shadow, subtle gradient, and hover feedback that show what can actually be clicked.

sources.title: NN/g: Flat Design: Its Origins, Its Problems, and Why Flat 2.0 Is Better for Users
UXPin: The 7-Minute Guide to Flat Design 2.0

terms.useWhen: flat surfaces, but affordance restored with light shadow

terms.name: Fling
terms.definition: The fastest of the drag family: contact is released while it is still moving, so the content keeps travelling and the gesture cannot be dragged back.

sources.title: Material Design: gestures (drag, swipe, and fling)

terms.useWhen: a throw that releases mid-motion and cannot be taken back

terms.name: FLIP
terms.definition: A technique that measures an element's first and last positions, inverts the difference with a transform, then plays it off, so layout changes animate cheaply.
terms.useWhen: a layout change must animate without animating layout properties

terms.name: Float animation
terms.definition: A slow continuous up and down drift on an idle element, so a static composition keeps breathing without asking for attention.
terms.useWhen: a hero illustration should not look frozen

terms.name: Floating action button
terms.definition: A round, raised button that hovers above the content in a fixed corner, carrying the one action the screen is most for.
terms.useWhen: the screen has a single dominant action

terms.name: Floating label
terms.definition: A label that sits inside an empty field and rises to the field's top edge when the field takes focus or holds a value.

sources.title: MUI Text Field: the label that shrinks on focus or value

terms.useWhen: the label starts inside the box and moves up

terms.name: Flowchart
terms.definition: A diagram of steps in boxes joined by arrows, read rather than operated, and now more often generated from a few lines of text than drawn by hand.
terms.useWhen: steps in boxes joined by arrows, read not operated

terms.name: Fluid grid
terms.definition: A grid whose columns and gutters are expressed as proportions rather than fixed pixels, so the whole composition stretches and shrinks with its container.

sources.title: Responsive Web Design, A List Apart

terms.useWhen: columns measured in proportions, not pixels

terms.name: Fluid hybrid
terms.definition: A mail layout that reflows with no media query at all: percentage widths held in by max-width, with fixed-width ghost tables that only Outlook can see.

sources.title: Email on Acid: a fluid hybrid design primer
Litmus: understanding responsive and hybrid email design

terms.useWhen: a mail that reflows without media queries

terms.name: Fluid space scale
terms.definition: A spacing ramp whose every step interpolates between a minimum and a maximum viewport, so gaps grow smoothly with the screen instead of jumping at breakpoints.
terms.useWhen: spacing that scales with the screen, not in steps

terms.name: Fluid typography
terms.definition: Type sizes that scale continuously with the viewport between a minimum and a maximum, rather than jumping at breakpoints.

sources.title: Creating a Fluid Type Scale (Modern CSS)

terms.useWhen: sizing text across screens without breakpoints

terms.name: Focal point
terms.definition: The one element a composition is built around, given enough size, contrast or isolation that the eye lands there before anywhere else.

sources.title: Design Principles: Compositional, Symmetrical And Asymmetrical Balance

terms.useWhen: naming the thing the eye should hit first

terms.name: Focus appearance
terms.definition: The size and contrast a focus indicator must reach to count as visible: enough area around the control, enough change against both the control and its background.
terms.useWhen: judging whether a focus ring is strong enough

terms.name: Focus delegation
terms.definition: A shadow root option that forwards focus from the host into the first focusable element inside it, so clicking the padding of a custom element does not leave focus nowhere.

sources.title: Frontend Masters: Shadow DOM focus delegation

terms.useWhen: a custom element swallows clicks near its edges

terms.name: Focus follows mouse
terms.definition: A focus model in which whatever the pointer is over receives keyboard input, without any click to claim it first.

sources.title: LWN: focus follows mouse or click to focus?

terms.useWhen: keyboard input goes where the pointer is pointing

terms.name: Focus management
terms.definition: Deliberately moving keyboard focus after a state change so the reader lands on the new content instead of at the top of the document.
terms.useWhen: deciding where focus goes when the UI changes

terms.name: Focus not obscured
terms.definition: The requirement that a focused control is not completely hidden by sticky headers, footers, cookie bars, or chat widgets when it receives focus.

sources.title: W3C F110: sticky footer or header hiding focused elements

terms.useWhen: the sticky header swallows the focused control

terms.name: Focus order
terms.definition: The sequence keyboard focus follows through a page, which should match reading order instead of source quirks or positive tabindex values.
terms.useWhen: the path Tab takes through a whole page

terms.name: Focus plus context
terms.definition: A layout that keeps one region in full detail inside its own surroundings, shrinking or dimming the context instead of moving it into a second pane.

sources.title: A Review of Overview+Detail, Zooming, and Focus+Context Interfaces, Cockburn, Karlson and Bederson

terms.useWhen: detail and its surroundings in one view

terms.name: Focus ring
terms.definition: The visible outline drawn around the element that currently holds keyboard focus, showing where the next keypress will land.
terms.useWhen: marking where keyboard focus is sitting right now

terms.name: Focus trap
terms.definition: A constraint that keeps keyboard focus cycling inside one region until that region is dismissed.
terms.useWhen: focus deliberately held inside one region

terms.name: Focus visible
terms.definition: A focus style shown only when focus arrived by keyboard or another non-pointer route, so a mouse click does not leave a ring behind.
terms.useWhen: showing the ring to keyboard users but not to clickers

terms.name: Focusable disabled
terms.definition: A control styled as unavailable but left in the tab order with aria-disabled, so a reader can find it and learn why it is off.

sources.title: ARIA APG: Developing a Keyboard Interface

terms.useWhen: a disabled control still needs to be discoverable

terms.name: Focusable scroll region
terms.definition: Giving a scrollable box its own tab stop so a keyboard user can scroll it, which matters whenever the content inside holds no focusable element of its own.

sources.title: Deque: Scrollable region must have keyboard access

terms.useWhen: a code block or log pane scrolls but cannot be reached

terms.name: FOFT
terms.definition: A loading strategy that shows the roman weight as soon as it arrives and lets the remaining styles swap in afterwards, so the swap happens in stages.
terms.useWhen: staging a font swap instead of taking it all at once

terms.name: FOIT
terms.definition: The blank period when a browser hides text entirely rather than show it in a fallback face while the web font loads.

sources.title: Ensure text remains visible during webfont load (Lighthouse)

terms.useWhen: the text is missing, not just wrong, on load

terms.name: Follow-through
terms.definition: Parts of a composition that keep moving briefly after the main element stops, and start slightly after it starts, so a group does not move as one rigid block.

sources.title: IxDF: UI Animation, applying Disney's 12 principles to UI

terms.useWhen: a group should move like connected parts, not one slab

terms.name: Hinting
terms.definition: Instructions inside a font that nudge its outlines onto the pixel grid at small sizes so stems stay crisp and even.
terms.useWhen: explaining why type looks fuzzy at small sizes

terms.name: Font metric override
terms.definition: Reshaping a fallback font's size and vertical metrics in CSS so it occupies the same space as the web font and the swap shifts nothing.

sources.title: Framework tools for font fallbacks (Chrome for Developers)
Creating Perfect Font Fallbacks in CSS

terms.useWhen: killing the layout jump when a web font lands

terms.name: Font pairing
terms.definition: Choosing two or more typefaces that work together, usually one expressive and one neutral, with enough contrast to read as a deliberate choice.

sources.title: Three secrets to font pairing (Adobe Design)

terms.useWhen: deciding which two typefaces to run together

terms.name: Font smoothing
terms.definition: How a device softens the edges of letterforms, either by shading whole pixels grey or by lighting a pixel's colored subpixels separately.

sources.title: What's the deal with WebKit Font Smoothing?

terms.useWhen: your type looks heavier on one platform than another

terms.name: Font stack
terms.definition: The ordered list of typefaces a rule names, each tried in turn until one is available, ending in a generic family.

sources.title: Creating Perfect Font Fallbacks in CSS

terms.useWhen: listing which fonts to try and in what order

terms.name: Font subsetting
terms.definition: Shipping only the characters a page actually needs, cutting the font file down and letting the browser fetch ranges on demand.
terms.useWhen: cutting a font file down to what the page uses

terms.name: Font weight
terms.definition: How thick a typeface's strokes are, named in steps from thin to black and numbered from 100 to 900 on the web.
terms.useWhen: naming how heavy the strokes are

terms.name: Force touch
terms.definition: A press whose depth is part of the input, letting a harder press mean something different from a light one on a pressure sensing surface.
terms.useWhen: press depth carries meaning, not just contact

terms.name: Forced colors mode
terms.definition: An operating system mode that replaces a page's palette with a small user-chosen set of system colours, overriding almost everything an author specified.

sources.title: Styling for Windows high contrast with forced colors

terms.useWhen: the OS is imposing its own palette on your interface

terms.name: Forced continuity
terms.definition: Turning a free trial into a paid subscription automatically, with the card taken up front and no reminder before the first real charge.
terms.useWhen: a free trial quietly becomes a paid plan

terms.name: Forgiving format
terms.definition: Accepting whatever shape the reader types and normalising it afterwards, instead of rejecting input that differs only in spacing or punctuation.

sources.title: GoodUI: Try Forgiving Inputs instead of being strict with data

terms.useWhen: the field takes the card number however you type it

terms.name: Form
terms.definition: A grouping of controls a reader fills in and submits together, carrying the labels, validation and submit affordance for the whole set.
terms.useWhen: a set of inputs is submitted as one unit

terms.name: FOUT
terms.definition: The visible swap when a page first paints text in a fallback face and then re-renders it once the web font arrives.
terms.useWhen: the text visibly changes font on load

terms.name: Frame rate
terms.definition: How many frames a second the interface actually draws, the budget every animation spends: 60fps leaves about 16ms per frame and a 120Hz display halves it.

sources.title: MDN: animation performance and frame rate

terms.useWhen: motion has to be judged in milliseconds per frame

terms.name: Friend spam
terms.definition: Asking for access to a contact list under one pretext and using it to send invitations that appear to come from the reader.

sources.title: Deceptive Design: types of deceptive pattern

terms.useWhen: the app mails your contacts as if you had

terms.name: Frozen column
terms.definition: A table column held against the edge while the rest scrolls sideways, so the row's identifying value stays readable.

sources.title: Data Grid column pinning, MUI X

terms.useWhen: a wide table where you lose track of the row

terms.name: Frutiger Aero
terms.definition: The mid 2000s look of glossy gradients, bubbles, water, bright skies, and clean humanist type, named after the typeface and Windows Aero.
terms.useWhen: glossy optimistic 2000s tech imagery

terms.name: Frutiger Metro
terms.definition: The flat vector cousin of Frutiger Aero: gradient color blocks, bloom and glow, silhouetted figures, swooshes and abstract flourishes, without the glossy water and grass.
terms.useWhen: gradient vector blocks with bloom and swooshes

terms.name: Full bleed
terms.definition: An element that breaks past the content column to span the whole viewport width while its neighbours stay constrained.

sources.title: CSS Grid full-bleed layout tutorial, Josh W. Comeau

terms.useWhen: one band that runs edge to edge inside a narrow page

terms.name: Functional need
terms.definition: A statement of the gap between what a person can do and what a design demands, the WCAG 3 draft's way of naming a barrier without sorting people into disability categories.
terms.useWhen: framing a barrier without naming a diagnosis

terms.name: Gamut mapping
terms.definition: Converting a colour that falls outside a display's range into the nearest one inside it, usually by lowering chroma in OKLCH rather than clipping each channel.
terms.useWhen: bringing an impossible colour into a display's range

terms.name: Gantt chart
terms.definition: One row per task with a bar along a time axis, the bar showing when the work runs and lines between bars showing what waits for what.
terms.useWhen: tasks as bars on a time axis, with dependencies

terms.name: Gauge
terms.definition: A dial style readout showing one value on an arc between a minimum and a maximum, borrowed from instrument panels.
terms.useWhen: a value read off an arc like a dial

terms.name: Generative UI
terms.definition: An interface whose parts are chosen or composed by a model at runtime, so a request is answered with a built form, chart, or panel instead of a paragraph of text.

sources.title: CopilotKit: Generative UI, understanding agent-powered interfaces
Builder.io: Designing generative UI in an agent-native world

terms.useWhen: the model assembles the screen, not just the words

terms.name: Ghost button
terms.definition: A button with no fill and often no border until you hover it, sitting at the bottom of the emphasis ladder above a plain link.
terms.useWhen: naming the least emphatic button variant

terms.name: Ghost click
terms.definition: A stray click the browser emits after a touch has already been handled, landing on whatever moved under the finger in the meantime.

sources.title: FastClick: polyfill to remove click delays
Chrome for Developers: 300ms tap delay, gone away

terms.useWhen: one touch produces a second, unwanted activation

terms.name: Glassmorphism
terms.definition: A style where surfaces are translucent and blur what is behind them, separated from the backdrop by a hairline edge and a soft shadow.
terms.useWhen: a translucent panel that blurs whatever is behind it

terms.name: Glitch aesthetic
terms.definition: A look that fakes signal failure with colour channel offset, torn scan bands, and jitter, used for emphasis or as a whole visual identity.
terms.useWhen: deliberate corruption used as decoration

terms.name: Global navigation
terms.definition: The links to the top tier of a site's structure, present on every page and unchanged wherever the reader currently is.

sources.title: The Difference Between Information Architecture and Navigation, NN/g

terms.useWhen: the nav that is the same on every page

terms.name: Gloss
terms.definition: A wet plastic finish made from a light gradient across the top half of a control, a highlight arc, and a darker lower half.

sources.title: GirlieMac: CSS3 Gradients, no image Aqua button

terms.useWhen: the control looks like polished wet plastic

terms.name: Glyph
terms.definition: A single drawn shape in a font, which may be one character, a variant of one, or several characters fused together.
terms.useWhen: talking about drawn shapes rather than characters

terms.name: Goal gradient
terms.definition: Effort rising as a visible goal gets closer, which is why interfaces show how little is left rather than how much has been done.
terms.useWhen: the interface shows how close you are, not how far you came

terms.name: Golden ratio
terms.definition: The proportion of roughly 1 to 1.618 used to divide a layout, so its parts relate to each other by a rule instead of by arbitrary numbers.

sources.title: A designer's guide to the Golden Ratio, Creative Bloq

terms.useWhen: picking proportions that are not arbitrary

terms.name: Gooey effect
terms.definition: Blurring a group of shapes and then crushing the blur back to a hard edge so overlapping elements merge into one liquid silhouette as they move apart and together.

sources.title: Animation Patterns: SVG metaball gooey filter with feColorMatrix

terms.useWhen: two moving shapes should read as one substance

terms.name: Grabber
terms.definition: The short rounded bar drawn at the top of a bottom sheet to say the surface can be dragged.
terms.useWhen: the little bar on top of a sheet

terms.name: Grade
terms.definition: A variable font axis that thickens or thins strokes without changing any character's width, so text can get darker without reflowing.
terms.useWhen: darkening text on a dark background without reflow

terms.name: Gradient
