terms.definition: A fill that transitions between two or more colours across a shape, defined by colour stops and by the space the transition is interpolated in.
terms.useWhen: a fill that changes colour across its own area

terms.name: Gradient border
terms.definition: An outline filled with a gradient rather than a single color, usually built from a conic or linear gradient behind a masked shape so the hue travels around the edge.

sources.title: web.dev: Use conic gradients to create a cool border
Bram.us: Animating a CSS Gradient Border
Bejamas: Finding the best way to create animated gradient borders in CSS

terms.useWhen: an outline whose color changes along its length

terms.name: Gradual engagement
terms.definition: Replacing a sign-up form at the front door with a first useful action, so the reader experiences value before being asked for anything.

sources.title: GoodUI: Try Gradual Engagement instead of a hasty sign up

terms.useWhen: the first screen does something instead of asking you to register

terms.name: Grainy gradient
terms.definition: A gradient with a fine noise layer over it, added to hide banding and give a flat background the texture of printed paper or film.

sources.title: ibelick: Creating grainy backgrounds with CSS

terms.useWhen: a smooth background deliberately roughened with noise

terms.name: Graph layout
terms.definition: Placing the nodes of a wired diagram by algorithm rather than by hand: layered for a flow, radial for a hub, force-directed for a mesh that has no direction.
terms.useWhen: nodes placed by algorithm rather than by hand

terms.name: Grid lanes
terms.definition: The native masonry mechanism in CSS grid, where one axis keeps strict tracks and the other lets items stack into whichever lane has room.
terms.useWhen: masonry without a library, straight from grid

terms.name: Group label
terms.definition: The one name that covers a set of controls, a question above its radio buttons or a heading above an address block, so each field is heard in context.
terms.useWhen: individual field labels make no sense on their own

terms.name: Grunge design
terms.definition: A 1990s style of torn and photocopied texture, overlapped and cut type, off-grid layout, and dirty muted colour, where legibility is traded for emotional pitch.

sources.title: Sessions College: The grunge typography of David Carson
Mew Design Docs: Grunge graphic design, the raw distressed art of the 90s

terms.useWhen: distressed texture and type deliberately off-grid

terms.name: Guest checkout
terms.definition: Letting a buyer complete a purchase without creating an account, with the offer to save details moved to after the order is placed.

sources.title: Baymard Institute: the checkout UX guide

terms.useWhen: buying without being made to create an account

terms.name: Gutenberg diagram
terms.definition: A model splitting evenly weighted pages into four quadrants, with the eye falling from the primary area at top left to the terminal area at bottom right.
terms.useWhen: placing the last thing you want read

terms.name: Gutter
terms.definition: The space between columns or tracks in a grid, distinct from the outer margin that separates the grid from the container edge.
terms.useWhen: the space between columns, not around them

terms.name: Half-leading
terms.definition: The empty space a browser splits evenly above and below a line of text when line height exceeds the font's own height, which is why text boxes never sit flush.

sources.title: Leading-Trim: The Future of Digital Typesetting

terms.useWhen: explaining the mystery padding around a line of text

terms.name: Halftone
terms.definition: Rendering tone as a grid of dots that vary in size, borrowed from print and used to give flat interface art a comic or newsprint feel.
terms.useWhen: tone made of print dots that grow and shrink

terms.name: Hamburger menu
terms.definition: A button of three stacked horizontal lines that opens a site's main navigation, usually in a panel over the page.

sources.title: Nielsen Norman Group: Hamburger menus and hidden navigation hurt UX

terms.useWhen: the three-line button that opens the whole navigation

terms.name: Hand-drawn UI
terms.definition: A style whose lines wobble as if sketched by hand, used to signal that a diagram or wireframe is provisional rather than finished.
terms.useWhen: the sketchiness says this is not final yet

terms.name: Hanging indent
terms.definition: A paragraph whose first line starts further left than the rest, so the following lines are indented under it.
terms.useWhen: setting bibliographies, definitions, or list labels

terms.name: Hanging punctuation
terms.definition: Letting quotes, hyphens, and other light marks sit outside the text column so the edge of the text reads as straight to the eye.

sources.title: Hung Punctuation and Optical Margin Alignment (CreativePro)

terms.useWhen: a quote mark makes the left edge look dented

terms.name: Haptic feedback
terms.definition: A brief physical vibration or tap produced by the device to confirm an interaction, mark a boundary, or signal success and failure.
terms.useWhen: feedback the user feels rather than sees or hears

terms.name: Has popup
terms.definition: A hint on a trigger that says something will open and what kind of thing it will be, a menu, a listbox, a dialog, before the reader commits to pressing it.
terms.useWhen: a button opens a menu and gives no warning

terms.name: HCT
terms.definition: Material's colour space of hue, chroma and tone, which borrows hue and chroma from CAM16 and lightness from CIELAB so tone alone predicts contrast.

sources.title: Material 3: how the color system works

terms.useWhen: generating a Material palette where tone predicts contrast

terms.name: Heading
terms.definition: A short line of type that names the section under it and, by its size and weight, says how far down the outline that section sits.
terms.useWhen: naming a section and showing its depth at once

terms.name: Heading hierarchy
terms.definition: The nested outline formed by heading levels, navigated directly by assistive technology and broken by skipping a level or picking a level for its size.
terms.useWhen: structuring a page so it can be skimmed by heading

terms.name: Height animation
terms.definition: Animating a container between collapsed and its content's natural size, long impossible because height auto did not interpolate and now opened up by interpolate-size and calc-size().

sources.title: Chrome for Developers: animate to height: auto

terms.useWhen: a section must grow to fit content without a magic pixel value

terms.name: Help drawer
terms.definition: Documentation opened beside the task rather than over it, keeping the form usable while the explanation is read and staying open across steps.
terms.useWhen: help opens beside the form instead of on top of it

terms.name: Helper text
terms.definition: The short line under a field that explains the format or constraint before anything goes wrong.
terms.useWhen: guidance under a field, not an error

terms.name: Hero
terms.definition: The large opening block of a page carrying a headline, a supporting line, imagery, and the main call to action.
terms.useWhen: the big opening block that sets the pitch

terms.name: Hex color
terms.definition: A colour written as a hash followed by three, four, six or eight hexadecimal digits, the notation most handoffs still speak even when the source is OKLCH.
terms.useWhen: the notation a colour is handed over in

terms.name: Hidden but focusable
terms.definition: An element hidden from assistive technology that is still in the tab sequence, so keyboard focus lands on something a screen reader refuses to describe.

sources.title: W3C ACT: Element with aria-hidden has no content in sequential focus navigation
Deque: aria-hidden elements do not contain focusable elements

terms.useWhen: focus disappears into an offscreen or hidden panel

terms.name: Hidden gesture
terms.definition: An action reachable only by an input the reader has to guess: a swipe, a long press, a two-finger tap, with nothing on screen saying it is there.
terms.useWhen: an action only an unadvertised gesture reaches

terms.name: Hit slop
terms.definition: Invisible padding that extends a control's activatable area beyond its drawn bounds, so a small icon can stay small and still be easy to hit.

sources.title: Smashing Magazine: accessible tap target sizes

terms.useWhen: the tappable area is bigger than the visible control

terms.name: Hit testing
terms.definition: Working out which element sits under a pointer, which decides who receives the event when shapes overlap or transparent areas are in the way.
terms.useWhen: asking which element a click actually lands on

terms.name: Hold to confirm
terms.definition: Requiring a press to be held for a moment before a destructive action commits, with progress shown so the wait is understood as deliberate.
terms.useWhen: a dangerous action guarded by a held press

terms.name: Holographic foil
terms.definition: A finish that shifts hue with viewing angle, imitating foil, soap film, or a CD surface with banded rainbow gradients over a pale metallic ground.

sources.title: Envato Tuts+: 100+ best holographic and iridescent textures
Effect Labs: CSS holographic effect, iridescent and chrome

terms.useWhen: a surface whose colour shifts as if it were foil

terms.name: Holy grail layout
terms.definition: A three column page with header and footer where the centre column is fluid, the two side columns are fixed, and all three appear equal height.
terms.useWhen: the classic fixed, fluid, fixed three column page

terms.name: Home indicator
terms.definition: The thin bar at the bottom of a gesture driven phone screen, reserved space that app content must not sit beneath.
terms.useWhen: the reserved strip at the bottom of a modern phone

terms.name: Honeypot field
terms.definition: A form field hidden from people but visible to automated form fillers, used to reject submissions that fill it in without challenging anyone.
terms.useWhen: the invisible field that only a bot would fill in

terms.name: Hover
terms.definition: A pointer resting over an element without pressing, a state that exists for mice and pens but has no true equivalent on touch.
terms.useWhen: the pointer is over something but has not committed

terms.name: Hover card
terms.definition: A rich preview panel that appears on hover over a link or an avatar, summarising what is behind it.
terms.useWhen: a rich preview that opens on hover, not on click

terms.name: Hover intent
terms.definition: Waiting out a short delay or watching cursor direction before acting on a hover, so a pointer merely passing through does not open anything.

sources.title: Baymard: Provide a hover delay of 300 to 500 ms
NN/g: Timing guidelines for exposing hidden content
CSS-Tricks: Dropdown menus with more forgiving mouse movement paths

terms.useWhen: telling a deliberate hover from one passing through

terms.name: Hover lift
terms.definition: A card or button that rises a few pixels and deepens its shadow while the pointer is over it, so the whole surface reads as lifted toward the reader.

sources.title: Subframe: CSS card hover effect examples

terms.useWhen: a whole surface should answer the pointer, not just its border

terms.name: Hoverable, dismissible, persistent
terms.definition: The three conditions content revealed on hover or focus must meet: reachable with the pointer, dismissible without moving focus, and not self-closing.

sources.title: WCAG 2.2: Content on Hover or Focus
W3C SCR39: making content on hover or focus hoverable, dismissible, and persistent

terms.useWhen: judging whether a tooltip or flyout behaves

terms.name: Hub and spoke
terms.definition: A navigation shape where every task is reached from one home screen and returns to it, with no way to move sideways between tasks.
terms.useWhen: every section is reached from home and returns there

terms.name: HUD panel
terms.definition: A small dark translucent floating window of controls that hovers over content without taking it over, common in media and creative tools.
terms.useWhen: a small dark floating palette over content

terms.name: Hue
terms.definition: The attribute that gives a colour its name, red or teal or violet, expressed as an angle around a colour wheel independent of how light or vivid it is.
terms.useWhen: naming the colour itself, apart from its lightness or intensity

terms.name: Hue shift
terms.definition: Rotating hue deliberately along a ramp, warmer at the light end and cooler at the dark end, so a scale looks alive instead of like one colour fading out.

sources.title: Rampensau: palette generation with hue cycling

terms.useWhen: steering hue across a ramp instead of holding it fixed

terms.name: Hydration
terms.definition: The pass where script attaches behaviour to server-rendered HTML, turning a page that is already painted and readable into one that answers input.
terms.useWhen: the window where a page looks ready but answers nothing

terms.name: Hyperreal 3D
terms.definition: Rendered objects pushed past photographic realism, with physically based materials, sharp specular detail, and studio lighting, floated over an otherwise plain interface.

sources.title: wings.design: 3D and depth in UI, function versus aesthetic

terms.useWhen: a rendered hero object that outdoes a photograph

terms.name: Hyphenation
terms.definition: Breaking a word across two lines at a syllable boundary so lines fill more evenly, marked with a hyphen at the break.
terms.useWhen: keeping narrow columns from tearing open

terms.name: Hyphenation ladder
terms.definition: Three or more consecutive lines ending in a hyphen, which builds a visible staircase down the right edge of a column.
terms.useWhen: naming a stack of hyphens down a column edge

terms.name: Icon
terms.definition: A small graphic symbol standing for an action, object or idea, read at a glance and rarely safe to ship without a label.
terms.useWhen: a symbol has to carry meaning in very little space

terms.name: Icon button
terms.definition: A button whose whole label is an icon, so it needs an accessible name and usually a tooltip to say what it does.

sources.title: ARIA Authoring Practices Guide: Button pattern

terms.useWhen: a square control carrying only a glyph

terms.name: Icon font
terms.definition: A font whose glyphs are icons rather than letters, addressed by code point or by a ligature so an icon can be styled like text.

sources.title: SVG, Icon Fonts, and Accessibility (24 Accessibility)

terms.useWhen: icons delivered as type instead of as images

terms.name: Icon morph
terms.definition: An icon that animates between two meanings rather than cutting, such as a hamburger whose bars rotate into a close cross.

sources.title: School of Motion: The Essential Motion Design Dictionary

terms.useWhen: one control carries two states and should show the change

terms.name: Identicon
terms.definition: A generated default avatar derived deterministically from an identifier, so the same account always gets the same abstract pattern without uploading anything.
terms.useWhen: an account needs a face before the user provides one

terms.name: Image
terms.definition: An embedded picture, sized and cropped by the layout around it, carrying the alternative text that stands in when it cannot be seen.
terms.useWhen: a picture is content rather than decoration

terms.name: Image comparison slider
terms.definition: Two images stacked with a draggable divider that wipes between them, used to show a before and an after in one frame.

sources.title: img-comparison-slider: a web component for before and after images

terms.useWhen: showing before and after in one frame

terms.name: Image well
terms.definition: An editable image view that shows its current picture and accepts a replacement dragged or pasted straight into it.

sources.title: Apple Human Interface Guidelines: Image wells

terms.useWhen: a picture is both the display and the drop target

terms.name: Images of text
terms.definition: Text baked into a raster image, which cannot be resized, restyled, selected, translated, or read by anything but the alt attribute someone remembered to write.
terms.useWhen: arguing a headline should be text, not a picture of text

terms.name: Imposter
terms.definition: A layout primitive that positions one element centred over its container, overlapping whatever is beneath rather than taking a place in the flow.
terms.useWhen: one element floated dead centre over the rest

terms.name: Inert
terms.definition: A state that removes a subtree from focus order, hit testing, and the accessibility tree at once, used to seal the background behind a dialog.
terms.useWhen: making a whole region unreachable, not just invisible

terms.name: Infinite canvas
terms.definition: A workspace with no page edges, where content is placed anywhere in an unbounded plane and the viewport pans and zooms over it instead of scrolling a document.
terms.useWhen: a board with no page, only a viewport over it

terms.name: Infinite scroll
terms.definition: A list that appends the next page of results automatically as the reader approaches the bottom, so the content never ends and no page controls appear.

sources.title: NN/g: infinite scrolling, when to use it and when to avoid it

terms.useWhen: the feed loads more by itself as you near the bottom

terms.name: Initial focus
terms.definition: Where focus lands when a view, dialog, or page first appears, chosen deliberately rather than left on the body or dumped on the first close button.
terms.useWhen: a dialog opens and nobody decided where focus goes

terms.name: Ink trap
terms.definition: A notch cut out of a letter's inside corners so spreading ink or blurring pixels do not fill the joint solid.
terms.useWhen: naming the cut-out notches in a display typeface

terms.name: Inline autocomplete
terms.definition: Completing the reader's text inside the field itself, with the guessed remainder selected so the next keystroke replaces it.

implementations.name: Editable Combobox With Both List and Inline Autocomplete

terms.useWhen: the field finishes your word inside the field

terms.name: Inline edit
terms.definition: Text that reads as plain content until you click it, at which point it becomes an input in the same place with save and cancel.
terms.useWhen: editing a value where it is displayed

terms.name: Inline validation
terms.definition: Checking a field as the reader fills or leaves it and showing the verdict beside that field, rather than saving every complaint for the submit button.

sources.title: A List Apart: Inline Validation in Web Forms
Nielsen Norman Group: 10 Design Guidelines for Reporting Errors in Forms

terms.useWhen: a field tells you it is wrong before you submit

terms.name: Input group
terms.definition: A field welded to text, a button or a select at one or both ends, so the addon reads as part of the same control rather than as a neighbour.
terms.useWhen: a unit, prefix or action belongs inside the field

terms.name: Input mask
terms.definition: A field that imposes a fixed shape as you type, inserting the slashes, spaces or brackets a phone number or card number needs.
terms.useWhen: the field types its own punctuation for you

terms.name: Input purpose
terms.definition: Machine readable autocomplete tokens on personal fields, which let browsers autofill and let personalisation tools add familiar icons or wording.
terms.useWhen: telling the browser what a field is actually for

terms.name: Inspector
terms.definition: A pane, usually on the trailing edge, that shows and edits the properties of whatever is currently selected.
terms.useWhen: a panel whose contents follow the selection

terms.name: Interaction color step
terms.definition: The convention that hover, active and selected are the next steps along the same scale rather than separate colours, so states are derived from one ramp.
terms.useWhen: hover and pressed derived from a scale, not picked

terms.name: Interactive transition
terms.definition: A transition whose progress is held by an ongoing gesture, so the reader can drag it partway, hesitate, and either complete it or send it back.
terms.useWhen: a gesture should own the transition until it is released

terms.name: Interest invoker
terms.definition: A link or button that shows more when a reader shows interest in it, by hovering, focusing or long pressing, with no click and no script deciding what interest means.
terms.useWhen: showing more on interest rather than on a click

terms.name: Interface metaphor
terms.definition: Explaining a system by dressing it as something the user already knows: the desktop, the trash can, the folder, the shopping cart.

sources.title: Nielsen Norman Group: Metaphors in UX

terms.useWhen: a familiar concept is carrying the explanation of an unfamiliar system

terms.name: Interpolation
terms.definition: The rule that produces the intermediate values between two endpoints, which is why some properties can animate smoothly and others can only switch.
terms.useWhen: explaining why a property will or will not animate

terms.name: Interruptible animation
terms.definition: Motion that can be caught, reversed, or redirected mid-flight from its current value, instead of finishing before it will accept a new input.
terms.useWhen: a reader may act again before the motion finishes

terms.name: Interstitial
terms.definition: A full screen placed between two steps of a flow, carrying a message, an advert, or a warning that the reader must pass through to continue.
terms.useWhen: a whole screen sits between you and where you were going

terms.name: Intrinsic web design
terms.definition: Building layouts from what the content needs, using grid, flexbox and intrinsic sizing together, instead of imposing a fixed column skeleton.
terms.useWhen: naming the era after responsive web design

terms.name: Invalid state
terms.definition: The programmatic mark that a field's value failed validation, paired with a pointer to the message that explains it.
terms.useWhen: the field itself must report that it is wrong

terms.name: Inverse color
terms.definition: A surface and text pair deliberately flipped against the current theme, so a snackbar or tooltip reads as a foreign object that arrived from outside the page.

implementations.name: Inverse surface, Inverse on surface, Inverse primary

terms.useWhen: an element deliberately styled opposite to the theme

terms.name: Inverted colors
terms.definition: A whole-screen colour inversion applied by the OS, which flips a design nobody tested upside down and turns every shadow into a highlight.
terms.useWhen: the OS inverts your palette and shadows go wrong

terms.name: Invoker command
terms.definition: A button that names the element it acts on and what to do to it, in markup, so opening a dialog or toggling a popover needs no script at all.
terms.useWhen: a button wired to another element in markup

terms.name: Isometric illustration
terms.definition: Art drawn on a fixed axonometric grid so depth reads without perspective, with parallel edges and no vanishing point.
terms.useWhen: depth without perspective, on a fixed 30 degree grid

terms.name: Italic
terms.definition: A companion style with letterforms redrawn on a cursive model, not merely slanted, used for emphasis and titles.
terms.useWhen: emphasis inside running text

terms.name: Jank
terms.definition: Visible stutter in motion caused by frames arriving late or not at all, so an animation that should be continuous reads as juddering.

sources.title: MDN: animation performance and frame rate
web.dev: jank busting for better rendering performance

terms.useWhen: naming why smooth-looking motion feels wrong

terms.name: Jiggle mode
terms.definition: An editing state announced by making every rearrangeable item wobble in place, so the whole screen says it can be reordered.

sources.title: How-To Geek: what is jiggle mode on iPhone

terms.useWhen: an editing mode should be announced by motion alone

terms.name: Juiciness
terms.definition: Stacking far more feedback on an act than it needs, so one small input wobbles, pops and sings, and the interface feels alive under the hand.

sources.title: Game Developer: Is your game juicy enough?

terms.useWhen: deliberately excessive feedback for one small act

terms.name: Justified gallery
terms.definition: A photo grid that scales and trims images so every row lands on one shared height with flush left and right edges, unlike masonry's ragged columns.
terms.useWhen: photos of mixed shapes in tidy flush rows

terms.name: Justified text
terms.definition: Text set so both edges of the column are flush, achieved by stretching or squeezing the spaces between words on each line.
terms.useWhen: you want both edges of a column flush

terms.name: Kanban board
terms.definition: A row of vertical columns, each one a stage, holding cards that move sideways as work progresses.
terms.useWhen: items that belong to exactly one stage at a time

terms.name: Kawaii UI
terms.definition: A cute style of pastel fills, rounded everything, oversized eyes and blush marks, sticker and mascot characters, and hand-lettered or bubbly rounded type.

sources.title: Kittl: 60+ graphic design styles, names and descriptions

terms.useWhen: cuteness carried by mascots, pastels, and round shapes

terms.name: Keyboard key
terms.definition: A key drawn as a small keycap in running text or a menu, so a shortcut reads as something you press rather than something you say.
terms.useWhen: printing a key the reader should press

terms.name: Kebab menu
terms.definition: A menu of secondary actions opened from a trigger of three vertically stacked dots, usually at the end of a row, card, or toolbar.
terms.useWhen: extra actions behind three stacked dots

terms.name: Ken Burns effect
terms.definition: A slow pan and zoom across a still image that gives it motion, named after the documentary filmmaker who made the technique famous.
terms.useWhen: a static image needs life without becoming video

terms.name: Kerning
terms.definition: The adjustment of space between two particular letters so the pair reads evenly.
terms.useWhen: the space between two particular letters

terms.name: Key repeat
terms.definition: A held key firing repeatedly after an initial delay, which is how arrow keys scroll and backspace deletes more than one character.

sources.title: ARIA APG: Developing a keyboard interface

terms.useWhen: holding a key keeps producing the action

terms.name: Key sequence
terms.definition: A shortcut typed as an ordered run of presses, where the first key opens a mode and the next chooses within it.
terms.useWhen: shortcuts typed in order, like a prefix then a letter

terms.name: Keyboard shortcut
terms.definition: A key or key combination that runs a command directly, giving practised users a path that skips the menus and the pointer entirely.

sources.title: ARIA APG: Developing a keyboard interface

terms.useWhen: a command reachable by keys instead of controls

terms.name: Keyboard shortcuts dialog
terms.definition: The panel opened by pressing question mark that lists every shortcut in the application, grouped by area.
terms.useWhen: the cheat sheet of every shortcut

terms.name: Keyboard trap
terms.definition: A place keyboard focus can enter but not leave by keyboard alone, stranding anyone who is not using a pointer.

sources.title: ARIA APG: Developing a keyboard interface

terms.useWhen: focus goes in and cannot be tabbed back out

terms.name: Keyframe
terms.definition: A point in an animation where a value is pinned, with the frames between generated by interpolating from one pinned point to the next.

sources.title: School of Motion: motion design dictionary

terms.useWhen: an animation needs waypoints, not just a start and end

terms.name: Keyline
terms.definition: An invisible line that content across a whole screen aligns to, such as the edge line every row starts at and the deeper line where text begins after an icon.
terms.useWhen: the shared line every row's text starts on

terms.name: Kinetic typography
terms.definition: Type animated over time, where letters and words move, scale, stagger, or morph so the setting carries tone and emphasis a static line cannot.

sources.title: What is kinetic typography, a guide to text in motion (SVGator)
Kinetic typography, the what, why and how (Linearity)

terms.useWhen: the type itself performs rather than sits still

terms.name: Knob
terms.definition: A round control turned by dragging in an arc, borrowed from hardware and mostly found in audio and creative tools.
terms.useWhen: a dial you turn rather than a track you slide

terms.name: Label association
terms.definition: The programmatic link between a label and its field, made by for and id or by wrapping, which makes the label clickable and the field named.
terms.useWhen: connecting the words to the input they name

terms.name: Label in name
terms.definition: The rule that a control's accessible name must contain its visible label text, so speaking the visible words works in voice control.

sources.title: WCAG 2.2: Success Criterion 2.5.3 Label in Name
Understanding Success Criterion 2.5.3: Label in Name, W3C WAI

terms.useWhen: aria-label and the visible text disagree

terms.name: Labor illusion
terms.definition: Showing the work a system is doing, or stretching it, so the answer feels earned: the search that lists the sites it is checking instead of answering at once.

sources.title: Buell & Norton: The Labor Illusion, Management Science 57(9)
Harvard Business School: The Labor Illusion

terms.useWhen: a wait made visible so the result feels worked for

terms.name: Landmark
terms.definition: A named region role (banner, navigation, main, complementary, contentinfo, search) that lets assistive technology jump between the major parts of a page.
terms.useWhen: naming the big regions so they can be jumped between

terms.name: Language attribute
terms.definition: The declared language of a document or a passage inside it, which picks the voice, the pronunciation rules, and the hyphenation a reader gets.
terms.useWhen: a quoted passage is in another language than the page

terms.name: Large text threshold
terms.definition: The size at which text counts as large for contrast purposes (about 18pt, or 14pt when bold) and its required ratio drops from 4.5:1 to 3:1.
terms.useWhen: deciding which contrast number a heading owes

terms.name: Lasso selection
terms.definition: Selecting by dragging a boundary around items on a canvas, freehand or as a rectangle, so whatever the outline encloses becomes the selection when the drag ends.
terms.useWhen: dragging an outline around items to select them

terms.name: Lawn mower pattern
terms.definition: A scanning shape for tables where the eye runs across one row, drops down and runs back the other way, mowing the cells in alternating directions.

sources.title: The Lawn Mower Eyetracking Pattern for Scanning Comparison Tables, NN/g

terms.useWhen: laying out a comparison table for scanning

terms.name: Layer cake pattern
terms.definition: A scanning shape where the eye reads headings and subheadings and skips the text between them, so the fixation map looks like stacked layers.

sources.title: Text Scanning Patterns: Eyetracking Evidence, NN/g
F-Shaped Pattern of Reading on the Web, NN/g

terms.useWhen: predicting a skim that only reads headings

terms.name: Layout grid
terms.definition: The shared column, gutter and margin structure a team lays every screen against, so different people's pages line up with each other.

sources.title: Layout grid, U.S. Web Design System

terms.useWhen: the agreed skeleton every screen is built on

terms.name: Layout margins
terms.definition: The reserved space between a container's edge and its content, sized by the system so content never touches the edge of the screen.
terms.useWhen: the outer breathing room, set once by the system

terms.name: Layout shift
terms.definition: Content moving after it has already been painted, usually because something arriving late took space that was never reserved for it.
terms.useWhen: the page jumped and you lost your place

terms.name: Layout shifter
terms.definition: A responsive pattern where the arrangement genuinely differs per breakpoint rather than reflowing, so each size gets its own composition.
terms.useWhen: sizes get different layouts, not the same one reflowed

terms.name: Layout thrashing
terms.definition: Reading a geometric value after writing to the DOM in the same frame, forcing the browser to lay out synchronously over and over and stalling the animation that caused it.

sources.title: web.dev: avoid large, complex layouts and layout thrashing
Paul Irish: what forces layout / reflow

terms.useWhen: an animation stutters and the cause is the code, not the curve

terms.name: Lazy loading
terms.definition: Deferring the fetch of an image, list section, or module until it is about to be needed, usually when it approaches the viewport.
terms.useWhen: content is fetched only once it is nearly on screen

terms.name: Lazy registration
terms.definition: Letting someone use a product and accumulate state anonymously, and asking for an account only when that state needs to survive the session.
terms.useWhen: you can start using it before making an account

terms.name: Leaderboard
terms.definition: A ranked list of participants by some score, with the reader's own position pinned into view even when it falls outside the visible range.
terms.useWhen: a ranked table with your own row pinned into view

terms.name: Leading
terms.definition: The vertical distance from one baseline of type to the next, which sets how a paragraph holds together as a block.
terms.useWhen: the vertical space between lines of type

terms.name: Legibility
terms.definition: How easily one letter can be told apart from another, a property of the typeface's drawing rather than of how the text is set.
terms.useWhen: judging the typeface, not the setting

terms.name: Letterboxing
terms.definition: Filling the mismatch between content shape and frame shape with bars: above and below for letterbox, at the sides for pillarbox.
terms.useWhen: the bars that appear when ratios do not match

terms.name: Letterpress text
terms.definition: A text effect that fakes stamping into the surface, using a one pixel light shadow below the glyphs and a slightly darker fill above it.
terms.useWhen: type that looks pressed into the surface

terms.name: Ligature
terms.definition: A single glyph that replaces two or more letters whose shapes would otherwise collide, such as the f and i pair.
terms.useWhen: two letters collide and the font fuses them

terms.name: light-dark()
terms.definition: A CSS function that takes two colours and returns the one matching the page's current colour scheme, collapsing a theme's light and dark values into one declaration.
terms.useWhen: writing both theme values inline instead of in a media query

terms.name: Light dismiss
terms.definition: Closing a transient surface by clicking outside it or pressing Escape, without a dedicated close control being used.
terms.useWhen: clicking away is enough to close something

terms.name: Lightbox
terms.definition: An overlay that shows one image or video large over a dimmed page, with next and previous controls and a dismiss.
terms.useWhen: an image opened large over the dimmed page

terms.name: Lightness
terms.definition: How light or dark a colour reads, from black at one end to white at the other, held separately from its hue and its colourfulness.
terms.useWhen: stepping a colour lighter or darker without changing the hue

terms.name: Line clamp
terms.definition: Cutting a block of text off after a fixed number of lines, with an ellipsis at the end of the last one.
terms.useWhen: capping a card's description at three lines

terms.name: Line drawing animation
terms.definition: An SVG stroke that appears to draw itself by animating its dash offset along its own length, used for signatures, check marks and illustrated line art.

sources.title: CSS-Tricks: how SVG line animation works

terms.useWhen: a mark should look drawn rather than revealed

terms.name: Line focus
terms.definition: A reading aid that dims everything except one to five lines of text, so the eye has a single band to track and cannot skip or reread a line by accident.

sources.title: Microsoft Support: Use Immersive Reader in Microsoft Edge

terms.useWhen: long prose has to be readable line by line

terms.name: linear() easing
terms.definition: An easing written as a list of sampled stops rather than a curve, which lets CSS express springs and bounces that no cubic bezier can describe.

sources.title: Chrome for Developers: create complex animation curves with linear()
Smashing Magazine: the path to awesome CSS easing with linear()

terms.useWhen: a curve is not expressible as one bezier

terms.name: Lining figures
terms.definition: Numerals all drawn to cap height so they line up evenly with capitals and with each other.

sources.title: OpenType at Work: Figure Styles (Type Network)

terms.useWhen: numbers next to capitals or in interface chrome

terms.name: Link
terms.definition: A control that navigates somewhere, named for its destination, and carrying the browser affordances of a destination (open in new tab, copy address).

sources.title: ARIA Authoring Practices Guide: Link pattern

terms.useWhen: the control goes somewhere rather than doing something

terms.name: Link purpose
terms.definition: Whether a link's own text says where it goes, the reason a list of read more and click here links fails when read out of context.
terms.useWhen: judging link text pulled out of its sentence

terms.name: Liquid Glass
terms.definition: Apple's 2025 material where controls float as a translucent layer that refracts what is behind them and reshapes fluidly as content moves underneath.
terms.useWhen: controls are a glass layer that bends the content behind

terms.name: List
terms.definition: A vertical run of related items presented as a set, where the shared shape of every row is what tells a reader the rows belong together.
terms.useWhen: items are peers and the set matters more than any one row

terms.name: List detail
terms.definition: A browsable list paired with a pane showing the selected item in full, collapsing to one screen at a time when the window is narrow.
terms.useWhen: browse a list, read one item, keep both in view

terms.name: List virtualization
terms.definition: Rendering only the rows currently in view and a small buffer around them, while spacers preserve the scrollbar of the full list.
terms.useWhen: a huge list renders only the rows you can see

terms.name: Listbox
terms.definition: An always visible list of options you choose from with the keyboard or pointer, without a popup or a text field.
terms.useWhen: the options are on screen already, not behind a popup

terms.name: Live activity
terms.definition: A persistent, updating view of something in progress, shown in system places like a lock screen so a reader can follow it without opening the app.
terms.useWhen: a task in progress must be followed outside the app

terms.name: Live region
terms.definition: A container marked so assistive technology reads changes inside it without moving focus, used for messages that appear after an action.
terms.useWhen: something must be spoken without stealing focus

terms.name: Load more
terms.definition: A button at the end of a list that fetches and appends the next batch only when pressed, keeping the reader in control of how much arrives.

sources.title: NN/g: Alternatives to Pagination on Product-Listing Pages

terms.useWhen: the next batch waits behind a button instead of arriving on its own

terms.name: Local navigation
terms.definition: Links contextual to where the reader is, showing the siblings and children of the current page rather than the whole site.

sources.title: Local Navigation Is a Valuable Orientation and Wayfinding Aid, NN/g

terms.useWhen: nav that changes with the section you are in

terms.name: Logical properties
terms.definition: Layout properties named by flow direction (inline start, block end) rather than by screen edge, so a layout mirrors itself in other writing modes.
terms.useWhen: spacing that must flip for right to left text

terms.name: Logo cloud
terms.definition: A row or grid of customer logos used as social proof, usually flattened to one colour so no brand dominates.
terms.useWhen: proof by association, laid out as a strip of marks

terms.name: Long description
terms.definition: An extended text alternative for a chart, diagram, or map, linked or referenced because a short alt string cannot carry the content.
terms.useWhen: the image is data and one line will not do

terms.name: Long press
terms.definition: A press held in place for a moment before release, used to reveal secondary actions, enter a rearrange mode, or open a contextual menu.
terms.useWhen: holding a touch to reach the secondary action

terms.name: Long shadow
terms.definition: A flat era decoration where an icon casts a single hard shadow at 45 degrees that runs far past the shape before fading out.

sources.title: NN/g: Flat Design: Its Origins, Its Problems, and Why Flat 2.0 Is Better for Users

terms.useWhen: one hard 45 degree shadow running off the icon

terms.name: Look and pinch
terms.definition: Spatial input where the eyes choose the target and a finger pinch commits the action, so selection and activation come from different body parts.

sources.title: Apple Developer: Explore game input in visionOS

terms.useWhen: gaze selects, hand confirms, no cursor involved

terms.name: Lorem ipsum
terms.definition: Scrambled pseudo-Latin placeholder text used so a layout can be judged on its shape and texture before the real copy exists.
terms.useWhen: filling a layout before the copy is written

terms.name: Lottie
terms.definition: A JSON format for vector animations exported from design tools and played natively on the web and mobile, so complex motion ships without video.

sources.title: School of Motion: motion design dictionary

terms.useWhen: designed animation must ship as an asset, not as code

terms.name: Low poly
terms.definition: A 3D style that keeps the polygon count low enough to see, so surfaces read as faceted triangles under flat shading instead of smooth curves.

sources.title: Aesthetics of Design: Low Poly Aesthetic
Sessions College: What is the deal with low poly art?

terms.useWhen: deliberately faceted 3D art with visible triangles

terms.name: Magazine layout
terms.definition: An editorial composition with mixed column widths, one dominant lead story and smaller supporting items arranged around it.
terms.useWhen: an editorial page with one clear lead and ranked rest

terms.name: Magic link
terms.definition: Signing in by clicking a single-use link emailed on request, with no password, and a screen that waits and offers to resend while the mail arrives.
terms.useWhen: you sign in by clicking a link sent to your email

terms.name: Magic tap
terms.definition: A screen reader gesture that fires the one action a screen is most likely about, so the reader does not have to hunt for the control.

sources.title: Apple: Supporting Accessibility (View Controller Programming Guide)

terms.useWhen: a screen has one obvious action worth a shortcut

terms.name: Magnetic button
terms.definition: A control that leans toward the cursor as it approaches, translating a fraction of the distance to its centre so it reads as attracted rather than merely hovered.

sources.title: Init HTML: magnetic hover effect, cursor-attracted buttons

terms.useWhen: a hero control should feel alive before it is clicked

terms.name: Marching ants
terms.definition: The animated dashed outline that circles a selection, moving continuously so the boundary reads as active rather than drawn.

sources.title: Computer Hope: What is a marquee?

terms.useWhen: the crawling dashed border around a selection

terms.name: Marking menu
terms.definition: A radial menu that can be answered before it appears: waiting shows the menu, while a confident stroke in the item's direction selects it outright.

sources.title: Kurtenbach and Buxton: user learning and performance with marking menus

terms.useWhen: an expert stroke that skips showing the menu

terms.name: Marking pattern
terms.definition: A scanning shape where the eye holds one spot on the screen while content scrolls past underneath it, most common on phones.

sources.title: F-Shaped Pattern of Reading on the Web, NN/g

terms.useWhen: reasoning about where eyes rest while scrolling

terms.name: Marquee
terms.definition: Text or logos that scroll continuously across a strip, either as a decorative ticker or because a label is too long for its box.

sources.title: School of Motion: The Essential Motion Design Dictionary

terms.useWhen: content is wider than its box and must still be read

terms.name: Masonry
terms.definition: A column layout that packs items of unequal height by placing each one in the shortest column, so the rows never line up and the bottom edge stays ragged.
terms.useWhen: unequal heights packed into the shortest column

terms.name: Material 3 Expressive
terms.definition: Google's 2025 update to Material 3: springier motion, emphasized typography, updated dynamic colour themes, and responsive components that stretch to hug the display.

sources.title: Google blog: Material 3 Expressive redesign for Android and Wear OS

terms.useWhen: Material turned up: emphasized type, springy motion

terms.name: Material You
terms.definition: Google's personalization layer where the system derives an app's entire color scheme from the user's wallpaper, so every app shifts together.
terms.useWhen: the palette comes from the user's wallpaper

terms.name: Maximalism
terms.definition: A style that fills the screen on purpose with layered color, pattern, and type, treating abundance rather than restraint as the message.

sources.title: Envato: Minimalism vs. Maximalism: Battle of the Divisive Design Styles
Twine: Minimalism vs Maximalism: The Pros and Cons for Web Design

terms.useWhen: abundance is the point, not a failure of editing

terms.name: Measure
terms.definition: The width of a column of text, judged in characters per line, with roughly 45 to 75 treated as the comfortable range for reading.

sources.title: Choose a comfortable measure (Elements of Typographic Style Applied to the Web)

terms.useWhen: deciding how wide a paragraph is allowed to get

terms.name: Meatball menu
terms.definition: An overflow menu whose trigger is three horizontal dots, usually sitting at the end of a row or a card.
terms.useWhen: extra actions behind three dots lying sideways

terms.name: Media controls
terms.definition: The cluster of play, pause, skip, volume and fullscreen controls attached to a player, which usually hides itself while playing.
terms.useWhen: the control bar of a video or audio player

terms.name: Media object
terms.definition: The pairing of a fixed size image or avatar on one side with a heading and text that fills the rest, repeated everywhere in interfaces.

sources.title: The media object saves hundreds of lines of code, Nicole Sullivan
The Media Object, A Bunch of Ways, CSS-Tricks

terms.useWhen: avatar or thumbnail beside a block of text

terms.name: Mega menu
terms.definition: A large navigation panel that drops from a top level item and shows many links at once, grouped into columns with headings.
terms.useWhen: a nav panel too big to be a simple list

terms.name: Memphis design
terms.definition: The 1980s Memphis Group look of clashing pastels, squiggles, confetti dots, and terrazzo shapes scattered across a layout.
terms.useWhen: squiggles and confetti shapes on clashing pastels

terms.name: Mention autocomplete
terms.definition: Typing a trigger character inside a text field to open a filtered list of people or objects, inserting the chosen one as a linked token.
terms.useWhen: typing @ opens a list of people to insert

terms.name: Menu bar
terms.definition: A permanent horizontal row of menu titles (File, Edit, View) whose menus open on click and then follow the pointer along the row.

sources.title: ARIA Authoring Practices Guide: Menu and Menubar pattern

terms.useWhen: the desktop row of File, Edit, View menus

terms.name: Menu bar extra
terms.definition: A small application controlled item living in the system menu bar or tray, usually an icon that opens a compact panel of status and controls.
terms.useWhen: an app's icon living in the system bar or tray

terms.name: Menu button
terms.definition: A button whose only job is to open a menu, marked with aria-haspopup and usually drawn with a downward chevron.

sources.title: ARIA Authoring Practices Guide: Menu Button pattern

terms.useWhen: the button opens a list of commands, nothing more

terms.name: Mesh gradient
terms.definition: A soft multi-point blend built from colours placed on a grid and smoothed between them, giving the blurred, cloudlike backgrounds a linear gradient cannot.
terms.useWhen: a soft multi-point colour blend, not a straight ramp

terms.name: Meter
terms.definition: A gauge of a known quantity within a known range, such as disk used or password strength, where the level is a fact rather than a task.

sources.title: ARIA Authoring Practices Guide: Meter pattern

terms.useWhen: a level within a known range, not a task

terms.name: Metered paywall
terms.definition: A paywall that grants a fixed number of free items per period and counts down publicly, so the barrier arrives only after the reader is invested.
terms.useWhen: you get three free articles a month and a counter says so

terms.name: Metro
terms.definition: Microsoft's typography led design language of flat coloured tiles, large light headings, and motion used in place of chrome, shadow, and texture.
terms.useWhen: flat coloured tiles and oversized light headings

terms.name: Mica
terms.definition: Fluent's opaque app background material, subtly tinted with the user's desktop wallpaper colour and going neutral when the window loses focus.

sources.title: Microsoft Learn: Materials used in Windows apps

terms.useWhen: an opaque window background tinted by the wallpaper

terms.name: Microcopy
terms.definition: An interface's smallest strings: the verb on the button, the line under the field, the sentence when it fails. Short enough to be read every time.

sources.title: NN/g: The 3 I's of Microcopy, Inform, Influence, and Interact
NN/g: UX Copy Sizes, Long, Short, and Micro
NN/g: The 3 C's of Informational Microcopy
Kinneret Yifrah, Microcopy: The Complete Guide (2nd edition)

terms.useWhen: the words a control needs to be understood, not the prose around it

terms.name: Microinteraction
terms.definition: A small self-contained loop of trigger, rule, feedback, and result, such as a toggle that flips, buzzes, and settles into its new state.
terms.useWhen: one tiny complete interaction, trigger to feedback

terms.name: Microsurvey
terms.definition: A one or two question survey placed inside the product at the moment being asked about, answered in place rather than on a separate page.
terms.useWhen: a one-question survey inside the thing it asks about

terms.name: Mid-century modern
terms.definition: A 1950s and 60s style of muted mustard, teal, and burnt orange, tapered organic shapes, textured paper grounds, and friendly geometric sans type.

sources.title: Kittl: 60+ graphic design styles, names and descriptions

terms.useWhen: muted 50s palette with tapered organic shapes

terms.name: Middle click
terms.definition: A press of the scroll wheel button, conventionally used to open a link in a new tab, close a tab, or start autoscrolling.
terms.useWhen: the wheel press, not the left or right button

terms.name: Miller columns
terms.definition: A browsing layout of side-by-side columns where selecting an item in one column fills the next with its children, keeping the whole path visible.
terms.useWhen: browsing a deep hierarchy with the path kept visible

terms.name: Mini cart
terms.definition: A compact view of the basket opened from the cart icon, confirming what was just added and offering checkout without leaving the current page.
terms.useWhen: the small basket panel that opens from the cart icon

terms.name: Minimalism
terms.definition: A style that reduces an interface to one typeface, one accent color, and generous empty space, letting whitespace rather than ornament carry hierarchy.

sources.title: Zoviz: Minimalist vs Maximalist Web Design

terms.useWhen: hierarchy carried by space, not by decoration

terms.name: Minimap
terms.definition: A shrunken overview of a long document or canvas beside the scrollbar, with a box showing which part is currently on screen.
terms.useWhen: a zoomed out map of a long document or canvas

terms.name: Misdirection
terms.definition: Using contrast, size, and position to pull attention to the option the business prefers while the other option is present but visually demoted.
terms.useWhen: the choice you want is there but styled to be missed
