terms.useWhen: a parent box stands over a partly checked group

terms.name: Mobile first
terms.definition: Designing and writing the narrow layout first and adding rules as space is gained, so the small screen is the default rather than the fallback.
terms.useWhen: which end of the range you start designing from

terms.name: Mockup
terms.definition: A screen shown as it will look rather than as it will work: colour, type and real copy all settled, and nothing in it clickable.

sources.title: NN/g: UX Prototypes, Low Fidelity vs. High Fidelity
NN/g: Prototypes vs Wireframes in UX Projects

terms.useWhen: showing what a screen will look like before anything behind it exists

terms.name: Modal dialog
terms.definition: A window that opens over the page and takes control of it, so nothing behind can be used until the dialog is answered or dismissed.

sources.title: ARIA Authoring Practices Guide: Dialog (Modal) pattern
Nielsen Norman Group: Modal and nonmodal dialogs

terms.useWhen: a window that blocks the page until it is dealt with

terms.name: Modal presentation
terms.definition: The slide-up-over transition that puts a sheet or dialog in front of the current screen while what is behind recedes, the platform motion for entering a modal context.
terms.useWhen: a task takes over the screen and must be dismissible

terms.name: Model selector
terms.definition: The control in an assistant interface that picks which model answers, usually a menu carrying a short description of each option.
terms.useWhen: choosing which model answers the request

terms.name: Modifier key
terms.definition: A key held to change what another input means, so the same click or keystroke can copy instead of move, or add instead of replace.
terms.useWhen: a held key changes what the next input does

terms.name: Modular grid
terms.definition: A grid with both columns and rows, dividing the page into equal modules that content can span in either direction.
terms.useWhen: content that needs to span rows as well as columns

terms.name: Modular scale
terms.definition: A type scale generated by multiplying a base size by a fixed ratio, so every step is proportionally related to the one before it.

sources.title: What the Font are Vertical Rhythm and Modular Scale?

terms.useWhen: generating sizes from a ratio instead of picking them

terms.name: Momentum scrolling
terms.definition: Content that keeps moving after the finger lifts, decelerating as though it had mass, so one flick can travel a long way.

sources.title: MDN: Basic concepts of scroll snap

terms.useWhen: scrolling that coasts after the gesture ends

terms.name: Monochromatic palette
terms.definition: A scheme drawn from one hue at many lightness and saturation levels, so hierarchy comes from contrast alone rather than from colour difference.

sources.title: The Ultimate Color Glossary For UI Designers

terms.useWhen: one hue carrying the whole interface

terms.name: Monospace
terms.definition: A typeface in which every character occupies the same horizontal width, so characters stack into columns down the page.
terms.useWhen: code, terminals, or anything that must line up in columns

terms.name: Morph transition
terms.definition: A transition where a shape or icon is interpolated into a different shape rather than swapped, so the two states read as one object changing.
terms.useWhen: two states are the same object in different forms

terms.name: Morphing control
terms.definition: One control that changes what it says and does according to state, showing play when paused and pause when playing rather than offering both.

sources.title: GoodUI: Try multifunctional controls instead of more parts

terms.useWhen: one button that becomes the next action each time

terms.name: Mostly fluid
terms.definition: A responsive pattern where a multi column grid stretches with the viewport up to a maximum width, then centres, stacking only on the smallest screens.
terms.useWhen: one grid that just widens, then caps

terms.name: Motion actuation
terms.definition: Triggering a function by moving the device itself, such as shake to undo, which needs a plain control alternative and an off switch.
terms.useWhen: the gesture is a shake or tilt of the device

terms.name: Motion blur
terms.definition: Blurring an element along its direction of travel so fast movement reads as speed instead of teleporting, borrowed from film and rare but real in interfaces.

sources.title: School of Motion: motion design dictionary

terms.useWhen: something moves fast enough that a sharp frame looks wrong

terms.name: Motion path
terms.definition: A defined path an element travels along, with its distance and rotation along that path animated instead of its x and y positions.
terms.useWhen: an element should follow a specific route

terms.name: Motion token
terms.definition: A named duration or easing value published by a design system, so timings are chosen from a set rather than typed per component.

sources.title: Material Design 3: easing and duration tokens

terms.useWhen: timings should be system decisions, not per-component ones

terms.name: Mouse gesture
terms.definition: A command issued by the shape of a pointer stroke, usually with a button held, so a movement stands in for a menu choice.
terms.useWhen: a drawn stroke that means a command

terms.name: Multi column layout
terms.definition: An application shell with three or more vertical regions, typically navigation, a list, and a reading pane, as in a mail client.
terms.useWhen: three regions at once: navigate, list, read

terms.name: Multi select
terms.definition: A select that accepts several values at once, usually showing the chosen ones as removable tokens inside the field.
terms.useWhen: one field, several answers

terms.name: Multi-touch
terms.definition: Input from more than one simultaneous contact point, letting a surface distinguish two-finger scrolling, pinching, rotating and larger finger counts.
terms.useWhen: naming input that depends on more than one finger at once

terms.name: Multi-window mode
terms.definition: A windowing mode where two or more apps share one screen, side by side, stacked, or as freeform windows, so every app must survive being any size.
terms.useWhen: the app is only part of the screen

terms.name: Multimodal interface
terms.definition: An interface that accepts and answers in more than one channel at once, letting a person speak, type, touch, or point and pick whichever suits the moment.

sources.title: NN/g: Voice First, the future of interaction?
UXmatters: Voice first versus the multimodal user interfaces of the future

terms.useWhen: voice, touch, and screen share one interaction

terms.name: Nagging
terms.definition: Interrupting a task again and again with the same request, so that agreeing becomes the cheapest way to be left alone.
terms.useWhen: the same prompt keeps returning until you give in

terms.name: Name, role, value
terms.definition: The three things every control has to expose to assistive technology: what it is called, what kind of thing it is, and what state it is currently in.
terms.useWhen: auditing whether a custom control is really a control

terms.name: Named color
terms.definition: One of the CSS keywords such as tomato or rebeccapurple that map to fixed sRGB values, a fossil vocabulary still useful for prototypes and debugging.
terms.useWhen: the keyword colours built into CSS

terms.name: Named grid areas
terms.definition: Naming regions of a grid and drawing the layout as rows of those names, so items are placed by name instead of by line number.
terms.useWhen: placing items by name instead of by number

terms.name: Named instance
terms.definition: A specific point in a variable font's design space that the designer has given a style name, so it can be picked like an ordinary weight.
terms.useWhen: picking a named style out of a variable font

terms.name: Natural language interface
terms.definition: An interface whose input is ordinary language, typed or spoken: the user states an intent in their own words and the system parses it, instead of picking from controls.
terms.useWhen: the input is a sentence, not a selection

terms.name: Navigation bar
terms.definition: The horizontal strip of primary destinations across the top of a site, usually holding the logo, the main sections and an account control.

sources.title: ARIA Authoring Practices Guide: Landmark regions

terms.useWhen: the top strip of site level destinations

terms.name: Navigation menu
terms.definition: A menu of destinations rather than commands, where opening an item moves you somewhere instead of running an action.
terms.useWhen: a menu whose items are places, not commands

terms.name: Navigation rail
terms.definition: A narrow vertical strip of top level destinations at the side of a screen, used at medium widths where a bottom bar is wasteful and a drawer is too heavy.
terms.useWhen: top level navigation on a medium width window

terms.name: Neo-skeuomorphism
terms.definition: The current return of depth and material to interfaces, using restrained texture, shadow, and highlight instead of literal leather, metal, and felt.

sources.title: Userology: Flat design is dead, the rise of neo-skeuomorphism

terms.useWhen: depth is back, but abstracted rather than literal

terms.name: Neon glow
terms.definition: A saturated colour surrounded by layered soft shadows of the same hue, so type or a border reads as a lit tube against a dark surface.
terms.useWhen: type or borders that look lit rather than filled

terms.name: Nested interactive
terms.definition: A focusable control placed inside another control, such as a button inside a link or a checkbox inside a clickable row, which garbles the announcement and can leave the inner control unreachable.

aliases.name: interactive controls must not be nested

sources.title: Deque: Interactive controls must not be nested

terms.useWhen: a whole card is clickable and so is its button

terms.name: Neubrutalism
terms.definition: A loud style built from thick black outlines, saturated flat color, square corners, and hard offset shadows with zero blur.

sources.title: NN/g: Neobrutalism: Definition and Best Practices

terms.useWhen: black outline plus a hard unblurred shadow

terms.name: Neumorphism
terms.definition: A style where controls look extruded from or pressed into one background colour, shaped only by soft light and shadow.
terms.useWhen: controls extruded from one flat background colour

terms.name: Neutral palette
terms.definition: The greys an interface is mostly made of, ramped from page background to body text, which carry the structure while the accent carries the attention.
terms.useWhen: the greys that most of the interface is actually made of

terms.name: New Wave design
terms.definition: The postmodern break from Swiss order: stair-stepped rules, diagonal and letter-spaced type, weights mixed inside a word, and text reversed out of bars.

sources.title: Hue and Eye: New Wave graphic design explained

terms.useWhen: the Swiss grid kept but deliberately violated

terms.name: No results state
terms.definition: What a search or filtered list shows when nothing matched, naming the query, explaining why, and offering a way to loosen the constraints.
terms.useWhen: the screen shown when a search matches nothing

terms.name: Node graph
terms.definition: A canvas of boxes wired to each other by lines, where each box does one job and the wiring between them is the thing being built, rearranged by dragging.

sources.title: React Flow: node-based UIs in React

terms.useWhen: boxes wired by lines, where the wiring is the content

terms.name: Node port
terms.definition: The typed stub on a node where a wire may land, coloured or shaped by what it accepts, so a connection that would make no sense refuses to complete.
terms.useWhen: the stub on a node where a wire connects

terms.name: Non-breaking space
terms.definition: A space that renders normally but forbids a line break, gluing two words together so they never end up on separate lines.
terms.useWhen: keeping a number and its unit on one line

terms.name: Non-text contrast
terms.definition: The requirement that controls, focus indicators and meaningful graphics reach 3:1 against what is next to them, which is the rule that governs borders and icons.
terms.useWhen: contrast for controls and icons rather than text

terms.name: Notification center
terms.definition: A panel collecting notifications that were missed or kept, usually opened from a bell with an unread count.
terms.useWhen: the panel behind the bell icon

terms.name: Notification digest
terms.definition: Collecting many similar alerts into one summary rather than delivering each, so the count rises but the number of interruptions does not.
terms.useWhen: many alerts arrive as one grouped summary

terms.name: Nudge
terms.definition: Moving or changing a value by one small fixed step with an arrow key, with a modifier switching to a larger step.

sources.title: Figma Learn: Adjust alignment, rotation, position, and dimensions

terms.useWhen: moving something by exact steps with the keyboard

terms.name: Object fit
terms.definition: How a picture or video is resized inside a box whose shape it does not match: stretched to fill, letterboxed to fit whole, or cropped to cover every edge.
terms.useWhen: choosing between cropping and letterboxing

terms.name: Oblique
terms.definition: An upright typeface slanted to the right without redrawing its letters, which is why it lacks the cursive forms a true italic has.
terms.useWhen: distinguishing a slanted roman from a real italic

terms.name: Obstruction
terms.definition: Putting deliberate hurdles in front of an action the business does not want taken, so the effort itself does the discouraging.
terms.useWhen: the path exists but is made exhausting on purpose

terms.name: Off canvas
terms.definition: Keeping secondary regions parked outside the viewport and sliding them in on demand, instead of stacking them below the main content.
terms.useWhen: secondary panels parked off screen until called

terms.name: Offline indicator
terms.definition: A persistent notice that the product has lost its connection, saying what still works, what is queued, and when the last sync happened.
terms.useWhen: the bar telling you the app is working offline

terms.name: OKLCH
terms.definition: A colour notation of lightness, chroma and hue built on Oklab, where changing the hue leaves the perceived lightness alone and equal steps look equal.
terms.useWhen: writing colour so that equal numeric steps look equal

terms.name: Oldstyle figures
terms.definition: Numerals with varying heights, some rising and some dropping below the baseline, so numbers blend into lowercase running text.

sources.title: OpenType at Work: Figure Styles (Type Network)

terms.useWhen: numbers inside a sentence, not in a table

terms.name: On-color
terms.definition: A colour defined by what it sits on, such as on-primary or on-surface, so every fill ships with the foreground guaranteed to be readable against it.

implementations.name: On primary, On surface, On error

terms.useWhen: the foreground colour that ships paired with a fill

terms.name: Onboarding checklist
terms.definition: A persistent list of setup tasks with completion state and a progress meter, kept available so the reader can return to unfinished steps.

sources.title: GOV.UK Design System: Complete multiple tasks

terms.useWhen: a setup list you can leave and come back to

terms.name: Onboarding tour
terms.definition: A short sequence of pointers layered over a live interface, each naming one control, advanced by the reader and skippable at any point.
terms.useWhen: a stepped overlay walks you around a live screen

terms.name: One thing per page
terms.definition: Asking a single question on each screen of a form so the reader never chooses which field to answer first and errors point somewhere unambiguous.
terms.useWhen: each form screen asks exactly one question

terms.name: One-time code login
terms.definition: Signing in by typing a short code sent to a second channel, keeping the reader inside the app rather than sending them out to a mail client.
terms.useWhen: you type a six digit code sent by mail or text

terms.name: Opacity
terms.definition: How much of what is behind an element shows through it, applied to the whole element and its children at once rather than to a single colour value.
terms.useWhen: fading an entire element and everything inside it

terms.name: OpenType features
terms.definition: Optional glyph substitutions and spacing rules packed inside a font file, addressed by four-letter tags and switched on from CSS.
terms.useWhen: reaching for a font capability that is off by default

terms.name: Operational transparency
terms.definition: Showing the work as it happens, the kitchen made visible, so a wait is understood rather than merely endured and the result is trusted more for having been watched.

sources.title: Buell & Norton: The Labor Illusion, Management Science 57(9)

terms.useWhen: letting the reader watch the work happen

terms.name: Optical alignment
terms.definition: Nudging an element off its measured position so it looks aligned, correcting for shapes whose bounding box lies about their visual centre.
terms.useWhen: it measures right but still looks wrong

terms.name: Optical kerning
terms.definition: Letting software space letter pairs by looking at their shapes, instead of using the pair values the type designer built into the font.
terms.useWhen: a font's own spacing is unreliable at display size

terms.name: Optical size
terms.definition: A font adjusting its own drawing for the size it is set at, thickening strokes and opening spacing for small text and refining both for large.

implementations.name: SF Pro Text and SF Pro Display

terms.useWhen: type that should be redrawn, not just scaled

terms.name: Optimistic UI
terms.definition: Showing the result of an action immediately and reconciling with the server afterward, instead of making the user wait for confirmation.
terms.useWhen: showing the result before the server confirms it

terms.name: Orbit
terms.definition: Rotating a camera around a fixed point by dragging, so the scene appears to turn while the subject stays centred.

sources.title: Apple Developer: Explore game input in visionOS

terms.useWhen: dragging to turn a 3D view around its subject

terms.name: Orbit animation
terms.definition: One element circling another on a continuous path, used for logo constellations and loading states where the revolving is the ornament.
terms.useWhen: elements should revolve around a fixed centre

terms.name: Order summary
terms.definition: The persistent panel beside a checkout listing items, quantities, and every cost line, kept visible so nothing about the total arrives as a surprise.
terms.useWhen: the panel beside checkout that itemises what you will pay

terms.name: Orientation lock
terms.definition: Restricting a screen to portrait or landscape, which strands anyone whose device is fixed in a mount or a wheelchair arm in the orientation the design refused.

sources.title: Understanding Success Criterion 1.3.4: Orientation, W3C WAI

terms.useWhen: a layout only works one way up

terms.name: Origin-aware animation
terms.definition: Scaling or fading a panel out of the control that opened it by putting its transform origin on that anchor, so the panel reads as belonging to its trigger.
terms.useWhen: a menu should look like it came from its button

terms.name: Ornament
terms.definition: A small panel of controls that floats just outside a window edge in visionOS, staying with the window without covering its contents.

sources.title: Creating Ornaments in visionOS, Create with Swift

terms.useWhen: controls must stay reachable without eating the content

terms.name: Orphan
terms.definition: A first line of a paragraph left alone at the bottom of a column or page, with the rest of the paragraph carried over.
terms.useWhen: naming a first line left behind at the bottom of a column

terms.name: Outline color
terms.definition: The role that draws boundaries, split into a stronger value for edges that must be seen and a weaker one for dividers that only need to hint at structure.

implementations.name: Steps 6 to 8, borders and focus rings

terms.useWhen: the colour of borders and dividers as a named role

terms.name: Overflow menu
terms.definition: A menu holding the actions that do not fit in the visible interface, opened from one compact trigger.
terms.useWhen: the actions that did not fit, behind one trigger

terms.name: Overloaded command
terms.definition: One command word or icon wired to different outcomes depending on where it sits, so having used it once teaches the reader nothing about the next one.
terms.useWhen: the same label doing different jobs in different places

terms.name: Overscan safe area
terms.definition: The inset a television layout keeps clear of the screen edge, about five percent, because sets crop the outer frame and anything near it disappears.

sources.title: Layouts in the Leanback UI toolkit, Android Developers

terms.useWhen: laying out for a screen that crops its own edges

terms.name: Overscroll
terms.definition: Scrolling input that continues after a scroller has reached its limit, which platforms answer with a bounce, a glow, or a handoff to the parent.
terms.useWhen: input keeps scrolling past the end of the content

terms.name: Overshoot
terms.definition: The part of a motion that carries past its final value before coming back, the visual signature of an underdamped spring or a back easing curve.
terms.useWhen: motion should read as having weight and momentum

terms.name: Oversized typography
terms.definition: Type set far past reading size so the words carry the layout, the headline doing the work a photograph would otherwise be hired for.

sources.title: Matej Latin: how to use huge type on the web

terms.useWhen: type so large the words are the layout

terms.name: Overview plus detail
terms.definition: A layout that shows a compressed overview and a detailed view at the same time in separate regions, so the reader keeps their place while inspecting one part.

sources.title: A Review of Overview+Detail, Zooming, and Focus+Context Interfaces, Cockburn, Karlson and Bederson

terms.useWhen: a map or minimap kept beside the detail

terms.name: Owned element
terms.definition: A child the accessibility tree is told to adopt from elsewhere in the DOM, used when the nesting a role requires is impossible in the markup.
terms.useWhen: a listbox and its options cannot be nested in markup

terms.name: Page break
terms.definition: Where content is cut to continue in the next fragment, a printed page, a column or a region, plus the rules that decide where the cut may fall.
terms.useWhen: controlling where printed or column content splits

terms.name: Page curl
terms.definition: A page turn that lifts and bends the leaf away from the spine as the finger drags it, the most literal transition a reader can be given.

sources.title: MacRumors: re-enable the classic page turning animation in Apple Books
Creating a page curl transition in SwiftUI

terms.useWhen: turning a page should read as paper rather than as a slide

terms.name: Page header
terms.definition: The band at the top of a screen carrying the page title, its context, and the actions that apply to the page as a whole.
terms.useWhen: the title band that owns the page's own actions

terms.name: Page indicator
terms.definition: The row of small dots under a carousel or onboarding screen showing how many pages there are and which one you are on.

sources.title: Page controls, Apple Human Interface Guidelines

terms.useWhen: the dots under a swipeable set of screens

terms.name: Page title
terms.definition: The document title, the first thing a screen reader speaks and the only label a reader has when picking between tabs, windows, and history entries.
terms.useWhen: the label a page carries outside its own viewport

terms.name: Page transition
terms.definition: Motion that covers a navigation between two whole pages or routes, replacing the hard cut a document load would otherwise produce.
terms.useWhen: navigation between routes should feel continuous

terms.name: Pagination
terms.definition: The numbered row of page links under a long result set, with previous and next controls and usually an ellipsis where numbers are skipped.
terms.useWhen: results split into numbered pages

terms.name: Pan
terms.definition: Moving the viewport across content in any direction while keeping contact, so the content feels anchored to the finger or cursor.
terms.useWhen: moving the view over content rather than the content itself

terms.name: Pancake stack
terms.definition: A three row page where the header and footer take only the height they need and the middle row absorbs every remaining pixel, even when the content is short.
terms.useWhen: header, body, footer with the body taking the slack

terms.name: Pane
terms.definition: A layout container that holds one destination's content inside a window, either fixed or flexible in width, combined with other panes to fill the space.
terms.useWhen: naming one region of a multi region window

terms.name: Pangram
terms.definition: A sentence that uses every letter of the alphabet at least once, used to show a whole character set in one line.
terms.useWhen: you need one line that shows every letter

terms.name: Parallax
terms.definition: Moving layers at different rates against the same input, so the slower layers read as farther away and the scene gains depth.
terms.useWhen: depth should come from relative speed, not shadow

terms.name: Parenting
terms.definition: Tying one element's motion to another's so moving or scaling the parent carries the child with it, which is how a group of parts reads as one object instead of several.

sources.title: UX Magazine: creating usability with motion, the UX in Motion Manifesto
Issara Willenskomer: the UX in Motion Manifesto

terms.useWhen: several elements must move as one because one of them leads

terms.name: Particle background
terms.definition: An ambient decorative background of many small moving agents: drifting dots, linked constellations, flocks, or starfields animating behind the page content.

sources.title: particles.js: a lightweight library for particles
Craig Reynolds: Boids, background and update

terms.useWhen: the backdrop is alive with drifting points

terms.name: Passkey
terms.definition: Signing in with a device-held credential unlocked by the reader's own biometric or screen lock, so the interface asks for a face or fingerprint, not a secret.
terms.useWhen: signing in with a fingerprint instead of a password

terms.name: Password reveal toggle
terms.definition: The control inside a password field, usually an eye or the word Show, that switches the characters between masked and readable.
terms.useWhen: naming the eye icon inside a password box

terms.name: Password strength meter
terms.definition: A gauge that scores a password while it is typed and names what would improve it, replacing a list of rules with continuous feedback.
terms.useWhen: the bar that rates a password as you type it

terms.name: Pause, stop, hide
terms.definition: A visible control for content that moves, blinks, scrolls, or updates on its own, so a reader can stop it before reading around it.
terms.useWhen: something animates or refreshes without being asked

terms.name: Paywall
terms.definition: A barrier that stops access to content or a feature until the reader pays, placed either before anything is shown or partway into the content.
terms.useWhen: the point where content stops until you pay

terms.name: Perceptual duration
terms.definition: How long a spring appears to take, measured to the point the movement stops being visible rather than to its mathematical rest, the figure to quote against a timed animation.
terms.useWhen: a spring must be compared with a duration

terms.name: Perceptual uniformity
terms.definition: The property of a colour space where equal numeric distances look like equal visual differences, which is what makes a generated ramp step evenly.
terms.useWhen: explaining why an HSL ramp looks uneven and an OKLCH one does not

terms.name: Permission priming
terms.definition: Explaining why access is needed in the product's own dialog first, and only firing the operating system prompt once the reader has said yes to that.

sources.title: web.dev: Permission UX for push notifications

terms.useWhen: your own dialog asks before the real system prompt does

terms.name: Petite caps
terms.definition: Capitals drawn to exactly x-height, shorter than small caps, so they sit flush with the lowercase around them.
terms.useWhen: you need caps that match x-height exactly

terms.name: Picture in picture
terms.definition: A small always on top window that keeps video or navigation visible in a corner while the reader works in another app or scrolls another page.
terms.useWhen: keeping video visible while doing something else

terms.name: Pilcrow
terms.definition: The paragraph mark, a reversed P with a doubled stem, used to show where a paragraph begins or as a hover anchor beside a heading.
terms.useWhen: naming the paragraph symbol in an editor

terms.name: PIN input
terms.definition: A row of single character boxes for a short code, where typing advances to the next box and pasting the whole code fills them all.
terms.useWhen: entering a short code one character per box

terms.name: Pinch to zoom
terms.definition: Two fingers moving apart or together on a surface to scale content up or down, with the scale tracking the distance between them.

sources.title: Material Design: Gestures (pinch open and closed)

terms.useWhen: two fingers changing the scale of what is on screen

terms.name: Pixel art UI
terms.definition: An interface drawn on a visible pixel grid, with bitmap type, hard aliased edges, and icons kept at their original low resolution.

sources.title: Sage: Retro Web Design: When Pixel Art Belongs on Your Site

terms.useWhen: the pixels are meant to be visible

terms.name: Pixel density
terms.definition: How many physical pixels a display packs into an inch, and the reason a CSS pixel is a unit of measure rather than a dot on the screen.
terms.useWhen: raster crispness, 2x assets, or dpi/ppi confusion is on the table

terms.name: Placeholder as label
terms.definition: The antipattern of using placeholder text as a field's only label, which vanishes on typing and usually fails both contrast and naming.
terms.useWhen: naming why a placeholder-only field is broken

terms.name: Plain language
terms.definition: Writing interface copy at the reading level of the people using it, with short sentences, familiar words, and the point first, rather than at the level of the org chart.

sources.title: Understanding Success Criterion 3.1.5: Reading Level, W3C WAI

terms.useWhen: the copy is correct but nobody can act on it

terms.name: Playhead
terms.definition: The marker showing the current position in a timeline or track, which travels during playback and can be dragged to move it.

sources.title: UX Patterns for Developers: pattern index

terms.useWhen: the marker showing where playback is

terms.name: Point size
terms.definition: The nominal size of type, measured in points, which describes the body the letters are drawn on rather than the height of any letter.
terms.useWhen: explaining why 16pt in two fonts looks different

terms.name: Pointer cancellation
terms.definition: Activating a control on pointer release rather than press, so someone who lands on the wrong target can slide off and abort.
terms.useWhen: letting a mis-press be taken back before release

terms.name: Pointer capture
terms.definition: Redirecting all events for one pointer to a chosen element, so a drag keeps reaching the control it started on even when it wanders off.
terms.useWhen: a drag must keep its grip after leaving the element

terms.name: Pointer gestures
terms.definition: Path based or multi finger gestures such as pinch, swipe, and drag along a track, which need a single pointer equivalent to stay operable.
terms.useWhen: a pinch or swipe is the only way in

terms.name: Pointer lock
terms.definition: Hiding the cursor and reading only its movement deltas, so input keeps flowing past the edges of the screen instead of stopping at them.
terms.useWhen: input is relative movement, not a screen position

terms.name: Politeness level
terms.definition: The urgency setting on a live region: polite waits for a pause in speech, assertive interrupts whatever is being read.
terms.useWhen: choosing whether an update may interrupt speech

terms.name: Pop art style
terms.definition: A comic and advertising style of flat primary color, heavy black outlines, printed dot shading, speech balloons, and bold condensed capitals.

sources.title: Kittl: 60+ graphic design styles, names and descriptions
Inkbot Design: 20 iconic graphic design styles

terms.useWhen: comic outlines, flat primaries, and printed dots

terms.name: Pop in
terms.definition: An entrance that scales slightly past full size before settling, so the element arrives with a small snap instead of simply being there.
terms.useWhen: an arriving element should feel eager rather than merely present

terms.name: Popconfirm
terms.definition: A small confirmation bubble anchored to the control you just pressed, asking whether you meant it without opening a dialog over the page.
terms.useWhen: confirming in place instead of in a dialog

terms.name: Popover
terms.definition: A small surface anchored to the control that opened it, holding content or controls of its own, and dismissed by clicking away or pressing Escape.
terms.useWhen: a small anchored surface with controls inside it

terms.name: Popover arrow
terms.definition: The small triangle joining a popover or tooltip to the thing it belongs to, which flips and slides as the popover repositions.
terms.useWhen: the little triangle pointing at the trigger

terms.name: Positive tabindex
terms.definition: Using tabindex values above zero to force an order, which yanks those elements to the front of the whole page sequence and is almost always a bug.
terms.useWhen: someone proposes tabindex="1" to fix an order

terms.name: POUR
terms.definition: The four principles WCAG is built on, perceivable, operable, understandable, and robust, used as a shorthand for sorting an accessibility problem into a bucket.
terms.useWhen: classifying what kind of barrier you are looking at

terms.name: Predictive back
terms.definition: A back gesture that reveals the destination underneath while the finger is still down, so the swipe can be finished or abandoned once the reader has seen where it goes.
terms.useWhen: a back swipe should show its destination before it commits

terms.name: Increased contrast
terms.definition: A user preference for more contrast than a theme's default, honoured by strengthening borders, text, and state colours rather than by shifting hues.

sources.title: MDN: Using media queries for accessibility

terms.useWhen: the system asks for a higher contrast version

terms.name: Reduced motion
terms.definition: A user preference asking interfaces to cut non-essential animation, honoured by shortening, cross fading, or removing movement rather than by doing nothing.
terms.useWhen: the reader has asked the system for less movement

terms.name: Preselected opt-in
terms.definition: Arriving at a choice with the answer that benefits the business already ticked, so consent is collected from everyone who does not notice.
terms.useWhen: the marketing box is already ticked when you get there

terms.name: Presence indicator
terms.definition: The small coloured dot on an avatar reporting whether a person is available, away, busy or offline.
terms.useWhen: the green dot on someone's picture

terms.name: Presentation role
terms.definition: Stripping an element of its semantics while leaving it on screen, so a table used for layout or a list used for spacing stops being announced as one.

sources.title: W3C: Using ARIA, rules of ARIA use

terms.useWhen: markup you needed for layout is lying about meaning

terms.name: Presentational children
terms.definition: The rule that some roles flatten everything inside them into their own label, which is why an icon and a span inside a button are never announced separately.
terms.useWhen: markup inside a control vanishes from the a11y tree

terms.name: Press-drag-release
terms.definition: Operating a menu in one gesture: pressing the trigger opens it, dragging moves through the items while the button stays down, and releasing over an item commits it.

aliases.name: press to open, release to select

terms.useWhen: a menu that answers one continuous press as well as two clicks

terms.name: Pressed state
terms.definition: The look a control takes while it is actually being held down, confirming that the press was received before the action runs.
terms.useWhen: the moment a control is under the finger

terms.name: Pressure sensitivity
terms.definition: Reading how hard a pen or finger presses, plus tilt and twist, so stroke weight and behaviour vary with the shape of the contact.
terms.useWhen: how hard or how tilted the input is matters

terms.name: Preview text
terms.definition: The line an inbox prints under a subject, written as hidden text at the top of the mail so the client shows those words instead of scraping whatever body copy comes first.

sources.title: Litmus: The Ultimate Guide to Email Preview Text

terms.useWhen: the line the inbox shows after the subject

terms.name: Prime mark
terms.definition: The slanted tick used for feet, inches, minutes, and seconds, which is a different character from either a straight quote or a curly one.
terms.useWhen: writing feet and inches, not quoting anyone

terms.name: Primitive color token
terms.definition: A raw palette value named for what it is, like blue-500, sitting under the semantic layer that names colours for what they do.

sources.title: Color token naming: primitive, semantic and component layers

terms.useWhen: the raw palette value beneath a semantic name

terms.name: Print stylesheet
terms.definition: The rules that decide what a page becomes on paper: navigation dropped, link targets spelled out, backgrounds abandoned, and the content given page margins.
terms.useWhen: what a page becomes when it is printed

terms.name: Priority plus navigation
terms.definition: A horizontal menu that keeps as many items visible as fit and moves the rest into a More control, recalculating whenever the available width changes.
terms.useWhen: the nav shows what fits and hides the rest behind More

terms.name: Privacy zuckering
terms.definition: Steering people into sharing more about themselves than they meant to, by making the permissive choice the easy one and the private choice several clicks deep.

sources.title: Deceptive Design: types of deceptive pattern

terms.useWhen: the settings are arranged so sharing is the easy answer

terms.name: Progress bar
terms.definition: A filling bar reporting how far along a task is, determinate when the end is known and indeterminate when it is not.

sources.title: ARIA Authoring Practices Guide: Communicating Value and Limits for Range Widgets
Nielsen Norman Group: Progress Indicators Make a Slow System Less Insufferable

terms.useWhen: showing how far through a task you are

terms.name: Progress ring
terms.definition: A circular progress indicator that fills around a ring, often with the percentage in the middle.
terms.useWhen: progress drawn as a filling circle

terms.name: Progressive blur
terms.definition: A blur whose strength ramps across a region instead of applying evenly, so content fades into softness toward an edge rather than stopping at a hard line.

sources.title: Devs Love Coffee: Making Apple progressive blur on the web

terms.useWhen: content should dissolve into blur, not meet an edge

terms.name: Progressive disclosure
terms.definition: Showing the few options most people need and keeping the rest one deliberate step away, so complexity arrives only when it is asked for.
terms.useWhen: keeping advanced options one click away instead of on screen

terms.name: Progressive image loading
terms.definition: Showing a cheap stand-in for an image, a blur, a dominant colour, or a low resolution copy, and swapping in the full file once it arrives.
terms.useWhen: a blurred or coloured block stands in until the photo loads

terms.name: Progressive profiling
terms.definition: Collecting profile details a few at a time across separate visits, instead of demanding the whole record in one long form at registration.
terms.useWhen: the product asks for one more detail each time you return

terms.name: Progressive reduction
terms.definition: Simplifying a control as the same person uses it more, dropping the label once the icon has been learned and restoring it after a long absence.
terms.useWhen: the label falls away once you have used it enough

terms.name: Prompt input
terms.definition: The composer at the bottom of an assistant interface: a growing text area with attachment, model and send controls attached to it.
terms.useWhen: the box you type an assistant request into

terms.name: Pronunciation
terms.definition: How a synthetic voice says a word, and the hints an author can give when the default reading turns a product name, a units string, or a homograph into nonsense.
terms.useWhen: the screen reader mangles a name or a number

terms.name: Property filter
terms.definition: A search field that builds structured queries from tokens, letting a reader filter by named properties with operators rather than free text.
terms.useWhen: filtering by named fields inside one search box

terms.name: Prototype
terms.definition: A design wired up just enough to be tried: screens linked so that a tap goes somewhere, with nothing real behind the links.

sources.title: NN/g: UX Prototypes, Low Fidelity vs. High Fidelity
Figma Help Center: Prototyping in Figma

terms.useWhen: putting a flow in someone's hands before it is built

terms.name: Proximity
terms.definition: The grouping principle that elements placed close together read as related, which is why spacing decides perceived structure more reliably than borders do.

sources.title: Proximity Principle in Visual Design, NN/g

terms.useWhen: arguing that spacing, not lines, makes groups

terms.name: Psychedelic style
terms.definition: A 1960s poster style of vibrating complementary color, warped and interlocking lettering that fills its own shape, kaleidoscopic symmetry, and liquid distortion.

sources.title: Kittl: 60+ graphic design styles, names and descriptions

terms.useWhen: vibrating color and lettering warped to fill a shape

terms.name: Pull quote
terms.definition: A phrase lifted out of an article and set large as a graphic element, to draw a browsing reader into the text.

sources.title: How to Attract Attention With Pull Quotes (CreativePro)

terms.useWhen: advertising a line of the article to a scanner

terms.name: Pull to refresh
terms.definition: Dragging a list downward past its top edge to trigger a reload, with an indicator that appears in the space the drag opens up.
terms.useWhen: tugging a list down to fetch new items

terms.name: Pulse
terms.definition: A slow repeating change in scale or opacity that keeps an element alive without moving it, used for waiting states and gentle attention.

sources.title: WCAG 2.2 Understanding SC 2.2.2: Pause, Stop, Hide

terms.useWhen: an element must signal life while nothing else happens

terms.name: Push notification
terms.definition: A system delivered message shown outside the app, on a lock screen or in a notification list, that has to earn the interruption it costs.
terms.useWhen: something needs saying while the app is closed

terms.name: Push transition
terms.definition: A navigation transition where the new view slides in and pushes the old one off, and reversing it pops back, encoding depth in a stack.
terms.useWhen: navigating deeper into a stack and back out

terms.name: QR code
terms.definition: A square matrix barcode rendered in the interface to hand a link or credential to a phone camera.
terms.useWhen: handing a link to a phone by camera

terms.name: Quasimode
terms.definition: A temporary mode held open by the user, such as a key kept down, so it cannot be forgotten and ends the moment the hold ends.
terms.useWhen: a mode that lasts only while you hold it

terms.name: Quick return header
terms.definition: A header that slides out of the way while the reader scrolls down and returns immediately on the first upward scroll, without waiting for the top of the page.

sources.title: Bram.us: hide a header when scrolling down, show it again when scrolling up

terms.useWhen: the bar hides going down and comes back the moment you scroll up

terms.name: Quick settings tile
terms.definition: A one tap button or toggle an app contributes to the system control surface, so one feature can be reached without opening the app.

sources.title: Android: Create custom Quick Settings tiles

terms.useWhen: one app feature deserves a place in system controls

terms.name: Quick view
terms.definition: Opening a summary of an item over the list it came from, so the reader can inspect it and return without losing scroll position or filters.
terms.useWhen: peeking at an item without leaving the list

terms.name: Radial menu
terms.definition: A menu whose items sit around the point of invocation, so a choice is made by direction and distance rather than by reading a list.
terms.useWhen: a menu chosen by direction from where you pressed

terms.name: Radio group
terms.definition: A set of mutually exclusive options, each with its own label and control, exactly one of which can be chosen.
terms.useWhen: one of several, each option labelled and visible

terms.name: Rag
terms.definition: The uneven edge left by unjustified text, and the thing typographers tune so that edge makes no distracting shapes down the side of a paragraph.
terms.useWhen: critiquing the uneven edge of a paragraph

terms.name: Rage click
terms.definition: A burst of repeated clicks on one spot, the shape frustration takes when a control answers nothing, and the analytics signal that goes looking for it.

sources.title: Smashing Magazine: Accessible Target Sizes Cheatsheet

terms.useWhen: the repeated clicking that reports a dead control

terms.name: Raised cap
terms.definition: An oversized opening letter that sits on the first line's baseline and rises above the text, rather than sinking into it.
terms.useWhen: the big opening letter rises instead of sinking

terms.name: RAM technique
terms.definition: A grid that decides its own column count from a minimum item width, so the same one line rule works at every screen size without a single breakpoint.

sources.title: RAM (Repeat, Auto, Minmax), web.dev layout patterns

terms.useWhen: a grid that reflows with no breakpoints at all

terms.name: Range select
terms.definition: Choosing a contiguous run of items by marking one end and holding Shift while marking the other, selecting everything between them.

sources.title: ARIA APG: Developing a keyboard interface

terms.useWhen: selecting everything between two items at once

terms.name: Range slider
terms.definition: A slider with two handles on one track that sets a lower and an upper bound, so the selection is an interval rather than a point.
terms.useWhen: the reader picks a from and a to on one track

terms.name: Rating
terms.definition: A row of stars or similar marks that both shows a score and, when interactive, takes one.

sources.title: Rating indicators, Apple Human Interface Guidelines

terms.useWhen: a score expressed as filled marks out of five

terms.name: Rating prompt
terms.definition: An in-product request to rate or review, usually timed to a moment of success and often filtered so only positive responses reach the public store.
terms.useWhen: the app asks how you like it right after something went well

terms.name: Reaction picker
terms.definition: A small row of emoji that appears on hover or long press so a message can be answered without a reply.
terms.useWhen: answering a message with one emoji

terms.name: Read aloud
terms.definition: Speaking a page's own prose with a synthetic voice, highlighting each word as it is spoken. A reading aid for people who can see the screen, not a screen reader.

sources.title: Microsoft Support: Use Immersive Reader in Microsoft Edge

terms.useWhen: distinguishing text to speech from a screen reader

terms.name: Read receipt
terms.definition: A per-message marker reporting how far a message got, sent, delivered, or read, drawn as ticks, labels, or the recipient's avatar.
terms.useWhen: the ticks that say sent, delivered, and read

terms.name: Readability
terms.definition: How comfortably a body of text can be read at length, a property of the setting: size, measure, leading, and contrast.
terms.useWhen: judging the setting, not the typeface

terms.name: Reader mode
terms.definition: A browser view that throws away your layout and rebuilds the article as plain text the reader can restyle, which is a verdict on how readable the original was.

sources.title: Use Immersive Reader in Microsoft Edge, Microsoft Support
mozilla/readability, the library behind Firefox Reader View

terms.useWhen: checking what survives when the design is stripped

terms.name: Reading flow
terms.definition: A CSS property that repoints reading and tab order at the visual arrangement of a flex or grid container, instead of leaving both stuck in source order.
terms.useWhen: a visual reorder has left tab order zigzagging

terms.name: Reading order
terms.definition: The order content is exposed in the DOM, which drives both speech output and tab order, and which visual reordering can silently contradict.
terms.useWhen: the visual order and the source order disagree

terms.name: Reading progress
terms.definition: A bar tied to scroll position that shows how much of an article remains, usually pinned to the top edge and filling as the reader descends.
terms.useWhen: the thin bar showing how far through the article you are

terms.name: Recurring event
terms.definition: An event stored once as a rule instead of as copies, so every second Tuesday can be edited, skipped for one week, or ended, without touching the rest.
terms.useWhen: one event that repeats by a rule

terms.name: Reduced transparency
terms.definition: A user preference asking for opaque surfaces instead of blur and translucency, honoured by swapping frosted layers for solid fills.

sources.title: MDN: Using media queries for accessibility

terms.useWhen: frosted panels have to become solid on request

terms.name: Redundant entry
terms.definition: The rule against asking for the same information twice in one process, unless it is re-entered for a real reason such as confirmation.
terms.useWhen: a wizard asks for the address a second time

terms.name: Reference line
terms.definition: A line drawn at a meaningful value across a chart: a target, a threshold, an average, a before-and-after moment.
terms.useWhen: a chart needs a benchmark the eye can compare marks against

terms.name: Reflow
terms.definition: The requirement that content works in one column at 320 CSS pixels wide without two dimensional scrolling, which is 400 percent zoom on a desktop.
terms.useWhen: checking a layout at heavy zoom, not just on phones

terms.name: Relative color syntax
terms.definition: CSS notation that builds a new colour from an existing one by naming an origin colour with from and then adjusting individual channels.
terms.useWhen: deriving a colour by editing one channel of another

terms.name: Relative luminance
terms.definition: The brightness of a colour measured on a 0 to 1 scale after each channel is linearised, which is the input every WCAG contrast calculation actually uses.
terms.useWhen: explaining why two colours of equal saturation contrast differently

terms.name: Relative timestamp
terms.definition: A time printed as a distance from now, two hours ago or in three days, updating itself and holding the exact time in its tooltip.
terms.useWhen: printing a time as how long ago it was

terms.name: Required field indicator
terms.definition: How a form says a field cannot be left empty, in the label text, in the announced name, and not by an asterisk whose meaning is explained somewhere else.
terms.useWhen: deciding how to mark required versus optional fields

terms.name: Resize handle
terms.definition: The small corner grip that lets you drag an element or window bigger and smaller, drawn as diagonal ridges on a textarea or window corner.
terms.useWhen: the corner grip that resizes a box

terms.name: Resize text
terms.definition: Text must scale to at least 200 percent without loss of content or function, which rules out fixed pixel heights around wrapping copy.
terms.useWhen: the reader has enlarged text, not the whole page

terms.name: Responsive upscaling
terms.definition: Designing what a layout does with the space it gains on very wide screens, rather than only what it drops as screens narrow.

sources.title: Responsive Upscaling: 11 Ideas for Large-Screen E-Commerce Design, Baymard

terms.useWhen: the layout has more room than it knows what to do with

terms.name: Responsive web design
terms.definition: One layout that adapts to any screen through fluid grids, flexible images and media queries, rather than a separate site built for each class of device.

sources.title: Responsive Web Design, A List Apart

terms.useWhen: the umbrella term for one adapting layout

terms.name: Retro film aesthetic
terms.definition: A treatment that makes digital imagery look shot on film, adding grain, halation, light leaks, faded contrast, dust, and sometimes a corner date stamp.
terms.useWhen: photography faked to look developed rather than rendered

terms.name: Retro-futurism
terms.definition: A style that pictures the future the way an earlier decade pictured it, so the technology shown is advanced but the type, color, and hardware belong to the past.
terms.useWhen: a future imagined by an older decade, not by this one

terms.name: Retro web design
terms.definition: A style that rebuilds the early desktop web on purpose: beveled window chrome, pixel and system type, garish color, and animated banners.

sources.title: Superdesign: Retro Web Design: CSS Recipe, Live Examples and Trend Data
Setproduct: Retro and brutalist UI design, a field guide

terms.useWhen: the page imitates a 90s desktop or an early website

terms.name: Reveal animation
terms.definition: Motion that uncovers content already in place, usually by growing a clip or mask outward from a point rather than moving the content itself.

sources.title: Android: reveal or hide a view using animation

terms.useWhen: content should be uncovered rather than moved in

terms.name: Review cursor
terms.definition: A second cursor a screen reader user can move over the screen to read text without moving the system focus, so inspecting a region does not disturb the app.
terms.useWhen: a reader inspects content without leaving the field

terms.name: Ribbon
terms.definition: A tall tabbed toolbar that replaces menus, grouping commands into labelled sections with the important ones drawn larger.

sources.title: Nielsen Norman Group: User interface elements glossary

terms.useWhen: the tall tabbed command strip in Office style apps

terms.name: Rich text editor
terms.definition: An editing surface that shows formatting as it will appear rather than as markup, so what the writer sees is close to what readers get.

sources.title: The Component Gallery: Rich text editor

terms.useWhen: authors need formatting without learning a markup language

terms.name: Rich text toolbar
terms.definition: The strip of formatting controls above or beside an editor, whose buttons report their state from wherever the caret sits.

sources.title: ARIA Authoring Practices Guide: Toolbar pattern

terms.useWhen: the formatting strip over a text editor

terms.name: Ripple
terms.definition: A circular wash that spreads from the point of contact to acknowledge a touch, Material's way of tying feedback to where the finger landed.
terms.useWhen: touch feedback that spreads from the contact point

terms.name: Risograph style
terms.definition: A print-inspired look of two or three flat spot colors that misregister slightly and show grain, imitating a riso duplicator.
terms.useWhen: flat spot colors that overprint and slip out of register

terms.name: River
terms.definition: An accidental channel of white space running down a paragraph where word spaces on consecutive lines happen to line up.
terms.useWhen: naming the white streak running down a paragraph

terms.name: Roach motel
terms.definition: Making entry into a commitment take one click and exit take a phone call, a chat queue, or a buried page, so the asymmetry keeps people subscribed.
terms.useWhen: easy to sign up, deliberately hard to leave

terms.name: Role description
terms.definition: An author supplied name for a widget's role, spoken in place of the stock role name, which overrides the platform wording and misleads easily.
terms.useWhen: renaming what a widget calls itself out loud

terms.name: Rotate gesture
terms.definition: Two fingers turning around a common center to rotate the object or view beneath them, the angle tracking the fingers as they orbit.
terms.useWhen: turning content with two fingers rather than a handle

terms.name: Rotor
terms.definition: VoiceOver's dial for choosing what a swipe or flick moves between: headings, links, landmarks, form controls, or characters.

sources.title: Use the VoiceOver rotor on Mac, Apple Support
VoiceOver gestures on iOS, Deque University

terms.useWhen: naming the VoiceOver dial that picks a navigation unit

terms.name: Route announcement
terms.definition: Telling assistive technology that a client side navigation happened, by moving focus to the new heading or posting the new title to a live region.

sources.title: Dave Rupert: Accessible page navigations in single page apps

terms.useWhen: the URL changed but the page never reloaded

terms.name: Roving tabindex
terms.definition: A focus technique where only one item in a group is in the tab order and arrow keys move that position, so Tab enters and leaves the whole group once.

sources.title: ARIA APG: Developing a keyboard interface

terms.useWhen: a group of controls that Tab treats as one stop

terms.name: RTL mirroring
terms.definition: Flipping a layout horizontally for right to left languages, moving navigation and progression to the other side while leaving some elements unmirrored.
terms.useWhen: shipping the same screen in Arabic or Hebrew

terms.name: Ruby annotation
terms.definition: Small guide text set beside or above a run of base text, most often to give the pronunciation of East Asian characters.
terms.useWhen: annotating characters with their pronunciation

terms.name: Rule builder
terms.definition: Assembling a condition from dropdowns and values, joined by and or or, so a non-programmer can express a query without writing one.
terms.useWhen: building an if-this-then-that condition from dropdowns

terms.name: Rule of thirds
terms.definition: Dividing a frame into nine equal cells with two lines each way and placing the important elements on the lines or their intersections.
terms.useWhen: placing a focal point off centre on purpose

terms.name: Runt
terms.definition: A single word left alone on the last line of a paragraph or heading.

sources.title: An end to typographic widows on the web (Clagnut)

terms.useWhen: naming the lone word on a heading's last line

terms.name: Safe area
terms.definition: The part of the screen guaranteed clear of notches, system bars and rounded corners, where interactive content can safely sit.

sources.title: Using safe-area-inset to build mobile-safe layouts, Polypane

terms.useWhen: the region a control can occupy without being clipped

terms.name: Sans-serif
terms.definition: A typeface drawn without finishing strokes on the ends of its stems, which is the default register of most interface type.
terms.useWhen: naming type without finishing strokes

terms.name: Saturation
terms.definition: How far a colour is from grey on a scale where 100 percent is the pure hue and 0 percent is neutral, as modelled by HSL and its relatives.
terms.useWhen: describing how vivid or washed out a colour looks

terms.name: Save for later
terms.definition: Moving an item out of the active list into a parked list that stays associated with the reader, without deleting it or committing to it.
terms.useWhen: parking an item without buying or discarding it

terms.name: Scaffold
terms.definition: The frame that positions an app's persistent regions, its bars, panes and body, so each screen drops content into named slots instead of inventing its own arrangement.
terms.useWhen: the named slots a screen's parts drop into

terms.name: Scanlines
terms.definition: Thin repeating dark lines laid over an interface to imitate the raster of a cathode ray tube screen, often with a slight curve and flicker.
terms.useWhen: the screen is dressed as an old CRT monitor

terms.name: Scarcity indicator
terms.definition: A label reporting how little of something is left, in stock, in seats, or in time, placed beside the action it is meant to accelerate.
terms.useWhen: only two left in stock, printed next to the buy button

terms.name: Scheduler
terms.definition: A grid of days crossed with hours where each event is a block in its own slot, so a week's free time is visible and an event is moved by dragging it.
terms.useWhen: hours down, days across, events as blocks in the grid

terms.name: Scope bar
terms.definition: The row of category buttons directly under a search field that narrows what the query searches, such as All, Mail, Files.

sources.title: Apple Human Interface Guidelines: Search fields

terms.useWhen: buttons under a search box that limit its reach

terms.name: Screen curtain
terms.definition: A screen reader mode that switches the display off entirely while navigation keeps working, used for privacy and by sighted testers checking an audio-only run.

sources.title: Apple Support: Use Screen Curtain with VoiceOver

terms.useWhen: testing whether a flow works with the screen dark

terms.name: Screen magnification
terms.definition: Blowing part of the screen up many times over, so a reader sees a keyhole of the layout at a time and anything far from the action is effectively off screen.
terms.useWhen: a toast at the corner will never be seen

terms.name: Screen reader
terms.definition: Software that speaks or brailles the accessibility tree and supplies its own keyboard commands for moving through a page.
terms.useWhen: naming the software that reads an interface aloud

terms.name: Scrim
terms.definition: A translucent or gradient layer laid over imagery or behind a dialog, dimming what is beneath so text on top clears contrast or so focus moves forward.
terms.useWhen: darkening what is behind so the layer above stays readable

terms.name: Scroll anchoring
terms.definition: Keeping the reader's position fixed when content loads or resizes above it, by adjusting scroll offset so the visible text does not jump.
terms.useWhen: content loads above and the view must not jump

terms.name: Scroll chaining
terms.definition: When an inner scroller reaches its end and the gesture continues, the scroll passes to the page behind it unless that handoff is blocked.
terms.useWhen: an inner scroll spills over into the page behind

terms.name: Scroll container
terms.definition: The element that actually scrolls its overflowing content, distinct from the page, and the box the browser calls the scrollport.
terms.useWhen: identifying which box is doing the scrolling

terms.name: Scroll edge fade
terms.definition: A gradient mask at the edge of a scroll container that fades clipped content out, hinting that more lies past the edge without drawing a control.

sources.title: Lea Verou: Pure CSS scrolling shadows with background-attachment local

terms.useWhen: showing a list continues past its clipped edge

terms.name: Scroll hijacking
terms.definition: Overriding the browser's scrolling so a wheel turn advances a scripted sequence instead of moving the page by the distance the reader asked for.
terms.useWhen: the page takes over what one scroll of the wheel does

terms.name: Scroll-linked animation
terms.definition: An animation whose progress is bound to scroll position rather than to time, so scrolling back rewinds it exactly.
terms.useWhen: the reader's scroll should drive the animation frame by frame

terms.name: Scroll lock
terms.definition: Freezing the page behind an open overlay so a wheel or swipe moves the overlay's own content and never the document underneath.
terms.useWhen: the page must hold still while an overlay is open

terms.name: Scroll pinning
terms.definition: Holding a section fixed in place while the page keeps scrolling, spending scroll distance on an animation instead of on movement.
terms.useWhen: a section should hold still while its content advances

terms.name: Scroll snap
terms.definition: Snap positions declared on a scroll container so scrolling settles on a chosen item edge instead of stopping wherever momentum runs out.
terms.useWhen: scrolling that must land on an item, not between two

terms.name: Scroll spy
terms.definition: Navigation that watches the scroll position and highlights the entry for the section currently in view.
terms.useWhen: navigation that highlights the section you are reading

terms.name: Scroll-triggered animation
terms.definition: An animation that scroll position only starts, after which it runs on its own clock and does not rewind when the reader scrolls back up.

sources.title: Chrome for Developers: CSS scroll-triggered animations are coming

terms.useWhen: scrolling should start the motion, not steer it

terms.name: Scrollbar
terms.definition: The bar beside a scrollable region whose thumb shows both how much content there is and where in it you are.
terms.useWhen: the bar that shows and sets scroll position

terms.name: Scrollbar color
terms.definition: The thumb and track colours of a scrollbar, which a page can set explicitly or leave to the declared colour scheme so the browser draws its own dark variant.
terms.useWhen: matching the scrollbar to a dark or branded theme

terms.name: Scrollytelling
terms.definition: A narrative layout where a pinned graphic stays fixed while text scrolls past it, each step changing what the graphic shows.
terms.useWhen: one visual that changes as the story scrolls past

terms.name: Scrubber
terms.definition: The seek control of a media player: a track showing elapsed and buffered time with a playhead you drag to move through it.
terms.useWhen: the bar you drag to move through a video

terms.name: Scrubbing
terms.definition: Dragging a playhead along a timeline to move through media by hand, previewing frames as the position changes rather than waiting for playback.
terms.useWhen: dragging through time to find a moment

terms.name: Scrubby slider
terms.definition: A numeric field whose label can be dragged sideways to change the value, giving a slider's feel without a slider taking up room.

sources.title: John Nack on Adobe: Scrubby sliders and more

terms.useWhen: dragging a label to change the number beside it

terms.name: Search field
terms.definition: A text input specialised for queries, with a magnifier, a clear control and often suggestions that appear as you type.

sources.title: Nielsen Norman Group: Search: Visible and Simple

terms.useWhen: the input is for searching, not for data entry

terms.definition: The alternate pointer press, usually the right button or a two-finger tap, reserved for opening contextual actions rather than activating.

terms.name: Seed color
terms.definition: The single input colour an algorithm expands into a whole scheme, so a palette becomes something derived from one decision rather than picked swatch by swatch.

terms.useWhen: one colour in, a whole palette out

terms.name: Segmented control
terms.definition: A single control holding two to five mutually exclusive options side by side, with the current one shown as a filled segment.
terms.useWhen: two to five exclusive options, all visible at once

terms.name: Select
terms.definition: A closed control that shows the current choice and opens a list of options when pressed, with no typing.

terms.name: Select all across pages
terms.definition: Offering to extend a selection from the visible page to every matching row, after a header checkbox has selected only what is on screen.
terms.useWhen: select all offers to also take the rows you cannot see

terms.name: Selection card
terms.definition: A radio or checkbox dressed as a card, where the whole tile is the target and the control itself is small or absent.

terms.definition: The highlight painted behind text a reader has selected, which a page can restyle and thereby break the contrast the operating system had guaranteed.
terms.useWhen: styling the highlight behind selected text

terms.name: Selection follows focus
terms.definition: A widget where moving focus also selects, so arrowing through tabs or a listbox changes the selection immediately rather than on a second press.

terms.useWhen: arrowing changes the choice, not just the highlight

terms.name: Selection handle
terms.definition: The draggable grip at each end of a touch text selection, used to widen or narrow the range a finger cannot adjust precisely.

sources.title: iOS HIG: Gestures (touch and hold in text)

terms.useWhen: adjusting a touch selection by its endpoints

terms.name: Semantic color
terms.definition: A colour named for the job it does rather than the colour it is, so that "danger" or "surface" can be repointed without renaming anything that uses it.

sources.title: Carbon Design System: color token usage

terms.useWhen: naming the colour after its job instead of its hue

terms.name: Semantic HTML
terms.definition: Reaching for the element that already means what you mean, so name, role, keyboard behaviour, and platform conventions arrive for free instead of being rebuilt.
terms.useWhen: choosing between a native element and a rebuilt one

terms.name: Semantic zoom
terms.definition: Switching between two views of the same content, a zoomed out view of group headings and a zoomed in view of individual items, instead of scaling pixels.
terms.useWhen: zooming out to headings, not to smaller text

terms.name: Sender name
terms.definition: The name a mail appears to come from, chosen rather than inherited, because a reader scanning an inbox decides on it before reading a word of the subject.

sources.title: Litmus: The Anatomy of a Good Email

terms.useWhen: the name a mail appears to come from

terms.name: Sentence case
terms.definition: Capitalising only the first word of a label or heading, plus any proper nouns, as you would in an ordinary sentence.

terms.name: Sequential palette
terms.definition: A data palette that runs light to dark in one direction, encoding an ordered quantity so that darker always means more.
terms.useWhen: colour encoding an ordered quantity

terms.name: Serif
terms.definition: The small finishing stroke at the end of a letter's stem, and by extension the class of typefaces that have them.
terms.useWhen: naming the little feet on the ends of strokes

terms.name: Set size and position
terms.definition: Telling assistive technology how big a list really is and where an item sits in it, so a windowed or paginated list still announces "item 6 of 16".
terms.useWhen: only twenty rows of ten thousand are in the DOM

terms.name: Shade
terms.definition: A colour with black mixed in, darker than the original hue and typically used for pressed states, borders and dark theme surfaces.
terms.useWhen: a darker version of a colour made by adding black

terms.name: Shake
terms.definition: A short lateral wobble used to reject an input, borrowed from the head shake and read as no rather than as an error message.

sources.title: School of Motion: motion design dictionary

terms.useWhen: an input is refused and should be felt, not just read

terms.name: Shake to undo
terms.definition: Physically shaking a device to trigger undo or redo, an accelerometer gesture Apple defines system wide for reversing a recent edit.
terms.useWhen: undo triggered by motion rather than a control

terms.name: Share sheet
terms.definition: The system panel of destinations and actions for sending the current item elsewhere, populated by whatever apps are installed.
terms.useWhen: the system panel for sending something onward

terms.name: Shared axis
terms.definition: Material's transition where outgoing and incoming views slide and fade along the same x, y, or z axis, so direction encodes the navigational relationship.
terms.useWhen: two views sit next to each other in a sequence or hierarchy

terms.name: Shimmer
terms.definition: The moving highlight that sweeps across placeholder shapes to signal that content is still on its way.

sources.title: WCAG 2.2 Understanding SC 2.2.2: Pause, Stop, Hide

terms.useWhen: the highlight travelling across a placeholder

terms.name: Show more toggle
terms.definition: The control at the end of clamped text that expands it to full length and, when honest, collapses it again.

sources.title: Expandable text, UX Patterns for Developers

terms.useWhen: expanding text that was cut off after n lines

terms.name: Sidebar
terms.definition: A persistent vertical region alongside the main content holding navigation or secondary controls, often collapsible on narrow screens.

terms.name: Sidenote

terms.name: Sign language interpretation

terms.name: Signature pad
terms.definition: A drawing area that captures a handwritten signature by pointer or touch, with a clear control and a baseline to sign on.
terms.useWhen: capturing a handwritten signature

terms.name: Signed distance field
terms.definition: A texture storing each pixel's distance to a shape's edge rather than its color, so glyphs and icons rendered from it stay crisp at any scale on the GPU.

terms.useWhen: text or icons must scale sharply inside a GPU pipeline

terms.name: Signifier
terms.definition: The visible cue that advertises an affordance, such as a grip texture, an underline, or a shadow that says this can be pressed.

terms.name: Site footer
terms.definition: The closing region of a site holding secondary navigation, legal links, and contact details that do not deserve top level placement.
terms.useWhen: everything that must exist but must not compete

terms.name: Situational disability
terms.definition: A barrier that comes from the moment rather than the body, one arm holding a baby, sunlight on a screen, a noisy train, and that makes the audience for access everyone.
terms.useWhen: widening who a barrier actually affects

terms.name: 60-30-10 rule
terms.definition: A proportion guideline that gives about 60 percent of a layout to a dominant colour, 30 percent to a secondary, and 10 percent to an accent.
terms.useWhen: deciding how much of each colour to use, not which colours

terms.name: Skeleton screen
terms.definition: A loading state made of grey shapes standing where the content will be, showing the layout before the data arrives.

sources.title: Luke Wroblewski: Mobile design details, avoid the spinner

terms.useWhen: showing the shape of content while it loads

terms.name: Skeuomorphism
terms.definition: A style that makes interface elements imitate real objects and materials, using leather, metal, paper, and glossy highlights so their purpose reads as familiar.

sources.title: NN/g: Flat Design: Its Origins, Its Problems, and Why Flat 2.0 Is Better for Users

terms.useWhen: the control is dressed as the physical object it replaces

terms.name: Skip link
terms.definition: A link at the very start of a page, revealed on focus, that jumps past repeated navigation to the main content.
terms.useWhen: the first-tab link past the navigation

terms.name: Slash command
terms.definition: Typing a forward slash in a composer to open a menu of actions, where choosing one runs it rather than inserting the words into the message.
terms.useWhen: typing / in the message box opens a command menu

terms.name: Slide to confirm
terms.definition: A control that commits only once its thumb is dragged the length of its track, so the effort of the gesture is the guard against doing it by accident.
terms.useWhen: making one irreversible action need a deliberate drag

terms.name: Slide transition
terms.definition: A transition where content translates in or out along one axis, using direction to say whether the user moved forward, back, up, or down.
terms.useWhen: the change has a direction the reader should feel

terms.name: Slider
terms.definition: A control that sets a value by dragging a handle along a track, showing the whole range at once.

sources.title: ARIA Authoring Practices Guide: Slider pattern

terms.useWhen: picking a value where the range matters more than the number

terms.name: Sliding indicator
terms.definition: A single underline or pill that travels between tabs to mark the selection instead of each tab drawing its own, so the move itself says which way the selection went.

sources.title: CSS-Tricks: creating an animated menu indicator with CSS selectors

terms.useWhen: selection should move between items rather than blink between them

terms.name: Small caps
terms.definition: Capital letters drawn at roughly lowercase height, with weight adjusted to match, so an abbreviation does not shout inside running text.
terms.useWhen: setting acronyms inside body text without shouting

terms.name: Small multiples

terms.useWhen: one chart would need too many series to stay readable

terms.name: Smart app banner
terms.definition: A strip pinned to the top of a mobile web page urging the reader to open or install the native app instead, with an install or open action.
