Google Search Central: Avoid intrusive interstitials and dialogs

terms.useWhen: the strip on a mobile site pushing you into the app

terms.name: Smart defaults
terms.definition: Prefilling a choice with the answer most people in this situation want, so the common case needs no work and every other case is still reachable.

sources.title: GoodUI: Try Smart Defaults instead of asking to do extra work

terms.useWhen: the form arrives already answered the way you would have

terms.name: Smart guides
terms.definition: Alignment lines that appear only while dragging, showing which edges or centers the moving object currently lines up with.
terms.useWhen: the guide lines that appear mid-drag

terms.name: Smart quotes
terms.definition: The curved opening and closing quotation marks a typeface actually draws, as opposed to the straight vertical marks inherited from typewriters.

sources.title: The Definitive Guide to Quotes, Apostrophes, and Primes

terms.useWhen: your quotes look like typewriter ticks

terms.name: Smooth scrolling
terms.definition: Animating a programmatic jump so the page travels to its destination instead of cutting there, which keeps an anchor link or a back-to-top button from losing the reader's place.
terms.useWhen: a jump would leave the reader unsure where they landed

terms.name: Snapping
terms.definition: Pulling a dragged object into exact alignment once it comes within a small distance of a grid, guide, or another object's edge.
terms.useWhen: a drag jumps into alignment near a guide

terms.name: Sneak into basket

terms.useWhen: something you never picked is in your basket

terms.name: Social login
terms.definition: Signing in by delegating identity to an existing account elsewhere, presented as a row of provider buttons above or instead of a password form.
terms.useWhen: the row of continue with Google and Apple buttons

terms.name: Social proof
terms.definition: Showing what other people did or said next to a decision, as counts, reviews, logos, or live activity, so the reader can borrow their judgement.

sources.title: GoodUI: Try Social Proof instead of talking about yourself

terms.useWhen: the interface shows what others chose to steady your choice

terms.name: Soft delete
terms.definition: Removing an item from view but keeping it recoverable in a trash or archive for a period, so deletion is reversible without a confirmation step.
terms.useWhen: deleted things go to a bin you can dig them out of

terms.name: Soft hyphen
terms.definition: An invisible character placed inside a word that marks where a hyphen may appear if the word has to break, and stays hidden otherwise.
terms.useWhen: telling the browser where a long word may break

terms.name: Solarpunk
terms.definition: An optimistic ecological future style of daylight palettes, plant growth over structure, stained glass colour, art nouveau curves, and visible solar and wind technology.
terms.useWhen: a hopeful green future rather than a dystopian one

terms.name: Sonification
terms.definition: Turning data into sound, mapping a series to pitch or rhythm, so a chart can be heard as a shape rather than described one value at a time.

sources.title: University of Washington: Making data visualizations accessible

terms.useWhen: a chart has to be perceivable without sight

terms.name: Sort indicator
terms.definition: The small arrow in a column header showing that the table is sorted by that column and in which direction.
terms.useWhen: the arrow in a header showing the sort

terms.definition: The announced direction of the one column a table is currently sorted by, carried on that column header alone rather than on every sortable header.
terms.useWhen: a sorted column shows an arrow but says nothing

terms.name: Spacer
terms.definition: A deliberate empty element between regions: the gap between two panes that carries the drag handle when they resize, or the flexible filler that pushes toolbar items apart.
terms.useWhen: the empty element that does the spacing

terms.name: Spacing scale
terms.definition: The fixed, named set of spacing values a system allows, so gaps come from a shortlist instead of being invented per screen.
terms.useWhen: why the gap is 12 and not 13

terms.name: Spanned layout
terms.definition: How an app arranges itself when one window is stretched across two displays, either keeping content clear of the seam or splitting the layout exactly at it.

sources.title: Surface Duo device modes, Microsoft Learn

terms.useWhen: one app stretched across two screens

terms.name: Sparkline
terms.definition: A tiny chart with no axes or labels, drawn inline at text size to show the shape of a trend beside the number it belongs to.
terms.useWhen: a trend line small enough to sit inline

terms.name: Spatial navigation
terms.definition: Moving focus by direction rather than by sequence, so arrow keys, a D-pad, or a TV remote jump to the nearest control up, down, left, or right.

terms.name: Spatial UI
terms.definition: Interface designed to sit in three dimensional space, where panels are made of a system glass material and hierarchy is carried by depth rather than by colour.

sources.title: WWDC23: Design for spatial user interfaces
Create with Swift: Ensuring interface legibility and contrast in visionOS

terms.useWhen: the interface floats in the room, not on a screen

terms.name: Specular highlight
terms.definition: The bright reflection drawn on a surface to say it is glossy, placed where a light source would strike a curved object.
terms.useWhen: the bright spot that makes a surface read as shiny

terms.name: Speculative loading
terms.definition: Fetching, or fully rendering, a page before the reader asks for it, on a guess about where they go next, so the navigation is already done when the click lands.
terms.useWhen: the next page is fetched before the reader clicks it

terms.name: Speed dial
terms.definition: A floating action button that fans out into three to six smaller related actions when pressed or hovered.
terms.useWhen: one prominent button that unfolds into a few actions

terms.name: Spinner
terms.definition: An indeterminate loading indicator that shows work is happening without saying how much of it is left.
terms.useWhen: work is happening and nobody knows for how long

terms.name: Split button
terms.definition: A two part control where the main area runs a default action and an attached arrow opens a menu of related alternatives.
terms.useWhen: one obvious action plus a menu of its variants

terms.name: Split-flap animation
terms.definition: A digit or letter changing by flipping through every character between the old value and the new one, imitating the mechanical boards of airports and flip clocks.

terms.useWhen: a changing value should read as mechanical rather than digital

terms.name: Split screen layout
terms.definition: A page cut into two equal full height halves, each carrying its own message or path, with no hierarchy between them.
terms.useWhen: two equally weighted choices on one page

terms.name: Split view
terms.definition: A layout of two or more side by side panes where a choice in the leading pane decides what the trailing pane shows.
terms.useWhen: two panes where one drives the other

terms.name: Splitter
terms.definition: The draggable bar between two panes that changes how much room each one gets, keyboard operable as a slider between limits.
terms.useWhen: the draggable bar between two resizable panes

terms.name: Spotlight hover
terms.definition: A soft radial glow centred on the pointer's position inside a card, lighting its surface and border as the cursor moves and going dark when the cursor leaves.

sources.title: Frontend Masters: how to build a glowing hover effect that follows the pointer
Cruip: how to create a spotlight card hover effect with Tailwind CSS

terms.useWhen: a card should light up under the pointer rather than change colour

terms.name: Spotted pattern
terms.definition: A scanning shape where the eye jumps to isolated words scattered down the page, hunting a keyword, a link or a number rather than reading anything.

sources.title: Text Scanning Patterns: Eyetracking Evidence, NN/g

terms.useWhen: predicting a keyword hunt rather than reading

terms.name: Spring animation
terms.definition: Motion driven by a simulated spring (mass, stiffness, damping) instead of a fixed duration, so the element settles rather than stopping on a schedule.

sources.title: Spring Animations in Pure CSS with linear()
Chrome for Developers: the linear() easing function

terms.useWhen: motion should react to how it was interrupted, not a timer

terms.name: Spring loading
terms.definition: Hovering a dragged item over a container until it opens, so a drag can travel through nested destinations without being dropped and restarted.

sources.title: MacPaw: What is spring loading on Mac

terms.useWhen: a drag opens what it hovers so it can go deeper

terms.name: Squash and stretch
terms.definition: Deforming an element along its direction of travel so it reads as having mass and flexibility, usually as a press squash or a launch stretch.

sources.title: Interaction Design Foundation: UI Animation, How to Apply Disney's 12 Principles of Animation to UI Design

terms.useWhen: a control should feel physical when pressed or launched

terms.name: Squircle
terms.definition: A rounded square whose corners curve continuously into the sides instead of meeting a circular arc, the shape behind iOS app icons.
terms.useWhen: corners that blend in rather than snap to an arc

terms.name: sRGB
terms.definition: The default colour space of the web, the one hex codes and plain rgb() values live in, and the baseline every wider gamut is described relative to.
terms.useWhen: the assumed colour space behind a hex code

terms.name: Stack
terms.definition: A layout primitive that puts one consistent gap between every child in a vertical run, so spacing lives with the parent instead of each item.
terms.useWhen: one rule for the space between everything vertical

terms.name: Stacking cards
terms.definition: A run of sections that each stick at the top of the viewport as the next one slides over it, so scrolling deals the page like a deck rather than passing it by.

sources.title: CSS-Tricks: stacked cards with sticky positioning

terms.useWhen: sequential sections should pile up instead of scrolling away

terms.name: Stacking context
terms.definition: A self contained depth ordering created by certain properties, inside which z-index only competes locally and can never escape to the level above.
terms.useWhen: why a huge z-index still sits behind something

terms.name: Stagger
terms.definition: Playing the same animation on a set of elements with a small delay added item by item, so the group arrives as a cascade instead of a block.
terms.useWhen: the same entrance played one item after another

terms.name: Stat
terms.definition: A single number shown large with a label and often a change indicator, the unit a dashboard is built from.
terms.useWhen: one number shown big with its label

terms.name: State layer
terms.definition: A translucent sheet of the content colour laid over a control at a fixed opacity per state, so hover, focus and pressed are one rule instead of three palettes.
terms.useWhen: one overlay opacity expressing hover, focus and pressed

terms.name: Static color
terms.definition: A colour deliberately excluded from theming because it sits on something that never changes, such as a label over a photo or a fixed brand mark.

terms.name: Status bar

terms.useWhen: an edge strip that reports rather than commands

terms.name: Status color
terms.definition: The small fixed set of colours a product reserves for outcome, typically success, warning, danger and info, so meaning is consistent wherever it appears.
terms.useWhen: colours that report an outcome rather than a brand

terms.name: Status message
terms.definition: A change in content that reports progress, result, or state and must be announced without taking focus, such as a count of search results.
terms.useWhen: reporting an outcome the reader did not navigate to

terms.name: Steampunk
terms.definition: A Victorian industrial style of brass, riveted plate, wood, and leather, with gauges, cogs, and valve controls standing in for ordinary interface widgets.

sources.title: Kittl: 60+ graphic design styles, names and descriptions
My Steampunk Style: What is retro-futurism?

terms.useWhen: brass gauges and cogs instead of plain controls

terms.name: Step indicator
terms.definition: A row or column of numbered stages showing where you are in a multi step flow and what remains.
terms.useWhen: showing progress through a numbered flow

terms.name: Stepped animation
terms.definition: Motion that jumps between a fixed number of discrete positions instead of interpolating, the mechanic behind sprite sheets, ticking clock hands and segmented spinners.
terms.useWhen: the movement should tick rather than glide

terms.name: Stepper
terms.definition: A small two part control with minus and plus that nudges a number up or down one step at a time.

sources.title: ARIA Authoring Practices Guide: Spinbutton pattern

terms.useWhen: adjusting a number by small known increments

terms.name: Steps left
terms.definition: Telling the reader where they are in a multi step task and how many steps are still to come, so the end of the task is visible from the start.
terms.useWhen: the flow says step 2 of 5

terms.name: Sticky add to cart

terms.useWhen: the buy bar that sticks once the real button scrolls off

terms.name: Sticky footer

terms.useWhen: a footer that will not float in the middle of a short page

terms.name: Sticky header

terms.useWhen: a header that pins itself once it hits the top

terms.name: Sticky hover
terms.definition: A hover style that stays applied on a touch device after a tap, because there is no pointer to leave and clear the state.
terms.useWhen: a tapped control stays looking hovered

terms.name: Sticky sidebar
terms.definition: A side column that scrolls with the page and then holds in place once its top reaches the viewport edge, releasing at the end of its container.
terms.useWhen: a side column that follows you down a long article

terms.name: Stories

terms.useWhen: the timed full-screen cards you tap through

terms.name: Streak
terms.definition: A count of consecutive periods in which the reader did the thing, displayed prominently and lost if a period is missed.
terms.useWhen: the running count of consecutive days you kept going

terms.name: Streaming announcement
terms.definition: How a screen reader is told about text that arrives token by token, holding the region quiet while it streams and speaking once when the answer is complete.

sources.title: Harvard User Research Center: Review of generative AI chatbots accessibility

terms.useWhen: a reply types itself in and floods the announcer

terms.name: Strikethrough
terms.definition: A rule drawn through the middle of text to mark it as removed, superseded, or no longer the current price.
terms.useWhen: showing text that no longer applies

terms.name: Structured format

terms.useWhen: one value split across several little boxes

terms.name: Styled alt text
terms.definition: Alt text given size, colour and weight so a mail whose images are blocked still reads as something designed instead of as a column of grey stubs.

sources.title: Litmus: the ultimate guide to styled ALT text in email
Litmus: the ultimate guide to email image blocking

terms.useWhen: alt text styled to hold a blocked image's place

terms.name: Stylistic set
terms.definition: A numbered bundle of alternate glyphs inside a font, switched on as a group to change the look of certain letters.

sources.title: Syntax for OpenType features in CSS (Adobe Fonts)
A Practical Guide to Alternate Characters (Pangram Pangram)

terms.useWhen: switching a font's single-storey a on

terms.useWhen: card internals that must align across sibling cards

terms.name: Subject line

sources.title: Litmus: The Anatomy of a Good Email
Litmus: 18 subject line tips from experts

terms.useWhen: the line a mail is opened or ignored on

terms.name: Submenu

terms.useWhen: a menu that opens out of another menu

terms.name: Subtractive colour
terms.definition: Colour made by taking light away, where inks stack towards black and every added layer can only darken, which is why a screen blue cannot be printed.
terms.useWhen: colour mixed by removing light, as ink does

terms.name: Superfamily
terms.definition: A type system whose serif, sans, and sometimes mono members share one skeleton, so they pair by construction rather than by taste.
terms.useWhen: picking two typefaces that are guaranteed to agree

terms.name: Superscript
terms.definition: Small raised characters used for footnote markers, ordinals, and exponents, ideally drawn by the font rather than shrunk by software.

terms.name: Supporting pane

terms.useWhen: helper content that cannot stand on its own

terms.name: Surface color
terms.definition: The colour of a plane that content sits on, defined as a set of stacked levels so a card on a page and a sheet on a card are told apart by value.
terms.useWhen: naming the plane content sits on, not the page background

terms.name: Surface tint
terms.definition: A wash of the primary colour blended into a surface in proportion to its elevation, so height reads as a colour shift rather than only as a shadow.

terms.name: Swash
terms.definition: A letter drawn with an ornamental flourish, usually an extended entry or exit stroke on an italic capital.
terms.useWhen: naming the decorative tail on a fancy capital

terms.name: Swatch
terms.definition: A small block of flat colour shown as a sample, used in pickers and documentation to stand in for a value the reader cannot otherwise see.

terms.useWhen: a small block standing in for a colour value

terms.useWhen: actions parked behind a row until it is swiped

terms.name: Swipe deck

terms.useWhen: a stack of cards you swipe left or right to judge

terms.name: Swipe to dismiss
terms.definition: Flinging an item off the edge of the screen to remove it, with the item tracking the finger and snapping back if the throw is too short.

sources.title: NN/g: Using Swipe to Trigger Contextual Actions

terms.useWhen: throwing a card or notification off the screen to clear it

terms.name: Swiss style
terms.definition: The Swiss modernist system of a strict grid, flush left sans serif type, asymmetric layout, and objective photography, still the base of clean UI layout.
terms.useWhen: grid, Helvetica, and nothing decorative

terms.name: Switch
terms.definition: A control shaped like a sliding track that turns one setting on or off and applies the change the moment it is flipped, with no separate save step.

sources.title: ARIA Authoring Practices Guide: Switch pattern

terms.useWhen: a setting that takes effect immediately

terms.name: Switch access
terms.definition: Operating a device with one or two switches, where a scanning cursor steps through targets in turn and a press selects the highlighted one.

sources.title: Android Accessibility Help: Get started with Switch Access

terms.useWhen: input is a single button and time, not a pointer

terms.name: Switcher
terms.definition: A layout primitive that flips between a row and a column at a threshold it works out from its own width, with no media query involved.
terms.useWhen: side by side until it does not fit, then stacked

terms.name: Symbol support
terms.definition: Marking a control with a concept code so a reader who uses an augmentative symbol set sees their own familiar picture in place of your icon and wording.
terms.useWhen: the words and icons themselves are the barrier

terms.name: Syntax highlighting
terms.definition: Colouring code by what each token is, keyword or string or comment or name, so the structure and the typo are visible before a line has actually been read.
terms.useWhen: colour that follows the code's own token classes

terms.name: Synthwave
terms.definition: A neon 1980s look built on sunset gradients, glowing perspective grids, and chrome type, close to vaporwave but sincere rather than ironic.

sources.title: Digital Heroes: Vaporwave Retro Brand Design 2026

terms.useWhen: neon grid and sunset 80s futurism, played straight

terms.name: System color keyword
terms.definition: A CSS keyword such as Canvas, CanvasText or LinkText that resolves to a colour chosen by the operating system rather than by the page.

sources.title: Windows High Contrast Mode and CSS custom properties

terms.useWhen: styling with the colours the OS itself picked

terms.name: System font
terms.definition: The typeface the operating system uses for its own interface, requested by keyword so each platform supplies its native face.
terms.useWhen: you want the app to look native and load nothing

terms.name: Tab stop
terms.definition: One position in the tab sequence: a place the Tab key can reach, counted once even when the widget it belongs to holds many focusable parts.

sources.title: ARIA APG: Developing a Keyboard Interface
Erik Kroes: A glossary of web accessibility terms

terms.useWhen: counting how many Tab presses a widget costs

terms.name: Tabbable
terms.definition: Reachable by the Tab key, as opposed to merely focusable: an element with tabindex of -1 can take focus from script but never from Tab.

sources.title: Eric Eggert: Two different kinds of focusable UI elements

terms.useWhen: distinguishing script focus from Tab reachability

terms.name: Table-based layout
terms.definition: Laying a page out in nested tables because the renderer has no box model worth trusting, which is how mail is still built and how the web was built before CSS.

sources.title: Litmus: understanding responsive and hybrid email design

terms.useWhen: layout built from nested tables, not CSS boxes

terms.name: Header association
terms.definition: The markup that ties a data cell to its row and column headers, so a cell read on its own still says what it is.
terms.useWhen: a table cell must announce which column it is in

terms.name: Table of contents
terms.definition: A list of a document's sections, linked in reading order, shown beside or above the text.
terms.useWhen: the document's own sections, in reading order

terms.name: Tabs
terms.definition: A set of labelled panels in one region, where selecting a label swaps the panel beneath it.
terms.useWhen: labelled panels in one region, one showing at a time

terms.name: Tabular figures
terms.definition: Numerals drawn to identical widths so digits stack into columns, and so a changing number does not shift the text around it.

sources.title: Facts about figures: numeric styles with OpenType features

terms.useWhen: numbers in a table, a timer, or a live counter

terms.name: Tag
terms.definition: A small label attached to an item to classify it, often coloured by category and sometimes removable.
terms.useWhen: a small label that classifies an item

terms.name: Tag input
terms.definition: A field that turns each entry into a removable tag sitting inside the field, with the caret waiting after the last one.
terms.useWhen: a reader types an open ended set of short values

terms.name: Tap
terms.definition: A single press and lift of one finger on a touch surface, the touch equivalent of a click, used to activate a control or select an item.
terms.useWhen: the touch gesture that activates something

terms.name: Tap delay
terms.definition: The pause a touch browser once held before dispatching a click, kept open in case a second tap arrived and turned the gesture into a zoom.

sources.title: Chrome for Developers: 300ms tap delay, gone away

terms.useWhen: naming the historic lag between tap and response

terms.name: Target spacing
terms.definition: The exception that lets an undersized control pass when no other target falls inside a 24 pixel circle centred on it, trading size for clearance.
terms.useWhen: small controls that cannot grow but can be separated

terms.name: Tearsheet
terms.definition: A tall modal anchored to the bottom of the viewport that holds a multi step creation flow, stackable when one flow opens another.
terms.useWhen: a full height modal for a creation flow

terms.name: 10-foot UI
terms.definition: The register for screens read from a couch: focus-driven navigation with a remote, oversized type and cards, horizontal rails, and safe margins for TV overscan.
terms.useWhen: the screen is across the room and the input is a remote

terms.name: Terminal aesthetic
terms.definition: A look borrowed from the command line: monospace type on a fixed character grid, a block cursor, and green or amber text on black.

sources.title: Setproduct: Retro and brutalist UI design, a 2026 field guide

terms.useWhen: the UI dressed as a command line

terms.name: Terrazzo
terms.definition: A background pattern of small irregular chips scattered on a plain field, copied from poured stone flooring and used flat and multicolored behind interface content.

sources.title: Creative Market: Design Trend Report, Terrazzo

terms.useWhen: a speckled chip pattern used as a background fill

terms.name: Text balancing
terms.definition: Choosing line breaks so a short block of text has lines of roughly equal length instead of a long first line and a stub second one.

sources.title: When to use text-wrap: balance vs pretty (LogRocket)

terms.useWhen: a two line heading breaks badly

terms.name: Text box trim
terms.definition: Cutting the leftover space above and below a line of text so the box hugs the cap height and baseline instead of the font's full ascent and descent.
terms.useWhen: you want a label's box to match the letters, not the font

terms.name: Text columns
terms.definition: Flowing one block of running text into several columns that fill and balance automatically, with an optional rule drawn between them.
terms.useWhen: one passage of text split into columns

terms.name: Text field
terms.definition: A single line box for typed input, carrying a label, an optional hint, and the error message shown when what was typed does not pass.
terms.useWhen: one line of free text or a number

terms.name: Text spacing
terms.definition: The requirement that a reader can increase line height, letter spacing, word spacing, and paragraph spacing without any content being lost or clipped.
terms.useWhen: proving a layout survives reader-set spacing

terms.name: Text area
terms.definition: A multi-line text box, usually resizable, for input that will not fit on one line: a comment, a description, an address, a note.
terms.useWhen: input that runs to several lines

terms.name: The fold
terms.definition: The bottom edge of the first screenful, above which content is seen without any scrolling and below which it must be earned.
terms.useWhen: arguing about what must be visible before a scroll

terms.name: Three-way merge
terms.definition: Three versions on screen at once, mine, theirs, and the ancestor they both came from, with the result edited underneath so a conflict is decided rather than guessed.
terms.useWhen: resolving a conflict against the common ancestor

terms.name: Throttle
terms.definition: Capping how often a continuous stream of input is acted on, so a response fires at a steady rate instead of on every event.
terms.useWhen: limiting how often a continuous input is answered

terms.name: Thumb zone
terms.definition: The arc of a phone screen a thumb reaches comfortably in a one handed grip, with harder to reach bands above and across from it.

sources.title: The Thumb Zone: Designing For Mobile Users

terms.useWhen: placing primary actions within easy reach on phones

terms.name: Thumbnail
terms.definition: A small stand-in image for a larger one, cropped rather than letterboxed so a row of them lines up.
terms.useWhen: a small preview image of a bigger one

terms.name: Tick marks
terms.definition: The small notches printed along a slider track that show the discrete stops the handle can land on.
terms.useWhen: naming the notches printed along a slider

terms.name: 3D tilt
terms.definition: Rotating a card in perspective toward the pointer so it appears to tip in three dimensions, often with a moving highlight to sell the depth.
terms.useWhen: a card should read as a physical object under the pointer

terms.name: Time picker
terms.definition: A control for choosing a time of day, either as a dial you tap around or as hour and minute lists.
terms.useWhen: choosing a clock time

terms.name: Time zone display
terms.definition: Whose clock a time is shown on, the reader's or the event's, and saying which, because a time with no zone beside it is a meeting somebody is going to miss.

sources.title: Google Calendar Help: view your day, week, or month

terms.useWhen: whose clock a time is displayed on

terms.name: Timeline
terms.definition: A vertical or horizontal line of dated events, each pinned to the line by a marker and reading in order.
terms.useWhen: events in order along a line

terms.name: Timeout warning
terms.definition: A warning before a session or form expires with a simple way to extend it, so a slower reader does not lose their work silently.
terms.useWhen: a session is about to expire under the reader

terms.name: Tint
terms.definition: A colour with white mixed in, lighter than the original hue and used for faint fills, hover washes and subtle backgrounds.
terms.useWhen: a lighter version of a colour made by adding white

terms.name: Tinted neutral
terms.definition: A grey with a trace of the brand hue mixed in, so backgrounds and borders belong to the palette instead of reading as a separate, colder system.
terms.useWhen: greys that quietly carry the brand hue

terms.name: Tiny tweaks
terms.definition: The lightest responsive pattern: a single column design that only adjusts type size, image size and margins as the screen changes.
terms.useWhen: one column that only nudges type and margins

terms.name: Title bar
terms.definition: The strip along the top of a window carrying its title and window controls, and the region you drag to move the window.
terms.useWhen: the draggable strip at the top of a window

terms.name: Title case
terms.definition: Capitalising the first letter of each significant word in a heading or label, leaving short articles, conjunctions and prepositions lowercase.
terms.useWhen: Apple-style headings, buttons, and menu labels

terms.name: Tittle
terms.definition: The dot above a lowercase i or j.
terms.useWhen: you need the word for the dot on an i

terms.name: Toast
terms.definition: A brief, self-dismissing message that appears at a screen edge to confirm an action or report status without interrupting the user's flow.

sources.title: ARIA Authoring Practices Guide: Alert pattern

terms.useWhen: a passing confirmation that cleans up after itself

terms.name: Tofu
terms.definition: The empty rectangle a font renders when it has no glyph for a character, named for the block of bean curd it resembles.
terms.useWhen: naming the empty box where a character should be

terms.name: Toggle button
terms.definition: A button that stays pressed, reporting an on or off state through aria-pressed rather than firing and returning.
terms.useWhen: a button that stays down once you press it

terms.name: Toggle group
terms.definition: A set of toggle buttons treated as one control, either single select like radios or multi select like a row of formatting toggles.
terms.useWhen: several toggles that belong to one decision

terms.name: Toggletip
terms.definition: A tip revealed by clicking rather than hovering, so it works by touch and may contain links or controls a tooltip could not.
terms.useWhen: a hint you click open, not hover open

terms.name: Toolbar
terms.definition: A grouped row of controls acting on the current view, sharing one tab stop and moving focus between its items with arrow keys.

sources.title: ARIA Authoring Practices Guide: Toolbar pattern

terms.useWhen: a row of controls acting on what is on screen

terms.name: Tooltip
terms.definition: A brief text label shown on hover or keyboard focus that names or explains the element it points at, and carries nothing you can interact with.

sources.title: ARIA Authoring Practices Guide: Tooltip pattern

terms.useWhen: a label that names the control under the pointer

terms.name: Top layer
terms.definition: The layer above everything else in a document where fullscreen elements, modal dialogs and popovers render, escaping every ancestor's clipping and stacking order.
terms.useWhen: explaining why a dialog is not trapped by overflow

terms.name: Top shelf
terms.definition: The band across the top of a television home screen that the focused app fills with its own content, so an app advertises itself before anyone opens it.
terms.useWhen: the focused app fills a band on the TV home screen

terms.name: Touch target
terms.definition: The area of a control that answers a press, padded out around whatever is drawn so a fingertip can hit it without catching its neighbours.

sources.title: Smashing Magazine: accessible tap target sizes

terms.useWhen: sizing what the finger must hit, not what is drawn

terms.name: Touch target size
terms.definition: The minimum area a control must offer a finger or imprecise pointer, measured on the activation region rather than the painted glyph.
terms.useWhen: sizing something for a fingertip, not a cursor

terms.name: Trace viewer
terms.definition: The view that lays a request's spans on one time axis, each nested under the span that called it, so the bar that is too long or starts too late is the finding.
terms.useWhen: reading where one request spent its time, span by span

terms.name: Track
terms.definition: The groove a slider thumb or scrollbar travels along, usually drawn as filled before the handle and empty after it.
terms.useWhen: naming the groove a handle slides in

terms.name: Tracking
terms.definition: The uniform space added to or removed from every letter across a run of text.
terms.useWhen: space added to every letter across a run

terms.name: Transactional email
terms.definition: Mail sent because one person did one thing, a receipt or a reset, which is why it may carry no marketing and why its design is a record rather than a pitch.
terms.useWhen: mail triggered by one action, not a campaign

terms.name: Transcript
terms.definition: A full text version of time based media, readable without playing it and searchable by both people and machines.

sources.title: WebAIM: Captions, Transcripts, and Audio Descriptions

terms.useWhen: offering the whole of a video or podcast as text

terms.name: Transfer list
terms.definition: Two side by side lists with arrow buttons between them, used to move items from available to chosen and back.
terms.useWhen: picking a subset by moving items between two lists

terms.name: Transparency checkerboard
terms.definition: The light grey and white checker grid a design tool paints behind transparent regions, a convention so universal that the pattern itself now reads as meaning alpha.
terms.useWhen: showing that a region is transparent rather than white

terms.name: Tree select
terms.definition: A select whose popup is a tree, so options can be chosen at any depth with parents collapsing over their children.
terms.useWhen: picking from a tree inside a field

terms.name: Tree grid
terms.definition: A table whose rows nest and expand like a tree, so hierarchy and columns of data coexist in one grid.
terms.useWhen: a table whose rows contain child rows

terms.name: Tree view
terms.definition: A nested list where branches expand and collapse in place, navigated with arrow keys as a single tab stop.

sources.title: ARIA Authoring Practices Guide: Tree View pattern

terms.useWhen: nested items that expand in place

terms.name: Triadic color scheme
terms.definition: A palette of three hues spaced evenly around the colour wheel, vivid by construction and usually applied with one hue dominant.
terms.useWhen: three hues balanced evenly around the wheel

terms.name: Trick wording
terms.definition: Phrasing a choice so its plain reading is the opposite of its effect, typically through double negatives or a label that describes the wrong outcome.
terms.useWhen: untick this box to not stop receiving emails

terms.name: True black theme
terms.definition: A dark palette whose background is pure black rather than near black, which switches OLED pixels off entirely but makes elements look like they float in a void.
terms.useWhen: a dark theme at pure black for OLED, not near black

terms.name: Truncated axis
terms.definition: Starting a value axis above zero so differences look bigger than they are; honest for lines and dots, a lie for bars.

sources.title: Fundamentals of Data Visualization: Proportional ink

terms.useWhen: judging whether cutting the y-axis exaggerates or clarifies

terms.name: Truncation
terms.definition: Cutting text that does not fit and marking the cut, usually with an ellipsis, so the reader knows something was removed.
terms.useWhen: text has to fit a box it does not fit

terms.name: Tween
terms.definition: A single animation from one value to another over a duration, named for the in-between frames a computer fills in.

sources.title: School of Motion: motion design dictionary

terms.useWhen: naming one animation as a unit you can play or reverse

terms.name: 12 column grid
terms.definition: The web's default column count, chosen because twelve divides cleanly into halves, thirds, quarters and sixths.
terms.useWhen: why almost every layout grid has twelve columns

terms.name: Type scale
terms.definition: The fixed set of text sizes a design allows, chosen so sizes relate to each other rather than being picked one at a time.
terms.useWhen: deciding what sizes are allowed to exist at all

terms.name: Type specimen
terms.definition: A display of a typeface's characters, sizes, and styles made to show what the face can do rather than to communicate the text itself.
terms.useWhen: showing off a typeface rather than using it

terms.name: Type to confirm
terms.definition: Guarding a destructive action by making the reader type the name of the thing being destroyed before the confirm button becomes usable.
terms.useWhen: you must type the repo name to delete it

terms.name: Typeahead
terms.definition: Offering suggestions that update on every keystroke, drawn from a live query, so the reader picks a result rather than finishing the phrase.
terms.useWhen: suggestions appear and change as you type

terms.name: Typeface
terms.definition: The designed set of letterforms itself, as distinct from a font, which is one particular file or instance you actually use.

sources.title: Family, type family, or font family (Google Fonts Knowledge)

terms.useWhen: distinguishing the design from the file

terms.name: Typewriter effect
terms.definition: Revealing text one character at a time, as if it were being typed, usually with a blinking caret trailing the last letter.

sources.title: School of Motion: motion design dictionary

terms.useWhen: text should arrive as if being written right now

terms.name: Typing indicator
terms.definition: The three bouncing dots shown while someone is composing a reply, or while an assistant is preparing one.
terms.useWhen: showing that a reply is being composed

terms.name: Typographic color
terms.definition: The overall lightness or darkness a block of text produces when you stop reading it and look at it as a grey texture.
terms.useWhen: judging a paragraph as texture rather than words

terms.name: Typographic hierarchy
terms.definition: The ordering of text by visual weight so a reader can tell at a glance what is a title, what is body, and what is a caption.

implementations.name: Type roles: display, headline, title, body, label

terms.useWhen: making importance readable without reading

terms.name: Typography token
terms.definition: A named bundle of type values (family, size, weight, line height, tracking) that a design system hands out instead of raw numbers.
terms.useWhen: naming a text style so it can be reused and themed

terms.name: Underline
terms.definition: A rule drawn under text, on the web the default marker for a link, ideally set to skip the descenders it would otherwise cross.
terms.useWhen: marking a link without relying on color alone

terms.name: Undo
terms.definition: Letting an action run immediately and offering to reverse it afterwards, instead of stopping to ask whether the reader really meant it.

sources.title: GoodUI: try undos instead of prompting for confirmation

terms.useWhen: the action happens first and offers a way back

terms.name: Universal navigation
terms.definition: A slim bar that links a subsite back to its parent organisation's other sites, sitting above the subsite's own global navigation.

sources.title: Universal Navigation: Connecting Subsites to Main Sites, NN/g

terms.useWhen: connecting a subsite back to the parent org

terms.name: Unsaved changes guard
terms.definition: Warning the reader that edits will be lost before a navigation or close is allowed to proceed, and offering to save or discard first.
terms.useWhen: leaving a form asks whether to discard your edits

terms.name: Unsubscribe link
terms.definition: The way out of a mailing list, which the law and the mail clients now both insist is one click, and whose difficulty is the honest measure of a sender.
terms.useWhen: the way out of a list, and how hard it is

terms.name: Use of color
terms.definition: The rule that colour must never be the only carrier of meaning, so a red field also needs an icon, wording, or shape change.

implementations.name: Use of color and color blindness

terms.useWhen: the only difference between two states is hue

terms.name: Utility bar
terms.definition: A persistent bar docked to the bottom of an application holding small tools that open into panels without leaving the current page.
terms.useWhen: tools docked along the bottom of the app

terms.name: Utility navigation
terms.definition: The strip of secondary tools and account actions, sign in, search, language, cart, kept apart from the links that describe the site's content.

sources.title: Utility Navigation: What It Is and How to Design It, NN/g

terms.useWhen: the small links above or beside the main nav

terms.name: Vaporwave
terms.definition: A retro internet look of magenta and cyan gradients, grid horizons, Japanese type, statuary, and 90s desktop chrome used ironically.

sources.title: Shutterstock: What Is the Vaporwave Aesthetic

terms.useWhen: 90s mall and desktop imagery reused with irony

terms.name: Variable font
terms.definition: One font file that contains a continuous design space, so any weight, width, or other axis value between the extremes can be requested.
terms.useWhen: you need many weights without many files

terms.name: Variation axis
terms.definition: One dimension a variable font can move along, named by a four-letter tag: lowercase for the five registered axes, uppercase for custom ones.
terms.useWhen: naming a single dial inside a variable font

terms.name: Velocity skew
terms.definition: Skewing or stretching content in proportion to how fast the page is scrolling and easing it back to square when the scroll stops, so speed shows up in the shape of the content.

sources.title: GSAP forums: skew on scroll velocity

terms.useWhen: scroll speed itself should be visible

terms.name: Verbosity
terms.definition: How much a screen reader says about each thing it reaches, a user setting that decides whether your carefully written description is heard at all.
terms.useWhen: arguing about how much detail a label should carry

terms.name: Vernacular web
terms.definition: The amateur homepage look of the GeoCities era: tiled backgrounds, sparkle GIFs, under construction signs, midi music, and hit counters.
terms.useWhen: the hand-made amateur homepage look

terms.name: Vertical rhythm
terms.definition: Spacing every block of text by multiples of one line height so the page keeps an even beat from top to bottom.

sources.title: What the Font are Vertical Rhythm and Modular Scale?

terms.useWhen: spacing paragraphs and headings by one consistent unit

terms.name: Vertical writing mode
terms.definition: Setting lines to run top to bottom in columns rather than left to right, as traditional Chinese, Japanese, and Korean typography does.
terms.useWhen: typesetting CJK text in columns

terms.name: VHS aesthetic
terms.definition: A look that imitates a worn videotape: tracking bands, smeared color bleeding past edges, interlace comb artifacts, and burned-in timecode or REC overlays.
terms.useWhen: artifacts of magnetic tape used as decoration

terms.name: Vibrancy
terms.definition: Apple's treatment where foreground colour is derived from the blurred content behind a material, so labels on a translucent panel shift with whatever they sit over.
terms.useWhen: foreground colour that reacts to the blur behind it

terms.name: Video player
terms.definition: A framed video with the controls needed to play, seek, mute and caption it, sized so the controls never crowd the picture.
terms.useWhen: video is the content and the reader controls playback

terms.name: View progress timeline
terms.definition: A scroll timeline measured by one element's passage through the scrollport, with named ranges for entering, being contained, covering, and exiting.
terms.useWhen: the animation should track one element, not the whole page

terms.name: View transition
terms.definition: An animated change between two states of a page, where the browser photographs before and after and interpolates the elements the two have in common.
terms.useWhen: one state of a page morphing into the next

terms.name: Viewport
terms.definition: The visible rectangle of a page inside the browser window, excluding the browser's own bars, and the unit basis for vh and vw.
terms.useWhen: the visible window, not the whole document

terms.name: Vignette
terms.definition: A gradual darkening toward the edges of an image that pulls the eye to the centre, borrowed from lens falloff and applied deliberately for focus and mood.
terms.useWhen: the edges of an image quietly dimmed to hold focus

terms.name: Virtual keyboard
terms.definition: The on screen keyboard a device raises for a field, whose key set the field itself chooses by declaring what kind of value it wants.
terms.useWhen: the field type decides which keys a reader is given

terms.name: Visual balance
terms.definition: The distribution of visual weight across a composition, reached by mirroring elements, by setting one large element against several small ones, or by radiating from a centre.

sources.title: Design Principles: Compositional, Symmetrical And Asymmetrical Balance

terms.useWhen: saying why a layout feels tippy or settled

terms.name: Visual hierarchy
terms.definition: The ordering of elements by visual weight, size, contrast, position and spacing, so a reader learns what matters most without being told.
terms.useWhen: deciding what a reader should notice first

terms.name: Visually hidden
terms.definition: Content removed from the visual layout but left in the accessibility tree, so screen readers announce what the design leaves unsaid.

sources.title: The A11Y Project: How to hide content
WebAIM: CSS in action, invisible content

terms.useWhen: text for screen readers that never shows on screen

terms.name: Voice control
terms.definition: Operating an interface by speaking control names or numbered overlays, which makes the visible wording of a control its address.

sources.title: Use Voice Control commands on Mac, Apple Support
Get started with Voice Access, Android Accessibility Help

terms.useWhen: the reader clicks by saying the button's name

terms.name: Watermark
terms.definition: Repeating faint text or a mark tiled across content to claim it or to mark it as a draft or a preview.
terms.useWhen: faint repeated text laid over content

terms.name: Waveform
terms.definition: An audio track drawn as a row of amplitude bars, used both to show what is in the file and as the surface you scrub along.
terms.useWhen: audio drawn as bars you can scrub

terms.name: Web font
terms.definition: A font file downloaded by the page rather than taken from the reader's device, declared in CSS and delivered like any other asset.
terms.useWhen: type the page ships rather than borrows

terms.name: Welcome mat
terms.definition: A full width introduction shown on first entry to a feature, listing what is new or what to set up, with a way to skip it for good.
terms.useWhen: a first run introduction to a whole feature

terms.name: Wheel picker
terms.definition: A spinning drum of values that snaps to the item under a fixed selection line, the iOS way of choosing from a short list.
terms.useWhen: the iOS drum you spin to pick a value

terms.name: Whitespace
terms.definition: The empty area between and around elements, treated as an active design material rather than as leftover space.
terms.useWhen: the empty space doing the grouping work

terms.name: Wide gamut
terms.definition: Colour beyond what sRGB can express, addressed in CSS through spaces such as display-p3 and rec2020 and shown only on displays that reach that far.

sources.title: Wide Gamut Color in CSS with Display-P3

terms.useWhen: reaching for colours sRGB cannot express

terms.name: Widget
terms.definition: A small, glanceable view of an app placed on a system surface such as a home screen or desktop, sized in fixed slots rather than freely.
terms.useWhen: app content is useful without opening the app

terms.name: Widow
terms.definition: A short last line of a paragraph, often a single word, stranded at the top of the next column or page.

sources.title: An end to typographic widows on the web (Clagnut)

terms.useWhen: naming a stranded last line at the top of a column

terms.name: Window controls
terms.definition: The cluster of close, minimise and zoom controls in a window's title bar, three coloured dots on macOS and three glyphs on Windows.
terms.useWhen: the close, minimise and maximise cluster

terms.name: Window size class
terms.definition: A named bucket for how much width an app window has, such as compact, medium and expanded, used in place of raw device categories.
terms.useWhen: reasoning about window width, not device type

terms.name: Windows Aero
terms.definition: The Windows Vista and 7 look built on translucent glass window frames, soft outer glows, reflections, and animated window transitions.
terms.useWhen: see-through window chrome from the Vista and 7 era

terms.name: Wipe
terms.definition: A transition where a moving edge or mask travels across the frame, replacing what was there with what comes next.

sources.title: School of Motion: motion design dictionary

terms.useWhen: a reveal should have a visible leading edge

terms.name: Wireframe
terms.definition: A screen drawn as structure only: blocks where the content goes, a crossed box for an image, ruled lines for text, with no colour or type decided yet.

sources.title: NN/g: UX Prototypes, Low Fidelity vs. High Fidelity
NN/g: Prototypes vs Wireframes in UX Projects

terms.useWhen: settling what goes where before deciding how any of it looks

terms.name: Wizard
terms.definition: A flow broken into ordered steps with back and next controls, where each step validates before the next one is allowed.
terms.useWhen: a long task split into ordered steps

terms.name: Word break
terms.definition: Whether a long unbroken string is allowed to split mid-word rather than overflow its container, and where that split may happen.
terms.useWhen: a long URL or token is bursting out of its box

terms.name: Word spacing
terms.definition: The width of the gaps between words, which justification stretches and which, set too wide, opens rivers down a paragraph.
terms.useWhen: the gaps between words, not between letters

terms.name: X-height
terms.definition: The height of a lowercase x in a typeface, measured from the baseline, which is what makes two fonts at the same point size look different sizes.
terms.useWhen: explaining why two fonts at the same size look different

terms.name: Y2K aesthetic
terms.definition: The turn of the millennium look of chrome type, bubble shapes, translucent plastic, and lens flares, revived as a web and app style.
terms.useWhen: chrome, bubbles, and translucent plastic futurism

terms.name: Yellow fade technique
terms.definition: Washing a just-changed element in colour and letting it fade back out, so a change made without a page reload is still noticed where it happened.

sources.title: Signal vs. Noise: Web Interface Design Tip: The Yellow Fade Technique

terms.useWhen: showing which thing on the page just changed

terms.name: Yo-yo loop
terms.definition: A repeating animation that plays forward then backward instead of jumping back to the start, so a loop has no visible seam.
terms.useWhen: a loop must repeat without a snap back to frame one

terms.name: Z pattern
terms.definition: The scanning shape on sparse pages: across the top, diagonally down to the lower left, then across the bottom to the final call to action.
terms.useWhen: laying out a sparse page with one clear action

terms.name: Zebra striping
terms.definition: Alternating row backgrounds in a table so the eye can track a single row across many columns.
terms.useWhen: shading every other row of a table

terms.name: Zero state
terms.definition: The first-run screen a feature shows before any data exists, written to teach the feature rather than to report emptiness.

sources.title: Empty states in application design, NN/g

terms.useWhen: the teaching screen shown before any data exists

terms.name: Zero UI
terms.definition: A paradigm where the screen stops being the interface and the interaction happens through voice, gesture, presence, or sensors, so the system responds without anything to look at.

sources.title: Designer Daily: The invisible interface, an introduction to designing for Zero UI
Microsoft Advertising: Zero UI, the invisible interface revolution
UX Planet: Zero UI, how to design invisible interfaces

terms.useWhen: the interaction has no screen to design

terms.name: Zero-width space
terms.definition: An invisible character that takes no width and adds a legal break point, letting a long string wrap without showing a hyphen.
terms.useWhen: breaking a long identifier with no visible mark

terms.name: Zigzag layout
terms.definition: Alternating rows that flip which side the image and the text sit on, so the eye zigzags down a list of features.
terms.useWhen: a run of feature blocks that would otherwise read as a list

terms.name: Zoom transition
terms.definition: A presentation that scales a tapped element up into the full view it opens, so the destination appears to come from the thing that was touched.
terms.useWhen: the destination should visibly come from what was tapped
